datasheet.title: Schneider Electric APC NetShelter Metered Rack PDU AP7821B product datasheet (5 Nov 2026 copy)

devices.description: APC by Schneider Electric NetShelter metered rack PDU, 1U horizontal: a 444 mm black metal box, 102 mm deep. It hands a 200 to 230 V feed (a C20 inlet; 16 A rated, 3300 VA) on to eight IEC C13 outlets in one row. It has no breaker and no switching. The outlet face has the inlet at the left end. At the right end it has a two-digit display, a round button, two jacks and three small lamps. The other face is plain, with a logo and a ground mark. A cord retention bracket and rack mounting brackets are supplied.

gaps.note: the datasheet says "Mounting location Front Rear" and names no face as the front. The face with the outlets is drawn as `rear` and the plain face as `front`, the usual way a horizontal PDU is racked; no held document says so.
gaps.wanted: the installation guide's mounting figure.

gaps.note: every position on the outlet face is borrowed from a reading of the AP7921B's photograph and is an estimate good to a few millimetres; none is measured on this model.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing or a straight-on photograph of this model with a scale.

gaps.note: the datasheet sells the unit as metered and says nothing of what is metered or where; the display is one window, so the input is the scope drawn.
gaps.wanted: the user manual's description of the metering.

gaps.note: small lamps stand over the display and beside the jacks, some lit green or amber in the photographs; their count, colours and meanings were not read off the pixels and no document names them, so three are drawn unlit and uncoloured.
gaps.wanted: the user manual's description of the status lamps.

gaps.note: the labels under the two jacks are not legible and no datasheet names a port.
gaps.wanted: the user manual, or a close photograph of the jacks.

gaps.note: no document held names the two rear jacks or prints a speed for them, so none is stated.
gaps.wanted: the user manual's port specification.

gaps.note: the datasheet lists rack mounting brackets and a cord retention bracket and gives no figure; no photograph shows them.
gaps.wanted: the installation guide's mounting figures.

gaps.note: no held document shows the top, the bottom or an end.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of the top, the bottom and an end.

datasheet.title: Performance, Vertical Cable Manager for 2 & 4 Post Racks, 84"H x 6"W, Single-Sided with Door (AR8615), product data sheet

devices.description: Single-sided vertical cable manager, 6 in wide, APC Performance AR8615 for 2 and 4 post open frame racks: a steel back plate 2134 mm tall with a column of 44 smooth plastic fingers down each side of one cable channel, a finger to each rack unit, and a full-length door with two quarter-turn latches that ships fitted. It stands beside the rack on three hex bolts through the upright and takes no rack unit.

gaps.note: the door "opens to left or right" on hinge pins and lifts off; the instruction sheet shows a quarter-turn latch and the door swinging off the finger tips either way, but no view dimensions a hinge. The door is drawn as one fitted plate that is either on or off.
gaps.wanted: a drawing or a close render of the door's hinge pins and latch

gaps.note: the data sheet advertises "multiple internal cable tie-off locations". The instruction sheet draws the slots and punches in the back plate that they are, but dimensions none, and the format has no place to state a tie point on a duct (#1009 states them only on the FS tray). They are not drawn or stated.
gaps.wanted: the back plate's slots dimensioned, and a place in the format for a duct's tie points

gaps.note: the instruction sheet shows an optional grounding and bonding point, a tab with a hole bent up at the foot of the back plate, "Hardware and cable not provided". No thread or hole size is stated, and a grounding point in the format is a stud or screw with a thread, so none is stated.
gaps.wanted: the size of the hole and the screw it takes

gaps.note: APC states "high capacity" and no figure on the data sheet, the instruction sheet or the brochure, so none is recorded and none is estimated.
gaps.wanted: a capacity figure and the cable it is stated for

gaps.note: the instruction sheet's isometric figure draws each finger as a smooth tongue with a rolled root. It is built as an arm 12 across and a hooked tip 22 across, 31 high, 296 long; the size, the length and the count (44, counted at constant pitch) are read off a figure that is not dimensioned.
gaps.wanted: a section through a finger and the back plate

gaps.note: where the first finger stands against the rack's units is not stated: the fingers are centred on the 2134 mm height, and which hole of the upright each bolt takes is not dimensioned, so whether they sit on the rack's units is not known.
gaps.wanted: the heights of the three bolt holes against the rack's first unit

gaps.note: the single-sided part has a back plate that takes the AR8652 spacer bracket (a PDU bracket) and the accessory brackets, sold separately; the instruction sheet draws them but they are other parts and are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: the accessory parts, if they are modelled

gaps.note: the door has an oval opening near its top in the instruction sheet's figure; it is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: its size and place

gaps.note: how far the manager stands from the upright when it is bolted on is not dimensioned; the part is drawn alone.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the manager fitted to an upright

datasheet.title: Amphenol Network Solutions 300CB08/nrg300CB08 8/8 Position Circuit Breaker Panel data sheet, 07.11.24 v.20

devices.description: 1RU dual-feed DC circuit breaker panel. Two electrically isolated sides, A and B, each fed at up to 325 A and each distributing to eight plug-in breaker positions of up to 60 A. This is the plain 300CB08: vertical dual-stud inputs and screw terminal-block outputs at the rear, a passive alarm card, and no circuit monitoring. Universal ±12, ±24 and ±48 V DC.

gaps.note: each feed is two stud terminals, one BATT and one RTN, and no drawing or sentence held says which is the outer one: the input-lug figure of the guide (Fig. 2-7) carries no legend, and its rear photograph prints BATT and RTN beside the output rows only. Each side is one part, `input-a` and `input-b`, whose two terminals are `terminal-1` and `terminal-2` by position, not by polarity.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph that resolves the input legends, or the panel itself.

gaps.note: the TPA fuse holder, part 307492, is seated from three-quarter views only: its face is placed by eye and its size is borrowed from the breaker whose position it fits. The covers-off view seats breakers only and does not touch this.
gaps.wanted: a face-on, dimensioned view of 307492.

gaps.wanted: the controller and sensor card current at 12, 24 and 48 V.

gaps.note: the face letters a RESET button and no document says what a press does; searched the guides and release notes for reset, press and factory.

datasheet.title: 7280R3A Series Data Center Switch Router - Data Sheet (04-0040-26, April 15th, 2025)

devices.description: Arista 7280DR3A-36 - a fixed 2RU data-centre router switch with 36 400G QSFP-DD ports in two stacked rows of eighteen columns (the odd number on the upper cage), numbered 1 to 36 in an orange strip between the rows, and two OSFP line-system ports (OSFP-LS, 37 and 38) for 400G-ZR optics at the upper right. Beside the line-system ports are four status lamps (system, fan, power supply 1, power supply 2), an RJ-45 console, a USB port and an RJ-45 management port; at the far right stand a Time-of-Day connector (USB-C) and two clock connectors (1PPS and 10 MHz). The rear carries four hot-swap fan modules and two hot-swap 2400 W power supplies, AC or DC, one above the other at the right, with a grounding pad between fans 1 and 2. The same front panel is sold as the DR3A-36, the DR3AM-36 (TunnelSec) and the DR3AK-36 (large routes and TunnelSec), and the DR3AK-36S (the K with secure boot enabled); they differ in software licence, encryption and secure boot, not in the metal.

gaps.wanted: A FIGURE OF THE DR3A-36 AND THE DR3AK-36 FRONT. Figure C-2 is captioned for all three models but prints the plate "7280DR3AM-36", so it is a picture of the DR3AM-36. The model plate of the other two is not shown, and this file prints "7280DR3A-36" on every configuration. A photograph of each plate closes it.

THE WHITE NUMBER TABS OVER THE CAGES. Figure C-2 draws a white square with a large numeral over the centre of each cage. A seated cage hides what is painted under it and the library has no layer above a cage for printed matter, so the numbers are modelled as the strip legends only. A drawing that says whether the tab is a sticker on the cage or part of it closes it.

A LEGEND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE FIRST STRIP. Column 1's strip reads something like "400G" between its arrows in the eight-times enlargement and no other column's does. At 1.87 px/mm the glyphs are three pixels high and resolve to a smear; the numerals and arrows beside it resolve, so the strip is readable and this text is the unresolved thing. It is not drawn.

THE SYMBOLS OVER THE SYSTEM AND FAN LAMPS, and the small legends over the console and management jacks. They are printed in blue at about two pixels' height and are not legible in the figure; PS1 and PS2 are. Guide figures A-1 and A-2 say the lamps are labelled in one of two ways and the held figure does not say which this chassis uses.
A LAMP AND A BLUE SYMBOL ABOVE THE ToD CONNECTOR (about 428.9 and 434.8 mm, 34.3 mm down). Figure C-2 draws them and no callout or table names them. They are not modelled.

WHETHER THE PPS AND 10MHZ JACKS ARE SMB OR SMA. The guide calls them "E-Sync clock connectors" and the data sheet "PPS/10M/ToD inputs"; neither names the connector. They are seated as std/smb@1 from their drawn size and their direction (input or output) is not stated either.

THE USB GENERATION. The guide says "USB port" and the data sheet "USB Ports 1"; neither gives a generation, and figure C-2 draws a gold tongue, which is neither USB-IF colour. The port is seated with the `usb2` (white) skin as the one that claims least; a data sheet line giving the generation closes it.

A BLACK ROUND HOLE at the left end, 4.8 mm from the edge and 53.4 mm down, in line with the strips. Figure C-2 draws it and nothing names it (an ESD socket is a candidate on other switches). It is drawn as a hole in decor and carries no part.

THE PRINTING AT THE REAR. The ground strip prints three symbols and the rear carries the airflow marks, but the guide's rear panel figure is 1.19 px/mm and its labels are unreadable. The supplies and fans print no numbers that resolve. A rear photograph closes it.

THE PWR-2411-DC FACE. The guide shows the PWR-1900-DC and PWR-500-DC (figure 4-5) and no PWR-2411-DC. Table 7 note 2 says its terminals are "twin #10 studs spaced for dual-hole lug with 5/8 inch hole spacing"; the supply here is the AC housing with a plain two-pole block, and the protective earth terminal "on the opposite side" is not drawn. The data sheet reads "AWG #6 Max" for the DC input connector and table 7 reads 2 to 4 AWG; the larger conductor (the guide's) is the one a lug takes.

THE KITS, AND THE EAR POSITION THAT IS NOT FLUSH. `chassis.ears` states the one position the guide names for a 2RU switch: section 3.5 says the bracket sits "either flush with the front and rear panels, or not flush with the panels", and section 3.4 gives no two-post mounting for the 2RU switches, so the position is `4-post` only. It has no `at` (the guide's mounting figures are isometric drawings of other switches, the 7050 and the 7050SX-128), no `default` (no figure shows the ears as shipped) and the "not flush" case is left out because the guide does not say which way it sits. The data sheet's ordering information lists KIT-7202 (spare tool-free accessory kit v2 for 2RU, 4-post mount, 2x C19-C20) and KIT-7004-2UL (extended tool-free 4-post kit for 2-4RU) for the DR3A-36. Guide appendix B.1 gives KIT-7202 "rack depths of twenty two to thirty two inches" (558.8 to 812.8 mm) and its parts (ASY-06132 rack ear, ASY-03765 front rail, ASY-03767 rear sliding rail, two of each), but no document dimensions any of those parts, and none gives KIT-7004-2UL a range or a parts list. A kit contract needs its parts as components with a size, so neither kit is modelled and `chassis.kits` is left out.
THE POWER DRAW OF FAN-7012H. Neither the guide nor the data sheet gives it. The supplies' own output (2400 W) is stated and is written.
The K and M variants print their own model line on the plate. This file prints one line.

datasheet.title: Casa Systems C100G Converged Cable Access Platform data sheet

devices.description: Casa C100G CMTS/CCAP - 13RU, 14 paired front/rear slots. Front and rear slot N are two halves of one logical position: a DOCSIS line card in front N requires its I/O partner in rear N.

gaps.note: The BDM2/BDM2m datasheet states "Total Power 300 W" in a technical specifications table headed "BDM2/2 m with 6+12 IO Card", whose RF connector row describes that card's six downstream and twelve upstream ports. The figure is the assembly's. A BDM position is TWO modules here - casa/bdm in a front bay and casa/io-6p12 in the paired rear bay, which is why casa/bdm already carries `pairs-with` - and no document we hold divides the 300 W between them. Writing it onto the front module would make the chassis total come out right and the answer to "what does a BDM front module draw" come out wrong, so neither half carries a figure and the chassis total stays a floor. The arithmetic does not settle it either way: 12 x 300 W lands on the C100G's stated 3.6 kW whether the 300 W is the pair or the front half with small rear cards. The C100G HIG corroborates the assembly reading and hedges it: Tables A-10 and A-11 both read "Approximately 300W per BDM" under titles scoping them to the BDM WITH its 6+12 I/O. THE LIBRARY IS CURRENTLY INCONSISTENT ABOUT THIS, ON PURPOSE AND VISIBLY. The three BDM variants carry NO power figure, for the reason above. The DQM and DCU cards added later DO carry one - DS8x8 220, DS8x96 320, DS8x192 350, US16x8 220, US16x4 150 - each with a `power-scope` provenance entry saying in the vendor's own words that the number covers the card WITH its I/O module and must not have a rear figure added to it. Both are defensible readings of the same problem: one keeps the per-module answer honest and the chassis total a floor, the other keeps the vendor's only published number reachable. They should not stay different once a pairing-scoped mechanism exists, and this is the record of which way each went and why, so that whoever unifies them is not guessing. THE THREE REAR RF I/O CARDS ADDED LATER FALL ON THE SAME SIDE OF THIS AS THE 6+12. casa/rfd, casa/rfu-16x8 and casa/ups-32x4 carry NO power figure, because Tables A-8 and A-9 give their port counts and connector types and no watts at all, and every figure Casa does publish for the slot is already the pair's - Table A-3 heads the DQM column "Maximum consumption with I/O module" and Table A-4 gives "Single DCU w/ RFU I/O" 200 W against "Single DCU w/ RFU UPS 32x4 I/O" 220 W for the same US16x8. Subtracting one from the other to get a rear card's share would be our arithmetic and would also be the wrong subtraction - the 20 W is the difference between two PAIRINGS, not between two I/O cards.
gaps.wanted: a pairable unit that can carry properties, so that a figure measured on a pair can be attached to the pair. The scope is now DATA - every card here declares `power-draw-scope: module-with-paired-io`, so a chassis sum knows not to add the rear partner and L30 catches it if one gains its own figure - but the scope says only THAT the figure covers a pair, not WHICH pair. The C100G HIG gives the same US16x8 200 W with the RFU I/O and 220 W with the RFU UPS 32x4, and the manifest can carry only one of them. Asking for "a per-module figure" was the wrong question: Casa states none, and one may not exist to be divided out. What is missing is the mechanism, and enough vendors doing this to design one from - Casa is the only one in the corpus.

gaps.note: The HIG body text states "Each fan assembly module has a maximum power consumption of 100W, totaling 300W across the three fan assemblies". Table A-2 of the same guide gives the row "Fan assembly (3)" as "330W maximum, 220W typical". Both are about the set of three and 300 is not 330. The contract takes 100 W because it is the only figure stated PER MODULE, which is the granularity a bay occupant needs; dividing 330 by three would be our arithmetic, not the vendor's. A chassis total is therefore 30 W light against the guide's own set figure, and no per-module typical exists at all.
gaps.wanted: a measurement from a running chassis, a vendor erratum, or a later revision of the guide that drops one of the two figures

gaps.note: Casa rates a power ENTRY module in amps and volts, never in watts. Table A-1 gives "Voltage -42 to -60VDC" and "Current 20A nominal per feed", and the chassis nameplate at Figure 1-3 gives "-48VDC, 30A per Feed (4+4 Feeds)" - but no document states a wattage, and deriving one means choosing a point the vendor left open: two current figures across a voltage range put V x I anywhere from about 810 W to 1800 W per feed. A power entry module also does not convert or regulate; it filters and distributes what the plant feeds it, so its rating is a current-carrying limit rather than the continuous output power-output-w means. The stated volts and amps are recorded in the contract's attrs; the L27 warning stays standing as the record that the watt figure is missing.
gaps.wanted: a wattage for the C100G power entry module from Casa - a nameplate photograph of the module itself would do it, or any document that rates it in watts rather than amps

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

datasheet.title: Casa Systems C40G Converged Cable Access Platform data sheet

devices.description: Casa C40G CMTS/CCAP - 6RU, 6 paired front/rear slots. Takes the same line cards as the C100G but HORIZONTALLY, so the card is one model placed at rotate 90.

gaps.note: THE ORDERING SHEET SELLS FOUR CHASSIS AND THIS LIBRARY MODELS TWO. C40G_DS_RevA lists C40G-CHASSIS-AC and C40G-CHASSIS-DC, which are here, and C40G-CHASSIS-ACR and C40G-CHASSIS-DCR, described as "with Redundant Power and Cooling", which are not. The sheet gives the phrase and nothing else - no count, no which modules, no dimensions - and the installation guide never uses the word for a chassis variant. What the guide DOES say is that the C40G takes up to four 1100 W PSUs operating concurrently and that fewer than two cannot power a C40G-20, which tells you the supplies are redundant by population rather than by chassis. That makes the R variants most likely a populated bundle rather than different metal - but "most likely" is not a source, and inventing two configurations from a four-word description would put a guess where a part number goes.
gaps.wanted: a Casa or CommScope ordering guide saying what the R bundles contain - how many PSUs and fan modules, and whether the chassis itself differs at all

gaps.note: Casa says two things about this terminal and they do not agree. The prose in "Connecting the chassis to ground" says it "provides two M6 screws to connect a double-lug ground terminal cable". Figures 1-2 and 1-4 both DRAW three studs, in a 2x2 grid with the protective-earth mark in the fourth corner, and the two figures agree with each other. THE DRAWING IS FOLLOWED, and the model carries three. The figure is the only source that says anything about arrangement at all, so following the prose would mean inventing a layout for the two it describes; and a third stud has easy explanations - a spare, an alternate lug pitch - while a stud drawn twice that is not there has none. That is a judgement, not a reading, which is why it is filed here. THE PITCH IS NOT MEASURED FROM EITHER. It is borrowed from casa/ground-bolts@1, 15.3, off the maintainer`s hand-built C100G rear SVG. Figure 1-4 gives 13.2 across and 14.7 down for what must be one square grid - an 11 percent disagreement with itself, which is that figure`s anisotropy rather than a rectangular pattern. THE LUG THE GUIDE NAMES POINTS AT 5/8 IN. AND AT A REASON FOR THE THIRD STUD, and neither is drawn yet (#828). Figure 2-10 calls for a Panduit LCD6-14AH-L (or Thomas & Betts 54205UF) 45-degree two-hole lug, and its first step reads "Select either horizontal or vertical mounting": stud-bl and stud-br would be the horizontal landing and stud-tr and stud-br the vertical one. Panduit's 'A' hole-spacing code is 5/8 in., so the pitch is most likely 15.875, not 15.3, but that is a reading of a part number and no held document dimensions the terminal. A pair host across stud-bl and stud-br waits: it would re-grid the terminal and move two of its nested slots under a new key, which is a major, and the pitch it would be drawn at is still an inference.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the C40G rear lower-left corner, which would settle the count and the pitch together in one look; or a dimensioned drawing of the shelf ground terminal, which would let the horizontal pair become one two-hole landing

gaps.note: The card band runs 37.5 to 386.7 in a body 432.95 wide, so it sits 37.5 from the left edge and 46.25 from the right - 8.75 mm out of centre, or 4.375 on the band's own centreline. Everything inside the band agrees with everything else; the question is whether the band is really off-centre in the metal, and nothing we hold answers it. IT IS NOT COSMETIC, and the AC input panel is where it bites. Its four C14 inlets sit behind the four front power supplies. Reflect the supply centres about the PANEL and the inlets are 1.2 out; reflect them about the CHASSIS - which is what walking round a box actually does - and they are 9.95 out. The gap between those two answers IS this asymmetry, and no arrangement of the parts inside the band can close it, because the disagreement is between the band and the chassis rather than within either. THE SUPPORTING NUMBERS ARE ALSO ODD IN THE SAME DIRECTION. The two front fan strips measure 36.0 wide each - equal, as you would expect - but leave 1.5 outside them on the left and 10.25 on the right. Two equal strips with unequal surrounds is exactly the shape of a band that has been positioned from one edge. NOT RESOLVED BY GUESSING, deliberately. Re-centring the band would move the two fan strips, the card bays on both faces, the PSU row, the PSU cover and the AC panel - and it would be one estimate reconciled against another, which this device's `pem-band-top-edge` note already records going wrong twice in opposite directions.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned C40G front or rear elevation from Casa, or a tape measure across a real chassis from its left edge to the first card slot and from the last card slot to its right edge

gaps.note: The PEM band's BOTTOM edge at 264.5 is agreed by every source and is not in doubt. Its TOP edge is known only to about 2 mm, and the three candidates each have support: 194.0 is the direct reading of Figure 1-4 and is impossible, because the card slot above ends at 194.82; 194.82 is flush against that slot; 196.0 is what the bays carry and is what the manifest now uses, on the argument that 194.82 is an accumulation of six DERIVED slot pitches (426.6 mm over 14 slots on the C100G, carried across) and that the front face shows a measured 1.48 mm margin in the equivalent position. That argument is sound but it is an argument, not a measurement, and the whole disagreement is six pixels at 2.982 px/mm. A tape measure on a real C40G, or any Casa drawing that dimensions the rear panel, would settle it in one number. FIGURE 1-12 HAS NOW BEEN LOOKED AT AND DOES NOT SETTLE IT, recorded so nobody spends the search twice. "C40G power entry module" is the only isolated drawing of this part and the first independent look anything has had at it. Its body measures 866 x 381 px for an aspect of 2.273. The modelled 158.0 x 68.5 is 2.307 and the superseded 158.0 x 70.5 is 2.241, and 2.273 lands 0.04 percent off the midpoint of those two - at 158.0 wide it implies a height of 69.51. IT IS EQUIDISTANT AND CONFIRMS NEITHER. This guide's isolated part drawings are in any case demonstrably about 10 percent wrong about their own aspect - Figure 1-20 draws a card at 12.54 whose real aspect is 11.34 - so a 1.5 percent lean is well inside the drawing's own error. THE NUMBER IS THEREFORE NOT MOVED. It has been moved twice already, in both directions, and a third move on evidence that splits the difference would be the reconciliation loop rather than an escape from it. What Figure 1-12 does confirm is the ARRANGEMENT, which is what a figure is good for: a bolted terminal cover across the top with three fasteners, a minus pair of studs above a plus pair inside two outlined blocks, two release levers standing proud of the body top and bottom, and the yellow disconnect-power label to their right - all of which casa/c40g-pem draws. RECORDED BECAUSE THE MODULE AND THE BAY NOW AGREE, which means nothing will ever flag this again - the fit check that found the original 2 mm discrepancy is satisfied by both being wrong together as easily as by both being right.

devices.description: Celestica DS5000 - a 2RU 64 x 800G OSFP data centre and AI fabric switch on a Broadcom Tomahawk 5 (51.2 Tbps) with an Intel Xeon D COM Express CPU and an optional BMC. All sixty-four OSFP cages are on the FRONT in TWO BANKS of sixteen stacked columns, the columns GANGED IN FOURS - four shells of four per bank - and numbered DOWN EACH COLUMN ACROSS BOTH BANKS: column 1 carries ports 1 and 2 in the upper bank and 3 and 4 in the lower. Each column has a legend row of four round lamps between `(up) N` and `N+1 (down)`, above the upper bank and below the lower. At the right of the wall sit a console and a management RJ-45 on their sides in one shell, a USB 3.0 Type-A, a reset button, two SFP28 ports numbered 65 and 66 with four triangular lamps between them, and four system lamps (STAT, ALM, PSU, FAN). The rear carries FOUR 2000 W supplies, two stacked at each end, and THREE fan modules between them; the front panel is black and the rear and body bright metal.

gaps.wanted: What the four lenses in each column's legend row mean and which port each serves. Neither the guide nor the datasheet has an LED section: the guide's overview callouts name the ports, the management jacks and the four system lamps and stop, and the datasheet mentions no LED at all. Two lamps per port is drawn, left pair to the upper port.
What the two lamps on each supply and the one on each fan module mean. The supplies' lamps carry tiny rotated legends that Figure 2 does not resolve; no document names them.

What the three small light squares between the STAT, ALM, PSU and FAN lamps are. A drawing or photograph of the cluster at 15 px/mm or better settles whether they are lenses and whether anything should be punched there.

Orderable part numbers for the 2000 W supply and the fan module. The datasheet's ordering table lists only the system (R4028-F9002-A1) and the guide's FRU pages give removal steps without part numbers, so both components are named for their form rather than their PN.

Orthographic drawings of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The guide's Side View and rear three-quarter view and the two product renders show all four at an angle: a plain lid with two stamped handles and two long pressings, and side walls carrying rail screws. Each face carries an `empty:` sentence.

Which way each OSFP bank faces. Figure 1 reads as 0/0 in the upper bank and 180/180 in the lower (a stacked 2x1 cage on each face of one board), the drawing here keeps 0/180 in both, and #799 first proposed 0/0 throughout. A photograph of the front, or a decision on the elevation's reading, settles it; until then every pair is held in stack-exceptions.

devices.description: Cisco ASR 9000 Series ASR 9001 Router - a 2 RU fixed-port aggregation services router with an integrated route processor, four fixed 10 GE SFP+ ports, two modular port adapter bays and 120 Gbps of fabric. Everything is on the front face: both MPA bays, both power supplies, the side-mounted fan tray and every port. The rear is a plain louvred panel.

gaps.note: The fixed-port install guide's power table (Table 35, "Power Consumption Specifications") has a column for the ASR 9001 and for the larger routers and none for the ASR 9001-S, and no other held document prints a power figure for the -S. The -S therefore lists the device's power figures, which are the ASR 9001's. Its 60 Gbps fabric bandwidth and its description are stated on the configuration.
gaps.wanted: a power figure for the ASR 9001-S: a column of its own in the guide's power table, or a data sheet that prints one.

gaps.note: Table 4 of the fixed-port install guide gives the 10MHz and 1PPS connectors as DIN 1.0/2.3. The standards registry has no key for it - sma, smb, mcx and f-type are there, DIN 1.0/2.3 is not - so these two openings are declared as panel cutouts at their measured size rather than composed from a std/ part. Substituting sma or smb would name a connector Cisco does not. THE REASON WAS vendor-silent AND THAT WAS THE WRONG TOKEN. Cisco is not silent - it names the connector outright. What is missing is a panel-cutout dimension, which is needs-drawing, and the difference matters because the two tokens ask different things of a reader: vendor-silent reads as closed until better documents appear, needs-drawing reads as an errand somebody can run today. The correction came from asr9k-cards, who had just been wrong in exactly this direction about the XFP - concluding a figure was unsourceable after searching the intake rather than the standards - and found it in INF-8077i ten minutes after looking somewhere else. IEC 61169-8 is the somewhere else here, and nobody has opened it yet.
gaps.wanted: a std/din-1-0-2-3 part and its standards.yaml key. THE CONNECTOR IS STANDARDISED, so a sourced dimension exists to be found rather than estimated - DIN 1.0/2.3 is specified in IEC 61169-8, and any manufacturer's bulkhead-jack panel drawing carries the D-hole figure. std/mcx is the worked example of exactly this being done properly earlier tonight: registered from IEC 61169-36 / CECC 22220 at 4.95 x 4.50 with confidence verified, replacing an estimate that was 28 percent too small. This should be done the same way, and until it is, an sma or smb standing in would be a plausible wrong answer - which is the failure mode this project keeps having to dig back out
the buried marks moved clear of the components that paint over them

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold
`attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices

devices.description: Cisco ASR 9006 Router - the 10RU, six-slot member of the ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Routers. Cards mount HORIZONTALLY: slots 0 and 1 at the bottom of the cage are reserved for a redundant RSP pair, slots 2 to 5 above them take line cards. Two fan trays sit above the cage behind a hinged door, and a single power shelf below it carries the AC or DC power modules, whose inlets are on the rear face. Modelled as a BARE CAGE: every slot is a bay that a card component drops into, not a traced faceplate.

gaps.note: Cisco publishes no chassis-level power draw for any ASR 9000. Table 14's "Power Dissipation" row says only "Use the Cisco Power Calculator ... to estimate the maximum power distribution", so the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Recorded in provenance as no-chassis-power-figure since the family was modelled; scoped here so a comparison can tell this apart from a figure nobody has looked for
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level maximum and typical draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the Power Calculator is the only answer the vendor will give

gaps.note: cisco/a9k-pwr-3kw-ac@1 states 142.78 mm wide. Three of them need 428.34 mm and this chassis's power shelf interior measures 416.50, so they do not fit - lint L13 flagged the overlap directly when they were placed at the measured centres. Against that, the stencil's shape box for the 'A9K Power Module' master reads 0.5477 in, which is 139.12 mm at the stencil's 1:10 scale, and my own measurement of the three openings in the ASR 9006 front master gives 138.35, 137.50 and 138.23. Those two agree to under a millimetre, and three at 139.12 come to 417.36 against a 416.50 shelf - the arithmetic a shelf that holds exactly three ought to produce. The 142.78 is most likely the art measured over something that is not the module's seating width, the same class of error as reading a card's shape box instead of its art. The bays here are sized to the measured openings, so the chassis is right and the component and the chassis disagree by about 3.7 mm until someone re-measures the master.
gaps.wanted: a re-measurement of the 'A9K Power Module' stencil master, or a Cisco dimension for the version 1 power module

gaps.note: STILL OPEN; the numbers around it changed. This file and the ASR 9010 manifest carry pitches that differ - 46.605 here against 44.332 there - for two chassis that take the same cards. For a while the 9010 was divided unevenly to fit a 1.81 in (46.0 mm) RSP-880; under the card standard every card is drawn 41.4 thick, so that reason is gone and the 9010 is again divided evenly across its measured cage. The two pitches still differ because the two measured cages differ, which is not a contradiction. HERE THE EVEN SIX-WAY DIVISION OF THE 279.63 mm CAGE IS STILL AN ASSUMPTION: at 41.4 per card any division giving each slot at least 41.4 admits every card, so the card size cannot discriminate between an even split and an uneven one. The even division is kept because it is what the cage measures and nothing here favours another. Neither this master nor the 9010 master prints slot labels or draws cage dividers, which is why both were assumptions in the first place - the 9904, 9906, 9910, 9912 and 9922 all have a ruler in the picture and these two do not.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned front elevation of the ASR 9006, or a per-slot width from any Cisco document

gaps.note: Two figures in b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf give the ASR 9006 body width differently. Table 13 "Cisco ASR 9000 Series Routers Physical Descriptions" (p130) says 17.50 inches (44.45 cm). Figure 9 "Cisco ASR 9006 Router Chassis Footprint Dimensions - Top Down View" (p24) dimensions the same body at 17.38 inches (44.15 cm). Same measure, same part, 3 mm apart, so this is a real conflict and not two scopes. The manifest carries 44.45 because the spec table is authoritative for overall dimensions and because Cisco's own Visio master independently records 1.9 in at 1:10 over the flanges, which back-solves to Table 13's split once the 19.05 mm flange protrusion is subtracted. The likeliest reconciliation is that 17.50 is over the outer skin and 17.38 is the sheet metal at the section plane Figure 9 cuts, but no document we hold says that, so it is not written as though one does. The height is unaffected - both sources and the stencil agree on 17.50 in there.
gaps.wanted: a Cisco mechanical drawing with a tolerance, or a tape measure on a real ASR 9006

gaps.note: The power modules load from the front but their inlets are on the rear, and the only artwork we hold for that rear panel is the stencil's ASR-9006-AC Rear master, which draws the VERSION 1 tray: three IEC inlets labelled M2, M1, M0 left to right (mirrored from the front's M0, M1, M2) with the legend "100-240V 50/60 Hz 16A MAX (3X)" and a yellow warning label. This chassis is modelled as version 2, which has four modules and therefore four inlets, and no figure in any document we hold shows the version 2 rear panel. Rather than mirror three inlets into four and invent a pitch, the rear carries the inlet panel's outer band only. The DC rear is a further unknown again - there is no ASR-9006-DC master in the stencil at all.
gaps.wanted: a figure or photograph of the version 2 AC rear panel, and of the DC rear panel

gaps.note: The air filter is real, sourced and correctly typed as a bay - Table 17 of b-asr9k-hardware-installation-guide.pdf places it along the right side accessible from the rear, and Figure 207 shows the panel and its thumb screw. What is NOT sourced is its geometry. Figure 207 is a three-quarter perspective view with no dimension lines on it, so its aspect is foreshortened and it fails gate 1 as a source of absolute size. The filter's 52 mm width and its 8 mm standoff from the rear edge are read as fractions of that figure and anchored to the chassis depth, and its height is set to the card cage band rather than measured. Treat the filter's extent as the one feature here that a tape measure would most likely move. Its presence, its side, its access direction and the fact that it is user-replaceable are all stated in words by the guide and are not in doubt.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side elevation of the ASR 9006, or the air filter's own spare-part drawing

gaps.note: RENAMED FROM blank-faces AND REWORDED, because both faces stopped being blank and the gap was still describing the file as it stood two commits ago. NO DOCUMENT WE HOLD SHOWS EITHER FACE OF AN ASR 9006 - that part is unchanged and is the gap. What each face now carries is derived from a figure of a DIFFERENT face, which is a weaker thing than being drawn and is why the gap stays open. The bottom carries the rack mounting surface, because the plane is dimensioned in Figure 9's top-down view and necessarily cuts the underside at the same depth it cuts the top. The left carries one of the three NEBS bonding points, because Figure 58 callouts a left-side pad and its position is INFERRED from a three-quarter view rather than dimensioned. Neither is a bottom or left drawing; both are a fact about the chassis that has to intersect this face. Everything else about these two faces - feet, labels, vents, plates, the flange profile - is still unknown, and the guide's "There is no clearance requirement for the left side of the chassis" (b-asr9k-hardware-installation-guide.pdf p1172) is consistent with a solid unfeatured panel without proving one. The sizes are from Table 13 and Figure 9 and are right, so the rack elevation and the 3D box are right, which is the load these two views actually carry.
gaps.wanted: a six-face photograph set, or the mechanical drawings behind Figure 9

gaps.note: No held Cisco document names A9K-16X100GE-SE beside a chassis. The card is accepted by the line card slots on the evidence of its -TR sibling's data sheet row (the se-line-card-seating provenance note), which is an inference and not a statement from Cisco. The -SE differs from the -TR in buffering and table scale, and that is not modelled. Re-read when the SIP-700 and SIP-700-8G were seated in the same slots: this gap is about the -SE cards only and is unchanged.
gaps.wanted: a Cisco document that names the -SE part beside a chassis, or says it is not compatible with one

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory`; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices

devices.description: Cisco ASR 9010 Router - the 21RU, ten-slot member of the ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Routers. Cards mount VERTICALLY across the full width of the cage: the two CENTRE slots, 4 and 5, are reserved for a redundant RSP pair, with four line card slots either side of them. A cable management tray runs along the top, two stacked fan trays and a front air intake sit below the cage, and two power shelves fill the bottom. Modelled as a BARE CAGE: every slot is a bay a card component drops into, not a traced faceplate.

gaps.note: THE CARD BAY EXTENTS ARE A FAMILY STANDARD, NOT MEASUREMENTS OF THIS CAGE. All ten slots are 41.4 x 395.7 with a 41.4 x 355.6 opening, chosen so one card component fits every ASR 9000 chassis. Two of the three numbers are Cisco figures: 395.7 is the fourth-generation "includes ejector bracket/lever" envelope, which a lab measurement of a real A9K-RSP880 supports at about 15 1/2 in (roc-ops/Portrayal#16), and 355.6 is the Table A-10 plate length, which the cage measured off the stencil (354.95) matches to 0.65 mm. The 41.4 thickness is the figure Cisco states most often and has NOT been measured; the 43.7 of the original-generation cards and the 46.0 of the RSP-880 are overridden by it as a modelling decision. The slot division is the measured cage split ten ways, which is arithmetic: the stencil master draws the cage as one undivided rectangle, and no per-slot width was found in the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide, the Hardware Installation Guide or the Overview and Reference Guide. The danger this entry exists to record still applies: a fit check compares a bay to a component and neither to the world, so a standard shared by both passes it whether or not it is true.
gaps.wanted: a caliper reading of an ASR 9000 card thickness (requested on roc-ops/Portrayal#16), a dimensioned front elevation or per-slot width for the ASR 9010, or a tape measure on a real one

gaps.note: cisco/a9k-pwr-3kw-ac@1 states 142.78 mm wide. Three of them need 428.34 mm and this chassis's power shelf interior measures 416.50, so they do not fit - lint L13 flagged the overlap directly when they were placed at the measured centres. Against that, the stencil's shape box for the 'A9K Power Module' master reads 0.5477 in, which is 139.12 mm at the stencil's 1:10 scale, and my own measurement of the three openings in the ASR 9006 front master gives 138.35, 137.50 and 138.23. Those two agree to under a millimetre, and three at 139.12 come to 417.36 against a 416.50 shelf - the arithmetic a shelf that holds exactly three ought to produce. The 142.78 is most likely the art measured over something that is not the module's seating width, the same class of error as reading a card's shape box instead of its art. The bays here are sized to the measured openings, so the chassis is right and the component and the chassis disagree by about 3.7 mm until someone re-measures the master.
gaps.wanted: a re-measurement of the 'A9K Power Module' stencil master, or a Cisco dimension for the version 1 power module

gaps.note: The ASR 9010's two fan trays occupy the band between the card guide bar at 566.51 mm and the front air intake grille at 673.60 mm - 107.09 mm for the pair, which is measured and solid. Where one ended and the other began was NOT measured. Scanning that band finds a dark separator at about 605.8 mm, but it does not bisect the band (39.3 mm above it, 66.9 mm below), so it was read as internal faceplate detail rather than the boundary, and an EVEN split was recorded as the right inference: the master labels both trays "ASR-9010-FAN", so they are the same part stacked twice and the same part is the same height. RESOLVED, AND THE SEPARATOR WAS THE BOUNDARY AFTER ALL. Dismissing it assumed the two trays fill the band, and they do not - two trays of 33.32 come to 66.64 of 107.09. cisco/asr-9010-fan was measured off this chassis's own front master at y 571.44 to 604.76, and that bottom edge and the separator at 605.8 agree to 1.04 mm: two measurements taken for different reasons, landing on the same line. Both trays are seated there now rather than split evenly, so the placement is measured and the inference is retired. What the band holds BELOW them - about 34 mm between the second tray and the grille starting at 675.08 - is still unnamed, and the band stays ONE cutout because a single opening with two trays in the top of it and intake beneath is what the guide's own cooling-path figure (Figure 71) draws.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned front elevation, or the ASR-9010-FAN spare-part drawing

gaps.note: The card slots are bays and accept the line card and RSP blank. THE FAN TRAYS HAVE SINCE LEFT THIS LIST - cisco/asr-9010-fan now exists and both are seated as bays at the positions its own size provenance measured off this chassis's front master. The eight power module positions and the air filter are still NOT modelled as bays, because a bay must name a component that fits it and library/components/cisco/ carries no version 2 or 3 power module and no filter. Their openings ARE measured and are drawn as cutouts, so the metal is right and only the occupants are missing. The power shelf openings are 13.96 to 431.66 mm at y 811.74 and 873.33; the fan band is 566.51 to 673.60. Pointing them at the line card blank would lint clean and claim something false - a 41.4 x 395.7 filler plate does not cover a power module opening.
gaps.wanted: an ASR 9010 fan tray, the version 2 and 3 AC and DC power modules, and the chassis air filter

gaps.note: The cisco logo, the "ASR 9000 Series" wordmark and an "OPEN" legend are printed on the CABLE MANAGEMENT TRAY, not on chassis metal - the stencil master draws them inside that band. Per the skill, text on a part's own face is that part's silkscreen, so this chassis deliberately carries none and the tray is not modelled as a placement for want of a component. The band itself is measured (0 to 163.76 mm) and drawn as decor, so the metal is right and only the printing and the tray are absent. This is the same decision taken on the ASR 9006's fan tray door.
gaps.wanted: a cable management tray component carrying its own branding

gaps.note: THE BOTTOM IS THE ONLY FACE OF THIS CHASSIS WITH NO SOURCE, and it is not a gap in this file's research. There is no bottom view of ANY ASR 9000 chassis anywhere in the 78-document intake: every figure caption in all 65 PDFs was searched for "Bottom View", "underside" and "bottom of the chassis", and the result is zero hits. That is a fact about how Cisco documents a rack chassis rather than about this model - a face that sits on rack rails and is never serviced gets no figure. The face is SIZED correctly from Table 13, so a rack elevation and the 3D box are the right shape; what it lacks is any statement of what is on it. Nothing is invented to fill it, and no region is added naming the absence, because a check passed by annotating that you have nothing is worse than a check failed honestly. THIS HOLDS THE CHASSIS AT CAPABILITY 2. Front, rear, top, left and right all now carry sourced content; the bottom alone does not, and level 3's implementation requires content on all six. The written design asks only that six faces be "present, sized, and mutually consistent", which this file satisfies - the content requirement comes from `_has_content`, which was written for level 1. See docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.
gaps.wanted: a bottom elevation, a photograph of the underside, or a way for a view to declare itself deliberately empty so that empty-by-verification counts where empty-by-omission does not

devices.description: Cisco ASR 9000 Series ASR 9901 Router - a 2 RU fixed-port provider-edge router with an integrated route processor and 456 Gbps of fabric. Everything a user touches is on the front: forty-two ports across the top in five blocks - eight 1GE, twelve dual-rate 10/1GE, two 100GE, twelve more 10/1GE and eight more 1GE - and below them the timing, management and console jacks, nine alarm lamps, a four-character LED matrix display and the shelf power switch. The rear carries three fan trays and two 1.6 kW supplies. Airflow is front to back, and nothing seats on the front face at all.

gaps.note: The fixed-port install guide names the Connectivity Management Processor port only in the front-panel callouts, and Table 4 has no row for it; the series overview guide describes CMP as a secondary processor with its own front-panel management Ethernet port, with no rate. The 9901 data sheet lists it without one.
gaps.wanted: the CMP jack rate, so the port can state a `speed`.

gaps.note: TWO CISCO DOCUMENTS GIVE THIS CHASSIS TWO HEIGHTS. The ASR 9901 Router Data Sheet (c78-740540) Table 2 says "Height: 3.43 inches (8.7 cm)", which is 87.12 mm. The fixed-port Hardware Installation Guide says "Height of the ... Cisco ASR 9901 Router and Cisco ASR 9001 Router is 3.47 inches (8.8 cm)", which is 88.14 - and note that one sentence covers two chassis, and that 3.47 in is the ASR 9001's own data sheet figure. THE DATA SHEET IS CARRIED AND THE STENCIL IS WHY. The rear master's shape box reads 87.38 mm and its body ink, at the scale set by the body WIDTH alone, comes out 87.11 mm - a hundredth of a millimetre from the data sheet's 87.12, on an axis that was never anchored to it. The guide's sentence looks like a sibling's number reused; it is recorded here rather than dismissed.
gaps.wanted: a ruler on a real ASR 9901, or a Cisco mechanical drawing.

gaps.note: THE DISPLAY IS MODELLED AND ITS READING DIRECTION IS NOT. cisco/led-matrix-4@1 carries the guide's "one row of four characters" and the twenty-eight readings of Tables 25 and 26, so the model can be asked what this display says. THE WINDOW STANDS ON END, and that is settled. It was two drawings agreeing, which is one drawing counted twice - the stencil master and Figure 12's line art, both portrait, both hatched with diagonals, either of which could have been a draughting symbol for "display". It is not a symbol: photographs of three real units show a light rounded bezel left of the CISCO wordmark with a dark portrait window in it, and the sharpest resolves the DIAMOND LATTICE the drawings were tracing. So Cisco's "one row of four characters" reads TURNED. WHICH WAY IT TURNS IS IN NOTHING. Up or down, no document says. Fourteen resale listings for this chassis were opened and every unit photographed is POWERED OFF, so not one of them reads the matrix. The skin draws the window and nothing in it, `characters: 4` is Cisco's sentence rather than a reading of the artwork, and no rotation is claimed.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a POWERED ASR 9901 front panel - the matrix mid-boot would read it off in one frame - or any Cisco drawing that puts characters in the window.

gaps.note: FAN 2, FAN 1 and FAN 0 are printed bottom-to-top on a narrow rail at the right of each tray, and the tray's own drawn plate covers that rail - the captive screw sits on the same strip. This model draws each tray as a filled rectangle, so the three marks land under their bays and L21 reports them. The marks are kept where the master puts them rather than moved somewhere they would render, because moving them would put ink where the device has none. It is the same defect cisco/asr-9902 and cisco/asr-9903 carry and the same fix closes all three.
gaps.wanted: cisco/asr-9901-fan@1 drawn with its flange cut away where the chassis prints the slot label, so the mark shows through.

gaps.note: The nine lamps are counted by Figure 12's callout 8 and printed by the master, and no document in the intake says what their colours mean. The guide's RP Front Panel Indicators section describes the ASR 9001's cluster and the LED matrix; Table 21, "LEDs at System Startup", covers line cards, power modules and fan trays. Searched both, plus the data sheet, for each legend by name. devices.description: Cisco ASR 9000 Series ASR 9902 Router - a 2 RU fixed-port aggregation services router delivering up to 800 Gbps. Two route processors across the top and the integrated fixed board below them, carrying forty-eight ports in two mirrored slices: eight SFP28, three QSFP28 and one QSFP-DD and twelve SFP+ on each. The rear carries two 1.6 kW power modules at the ends and three fan trays between them, with the power switch on the left panel and the NEBS grounding lug on the right. Airflow is front to back. Nothing seats in the front: the board is part of the chassis and there is no Port Expansion Card bay, which is what separates this from its 3 RU ASR 9903 sibling.

gaps.note: The PWR-1.6KW supply is 74.94 mm wide in this chassis' rear master and in its two bays, and that is an estimate: the ASR 9903's master reads the same part 74.02 once rescaled, and a search online and in the document set on 2026-10-18 found no source that gives the module's width. Both chassis seat cisco/pwr-1p6kw-ac@2 and cisco/pwr-1p6kw-dc@2 at 74.94. See provenance.supply-width.
gaps.wanted: A Cisco site-planning or spares document with a power-module table, or a straight-on rear photograph of an ASR 9902 or ASR 9903 with the supplies seated, resolving at least 2 px/mm across the body.

gaps.note: FT0, FT1 and FT2 are printed bottom-to-top on a narrow rail at the left of each tray, and the tray's own drawn plate starts on that rail rather than beside it - the captive screw sits on the same strip. This model draws each tray as a filled rectangle, so the three marks land under their bays and L21 reports them. The marks are kept where the master puts them rather than moved somewhere they would render, because moving them would put ink where the device has none. It is the same defect cisco/asr-9903's fan labels carry and the same fix closes both.
gaps.wanted: cisco/asr-9902-fan@1 drawn with its left flange cut away where the chassis prints the slot label, so the mark shows through.

gaps.note: THE TOP, BOTTOM AND TWO SIDES ARE SIZED AND NOT DRAWN, and each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where the search ran. What they have in common is that no source in the intake ELEVATES them. The Visio stencil's 119 masters are front and rear elevations and hold no plan or side view at all. The install guide's figures for this chassis are two elevations, a top-view FOOTPRINT (Figure 18, which dimensions the outline and draws no feature), an airflow path, eight rack-mounting sequences across 19-inch and 23-inch, 2-post and 4-post racks, a stacking figure and an air-filter view - the mounting figures show the sides at an angle and dimension nothing on them. None is positioned by anything, and drawing them by eye off a three-quarter render would put unmeasured furniture on four faces at once.
gaps.wanted: a Cisco mechanical drawing of the ASR 9902, or orthographic photographs of the top and one side with something of known size in frame.

gaps.note: The furniture strip at the right of the RP row carries a captive screw, a round dimple above it and a small dark circle between them, and the guide names none of the three. The same two unnamed features appear on the ASR 9903 in the same place. They are the right shape for an ESD wrist-strap jack and a captive-screw well, and calling them so would be a guess with a citation attached, so they are left off the face.

devices.description: Cisco ASR 9000 Series ASR 9903 Router - a 3 RU fixed-port aggregation services router delivering up to 3.6 Tbps. Everything a user touches is on the front: two route processors across the top, the integrated fixed board in the middle with sixteen 100GE QSFP28 ports and twenty 10GE SFP+ ports, and one bay below it for an optional Port Expansion Card. The rear carries four 1.6 kW power modules in a row and four fan trays below them, with the NEBS grounding lug on a fixed panel between the middle pair. Airflow is front to back.

gaps.note: THE POWER MODULE'S WIDTH IS AN ESTIMATE, 74.94 MM, AND THE TWO CHASSIS' MASTERS DO NOT AGREE ON IT. The ASR 9902's rear master reads the PWR-1.6KW supply 74.94 mm wide; this chassis' master read it 74.69 at the old scale, which the rescale to the guide's 439.9 makes 74.02. The part has one width, so the 74.94 is carried on both chassis, marked estimated, and the 0.92 mm to this master's reading is the open difference. Searched on 2026-10-18, online and in the document set, for a Cisco figure that dimensions the module or a straight-on photograph that could be measured: the data sheets give the chassis and the two PECs only, the installation guide's power chapters give no envelope, and the reseller listings found are unlabelled and not credible. Nothing settles the width to 0.5 mm.
gaps.wanted: A Cisco site-planning or spares document with a power-module table, or a straight-on rear photograph of an ASR 9902 or ASR 9903 with the supplies seated, resolving at least 2 px/mm across the body.

gaps.note: TWO CISCO DOCUMENTS GIVE THIS CHASSIS TWO MAXIMUM WEIGHTS and they are not reconcilable as different scopes. Table 2 of the ASR 9903 data sheet (c78-744035) gives ASR 9903 chassis with 2 RPs, 4 PSUs and 4 FANs, 5.18 x 17.475 x 30 in. and 81.62 lb, or 131.57 x 443.86 x 762 mm and 37 kg. The fixed-port Hardware Installation Guide's Lifting Guidelines read "A fully-configured Cisco ASR 9903 can weigh as much as 70 pounds (31.75 kg)". Both are maxima and the guide's scope is the WIDER of the two - "fully configured" must include a PEC, which the data sheet's list does not - so the larger figure should have been the guide's, and it is 5.25 kg smaller. `chassis.weight-kg` carries the data sheet's 37 kg because the source table makes the data sheet authoritative for weight, and this gap carries the guide's figure so the disagreement is not silently resolved.
gaps.wanted: a scale under a real ASR 9903, or a Cisco document that states the weight with its scope spelled out.

gaps.note: The furniture strip at the right of the RP row carries four features. Two are identified and drawn: a hex grounding stud and an IEC 60417-5019 earth symbol. The other two are not. Above the stud the master draws a plain circular dimple about 3 mm across, and between them a smaller dark circle that reads as a through-hole on the install guide's Figure 3 render at 2.7 px/mm. NO SENTENCE IN THE INTAKE NAMES EITHER. They are the right shape and the right place for an ESD wrist-strap jack and a captive-screw well - the ASR 9001 has an ESD socket on its front and Figure 9 of the same guide points at it - but the ASR 9903 is not in that figure and the guide's ESD section names no socket for this chassis. Drawing them as an esd-jack would be a guess with a citation attached, so they are left off.
gaps.wanted: a callout in a Cisco figure, or a photograph of the front right corner close enough to read the two features.

gaps.note: The front master draws a recessed frame 13.39 x 26.01 mm at the left end of the fixed board with a yellow tag in it reading ATTENTION / ON-OFF, and the install guide's Figure 3 render shows the same recess with a plain white tag. WHAT IT IS, IS NOT SAID FOR THIS CHASSIS. The identical assembly on the ASR 9902's REAR is captioned in Figure 158 of the same guide with POWER printed under it and a lamp beside it, so on that chassis it is a power switch. For the ASR 9903 the guide says only that the AC and DC PSUs for ASR 9903 routers have no power switch, being plug-and-play, and that the power LED (PWR) is on the router's front, which places a PWR lamp on the front and names no switch. So the recess and its tag are drawn as panel decor and silkscreen, exactly as the artwork has them, and nothing here asserts that they are a switch.
gaps.wanted: a callout naming this feature on the ASR 9903, or a photograph of the front left corner.

gaps.note: FT0 to FT3 are printed on the chassis in a notch at the bottom left of each tray - the tray is cut away there and the label plate shows through, which is how the drawing and the guide's Figure 4 both have it. This model draws each tray as a filled rectangle, so the four marks land under their bays and L21 reports them. The marks are kept at the positions the master gives rather than moved somewhere they would render, because moving them would put ink where the device has none; the honest fix is a notched tray outline, which is a component change.
gaps.wanted: cisco/asr-9903-fan@2 drawn with its bottom-left notch, so the chassis label shows through it.

gaps.note: THE TOP, BOTTOM AND TWO SIDES ARE SIZED AND NOT DRAWN, and each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where the search ran. What they have in common is that no source in the intake ELEVATES them. The Visio stencil's 119 masters are front and rear elevations and hold no plan or side view at all. The install guide's figures for this chassis are two elevations, a top-view FOOTPRINT (Figure 19, which dimensions the outline and draws no feature), an airflow path, two rack-mounting sequences, a bracket-to-side sequence and an air-filter exploded view - the last two show the sides at an angle and dimension nothing on them. The data sheet gives the envelope. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, from the photographs, is a cisco wordmark and a large product label on the top, four feet and the bracket landings underneath, and a bracket rail on each side. None is positioned by anything, and drawing them by eye off a three-quarter render would put unmeasured furniture on four faces at once.

devices.description: Cisco ASR 9904 Router - the smallest modular chassis of the ASR 9900 generation, four slots in 6 RU. Cards mount HORIZONTALLY and the redundant RSP pair sits in the MIDDLE, slots 1 and 2, with a line card above and below it. A single fan tray is fitted from the rear and a power shelf of four modules fills the bottom. Modelled as a BARE CAGE. The card openings are cutouts rather than bays for now - see gaps.

gaps.note: Cisco publishes no chassis-level power draw for any ASR 9000. Table 14's "Power Dissipation" row says only "Use the Cisco Power Calculator ... to estimate the maximum power distribution", so the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Recorded in provenance as no-chassis-power-figure since the family was modelled; scoped here so a comparison can tell this apart from a figure nobody has looked for
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level maximum and typical draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the Power Calculator is the only answer the vendor will give

gaps.note: The power shelf is drawn as one opening, 423.85 x 48 mm, rather than four module openings. Figure 20 and Table 15 both establish that there are FOUR modules and that Cisco numbers them M0 to M3, so the count and the numbering are not in doubt - what is missing is where the boundaries fall. The stencil master draws this shelf POPULATED, with each module rendered as a pair of fan wheels, so scanning the band returns grille detail rather than separators and the per-module pitch could not be recovered the way the ASR 9006's was from its bare shelf. An even four-way division would be arithmetic rather than measurement, and the 9006 showed the gaps between modules are not uniform with the end margins.
gaps.wanted: a bare-shelf figure, or a front elevation with the power shelf dimensioned

gaps.note: top, bottom and left are sized from Table 13 and Figure 10 (the 9904's top-down footprint) and are deliberately EMPTY. No document we hold shows any of the three. The right side is not blank - the guide states the air inlet and the air filter are both there - and the rear carries the single fan tray and two grounding points, so four of the six faces have sourced content. The sizes here are right, which is what these views are carrying for a rack elevation and the 3D box.
gaps.wanted: a six-face photograph set, or the mechanical drawings behind Figure 10

gaps.note: No held Cisco document names A9K-16X100GE-SE or A99-32X100GE-SE beside a chassis. devices.description: Cisco ASR 9906 Router - the 14 RU, six-slot member of the ASR 9900 generation. Cards mount VERTICALLY and the redundant RSP pair takes the OUTER slots, 0 and 5, with four line cards between them. The layout is unusual for the family: a vertical power shelf runs down the LEFT of the card cage and two fan trays sit behind a door on the RIGHT, with a full-width air intake along the bottom. Modelled as a BARE CAGE; the card openings are cutouts rather than bays - see gaps.

gaps.note: Cisco publishes no chassis-level power draw for any ASR 9000. Table 14's "Power Dissipation" row says only "Use the Cisco Power Calculator ... to estimate the maximum power distribution", so the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Recorded in provenance as no-chassis-power-figure since the family was modelled; scoped here so a comparison can tell this apart from a figure nobody has looked for
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level maximum and typical draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the Power Calculator is the only answer the vendor will give

gaps.note: THESE BAY DIMENSIONS ARE A MODELLING STANDARD AND NOT MEASUREMENTS OF THIS CAGE. Every slot bay is 41.4 x 395.7 with a 41.4 x 355.6 opening, the envelope now shared by every full-size ASR 9000 card (see asr9000-card-standard). Earlier revisions grew these bays to 42.67 x 403.40 to satisfy a fit check against one accepted card, which a fit check would pass just as readily if both sides were wrong; that is gone, but a standard is not a measurement either. What each figure rests on: 395.7 is the Cisco "includes ejector bracket/lever" envelope and agrees with a lab measurement of a real RSP-880; 355.6 is the Table A-10 plate length; 41.4 is the thickness Cisco states most often and has not been measured. What IS independently grounded here is the cage, measured off the stencil at 260.52 x 364.32 and corroborated by the printed slot labels, and the 43.42 pitch. The measured cage height is 8.72 mm taller than the 355.6 opening now drawn, a difference the standard accepts rather than explains.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned figure giving the clear opening of any ASR 9000 card cage, or a caliper reading of a card thickness, either of which would replace a standard figure with a measured one

gaps.note: The shelf is one cutout, as on the ASR 9904, and the module positions are now bays inside it: three AC (`ps0-pm-0` to `ps0-pm-2`, PWR-6KW-AC-V3, base and `ac`) and four DC (`ps0-dcpm-0` to `ps0-dcpm-3`, PWR-4.4KW-DC-V3, `dc` only), M0 at the bottom, each turned from the horizontal drawing. Figure 21, Figure 42 (AC, six fan wheels), Figure 43 (DC, eight) and Tables 15 and 16 give the counts; the pitch is the stencil master's, 139.0 mm for AC and 104.7 mm for DC. THE AC AND DC BAYS SHARE ONE FOOTPRINT; FILL ONE SET. Each set is `only-in` its own configurations so the two never coexist, and that mixing AC and DC is not supported (Data Sheet p5, "mixing of AC and DC supplies is not supported"; Hardware Installation Guide Table 2: "A hybrid (AC+DC) power configuration is not supported") is not enforced by the model. STILL OPEN: the module dimensions are measured off the stencil's populated drawing and a straight-on callout, not stated by Cisco (see the two components); the shelf is not drawn empty, so its own metal (the end hardware, the divider rails, the ON/STANDBY switch Figure 67 shows on the front) is not drawn; the module weight and depth are not stated; the DC tray's feed arrangement is not modelled; the tray itself (`A9K-AC-PEM-V3` and `A9K-DC-PEM-V3`, drawn 468.12 mm wide against a 447 mm chassis) is not seated, because no tray-level bay exists - which part is the 9906's tray is a question, since the guide's `show platform` output names `0/PT0 A9K-AC-PEM-V3` only for the 9910. The module-to-module bays are positioned on the measured pitch and sized by their occupants, so they are a modelling standard and not a measurement of the empty shelf.
gaps.wanted: a figure showing the power shelf empty, or a dimensioned front elevation, and the module dimensions from Cisco

gaps.note: The ASR 9906's rear carries the fabric card cage and we know a great deal ABOUT it and almost nothing about its geometry. Cisco's stencil does list an "ASR-9906 Rear" master (image104.emf, 24.50 in tall), which has not been used to draw this face, and Figure 21 shows only the front. The count is sourced but indirectly: Table 13 quotes the configured weight for a chassis "Configured with two fan trays, two RSPs, five fabric cards, and one PEM", so five, and the sibling ASR 9910's Figure 22 shows fabric slots numbered from 0. Nothing states their width, their height, or where the PEM sits. The rear is therefore sized and carries regions naming what is there. ONE CUTOUT NOW EXISTS ON THIS FACE and it is not an exception to that: the NEBS grounding receptacle, which Table 12 states and Figure 61 shows, on an offset borrowed from the sibling chassis rather than measured - see provenance/grounding. The fabric card cage is still not drawn and is no better sourced than it was.
gaps.wanted: an ASR 9906 rear elevation, or a rear photograph

gaps.note: THE BOTTOM IS THE ONLY FACE OF THIS CHASSIS WITH NO SOURCE, and it is not a gap in this file's research. There is no bottom view of ANY ASR 9000 chassis anywhere in the 78-document intake: every figure caption in all 65 PDFs was searched for "Bottom View", "underside" and "bottom of the chassis", and the result is zero hits. That is a fact about how Cisco documents a rack chassis rather than about this model - a face that sits on rack rails and is never serviced gets no figure. The face is SIZED correctly from Table 13, so a rack elevation and the 3D box are the right shape; what it lacks is any statement of what is on it. Nothing is invented to fill it, and no region is added naming the absence, because a check passed by annotating that you have nothing is worse than a check failed honestly. THIS NO LONGER HOLDS THE CHASSIS BACK, and the reason is worth recording rather than deleting. The face now carries what IS sourced about it - the two rack mounting surfaces, at 5.00 in and 9.45 in from the front - so it is no longer content-free and the chassis reads at capability 4. That is not the gap closing. The bottom still has no elevation and nothing is drawn of what sits between those rails; what changed is that the little which is published got written down. The sibling ASR 9910, which has no bottom view at all, is the one still held at capability 2.
gaps.wanted: a bottom elevation or a photograph of the underside. What is on this face between the rack rails remains unstated by every document in the intake

devices.description: Cisco ASR 9910 Router - the 21 RU, ten-slot member of the ASR 9900 generation. Cards mount VERTICALLY on the front with the redundant RSP pair at the OUTER slots, 0 and 9, and eight line cards between them. The REAR carries a separate cage of five fabric cards with its own numbering restarting at 0, two fan trays and a rear exhaust. Modelled as a BARE CAGE; the fan trays are real bays and the card openings are cutouts - see gaps.

gaps.note: Cisco publishes no chassis-level power draw for any ASR 9000. Table 14's "Power Dissipation" row says only "Use the Cisco Power Calculator ... to estimate the maximum power distribution", so the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Recorded in provenance as no-chassis-power-figure since the family was modelled; scoped here so a comparison can tell this apart from a figure nobody has looked for
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level maximum and typical draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the Power Calculator is the only answer the vendor will give

gaps.note: THESE BAY DIMENSIONS WERE GROWN TO MEET A COMPONENT AND ARE NOT MEASUREMENTS. Each was set by taking the size of a card the bay accepts, because a fit check reported the bay as too small. On this chassis: 492.10 on 5 bays - a99-sfc3-s, 492.10 long The ten card bays left this list when they took the family standard, 41.4 x 395.7 (see asr9000-card-standard). They had been 42.67 thick and 403.40 long, grown to meet a9k-4hg-flex and a99-rsp-se. The 395.70 is sourced; the 41.4 is a stated thickness chosen as a standard and is NOT measured, so those bays are standardised rather than measured. The danger is specific and it is why they are listed rather than left to look like geometry. A fit check compares a bay to a component and NEITHER of them to the world, so it is satisfied by both being wrong together exactly as easily as by both being right. Every mismatch resolved by moving one side removes the signal without adding any truth, and once resolved nothing will flag it again. These are the entries where that happened, so the record survives the check going quiet. What IS independently grounded and is not in this list: the cage extents, measured off the stencil and confirmed on several chassis by printed slot labels or a card guide rail; the slot pitch; the 395.70 fourth-generation envelope, which is Cisco's own "includes ejector bracket/lever" figure; and the shapesheet sizes for the power modules and fan trays. The ejector arithmetic that explains why a bay legitimately exceeds its cage opening - 355.60 against 395.70, 40.10 mm - is also sourced, and it justifies the SHAPE of these numbers without justifying any particular one of them.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned figure giving the clear opening of any ASR 9000 card cage, which would replace every reconciled figure above with a measured one

gaps.note: The two shelves are still one cutout each, and the module positions are now bays inside them: three AC per tray (`ps0-pm-0` to `ps0-pm-2` and `ps1-pm-0` to `ps1-pm-2`, PWR-6KW-AC-V3, base and `ac`) and four DC per tray (`ps0-dcpm-0` to `ps0-dcpm-3` and `ps1-dcpm-0` to `ps1-dcpm-3`, PWR-4.4KW-DC-V3, `dc` only), M0 leftmost, so six AC or eight DC modules in all. Table 15 ("up to six AC power modules per system, three per tray"), Table 16, Figure 44 (AC, three per tray) and Figure 45 (DC, four per tray) give the counts; the pitch is 139.0 mm for AC and 104.7 mm for DC (see power-shelves). THE AC AND DC BAYS SHARE ONE FOOTPRINT; FILL ONE SET. Each set is `only-in` its own configurations so they never coexist; that mixing AC and DC is not supported (Data Sheet p5; Hardware Installation Guide Table 2) is not enforced by the model. STILL OPEN: the redundancy is stated two ways - the text of the guide's "Cisco ASR 9910 Router Power Modules" says AC 4+2 and DC 5+3, Table 15 says AC N+N and Table 16 says DC N+3. The groups `power-modules-ac` and `power-modules-dc` state the table forms (`n+n`, `n+3`) and declare the text forms as conflicts in their `redundancy-note`, so the text and the tables are still unreconciled; Table 13 gives the 9910's weight "configured with ... one PEM" although it has two trays; Table 21 has no maximum output for the 9910; the module dimensions are measured, not stated (see the two components); the shelf is not drawn empty, so its end hardware and the tray's switch are not drawn; the trays (`A9K-AC-PEM-V3` is the `0/PT0` and `0/PT1` of the guide's `show platform` output, drawn 468.12 mm wide against a 447 mm chassis) are not seated, because no tray-level bay exists; and the rear inlets and feeds are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a figure showing the power shelves empty, the module dimensions from Cisco, and a statement of the redundancy that reconciles the text with the tables

gaps.note: THE BOTTOM FACE IS EMPTY BY VERIFICATION, NOT BY OMISSION, and this is the only chassis in the Cisco family where that is still true. Its seven siblings each earn this face from a rack mounting surface strip dimensioned in their own footprint figure. FOUR ROUTES WERE TRIED HERE AND ALL FOUR FAIL: (1) Figure 12's Top View, read whole at 300 dpi, carries exactly one dimension - 17.600, the width - and no mounting offset. (2) The fraction route needs a scale, and that view has none that reconciles: 17.600 across its short axis makes its long axis 28.04 in, which is 11 percent off Table 13's 31.50 and 10 percent off its own side view's 31.266. (3) The HIG's 4-post mounting figures for this chassis are undimensioned illustrations. (4) Transferring the ASR 9906's 127.0 and 240.0 mm would cross two chassis differing by 313 mm in height, which is the sibling transfer this work has spent the session correcting. Separately and for the whole family: no bottom VIEW of any ASR 9000 chassis exists in the 78-document intake - every figure caption in all 65 PDFs was searched for "Bottom View", "underside" and "bottom of the chassis", returning zero hits. Nothing is drawn and no region names the absence. The face is correctly SIZED, so the 3D box and a rack elevation are the right shape; what is missing is a statement of what is on it, and this chassis holds at capability 2 rather than borrow a number it cannot source.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rail or mounting-flange position for the ASR 9910 from any figure, or a way for a view to declare itself deliberately empty so empty-by-verification can count

devices.description: Cisco ASR 9912 Router - 30 RU, and the first chassis in this family with TWO card cages on one face. Ten vertical line card slots sit above a second cage of nine positions carrying two route processors flanking seven fabric cards, with three power shelves below. The two fan trays are fitted from the REAR, which the guide marks on the figure itself. Modelled as a bare cage with every card position a real bay.

gaps.note: Which line cards run with which fabric card generation, and whether the A99-SFC2 and A99-SFC3 may be fitted together, is NOT ENFORCED: no bay restricts what sits beside it. The Hardware Installation Guide has a 'Migrating from A99-SFC2 to A99-SFC3 Card' section (printed p270) that was not read for a rule. The A99-SFC2's power is scoped like the SFC3's: Table 23 gives 'FC2 Card (ASR 9912)' 105 W at 55 C and the component carries the ASR 9922's 165 W.
gaps.wanted: a rule that pairs a fabric card generation with the line cards and with the other fabric cards.
