Table 14's "Power Dissipation" row says only "Use the Cisco Power Calculator ... to estimate the maximum power distribution", so the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Recorded in provenance as no-chassis-power-figure since the family was modelled; scoped here so a comparison can tell this apart from a figure nobody has looked for
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level maximum and typical draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the Power Calculator is the only answer the vendor will give

gaps.note: NARROWED BY THE ASR 9000 CARD STANDARD, NOT CLOSED. The line card bays here were once grown to meet a component - 42.67 thick to fit a9k-4hg-flex and 403.10 long to fit the 5th-generation envelope - and the RP bays to 46.0 to fit a supervisor data sheet. None of those numbers is used now: all 19 card bays are 41.4 x 395.7 with a 41.4 x 355.6 opening, per asr9000-card-standard in provenance. Two of the three standard figures are sourced: 395.7 is the fourth-generation "includes ejector bracket/lever" envelope, and 355.6 is the Table A-10 plate length, 0.65 mm from the ASR 9010 cage and 1.75 / 2.55 mm under the two cages measured here. THE THICKNESS IS NOT. 41.4 is the figure Cisco states most often, chosen so every card in the family is one envelope; the original-generation cards are stated at 43.7 and the RSP-880 at 46.0, and both are drawn at 41.4 by decision. A fit check between a bay and a card is now satisfied by construction, so it can no longer catch a wrong thickness - which is why this stays open.
gaps.wanted: a caliper reading of an ASR 9000 card thickness (still requested on roc-ops/Portrayal#16), or a dimensioned figure of the clear opening of any ASR 9000 card cage, which would confirm or move 41.4

gaps.note: cisco/a99-sfc3@1 carries power-draw-max-w 340, and that figure is the ASR 9922's. Table 23 of b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf lists the SAME part number twice with different figures scoped by chassis - "A99-SFC3 Card (ASR 9922)" at 320/330/340 W across the three ambients, and a separate ASR 9912 row at a lower number. These are two scopes rather than two answers: the same card draws less in this chassis than in the 9922. A chassis total built from the component here is therefore CONSERVATIVE - it over-counts each of the seven fabric cards - which is the safe direction but is not the right number. The component cannot carry both without a chassis-scoped mechanism, which the library does not have; casa/c100g records the same species of problem for paired modules.
gaps.wanted: a per-chassis power scope on a component contract, or a separate PID for the 9912 variant

gaps.note: Three power shelves are drawn as single openings rather than four module openings each. Figure 23 numbers them M0 to M3 per shelf and Table 15 gives "Version 2 power system: Up to twelve AC power modules per system, four per tray" - so twelve, and the count is not in doubt. The boundaries are: the master draws all three shelves populated, so scanning returns module detail rather than separators. The shelves' vertical extents here are estimated from the band below the RP/FC cage rather than measured off separator rules, which is weaker than everything else in this file and is why they are cutouts and not bays.
gaps.wanted: a figure showing the power shelves empty, or a dimensioned front elevation

gaps.note: THE BOTTOM IS THE ONLY FACE OF THIS CHASSIS WITH NO SOURCE, and it is not a gap in this file's research. There is no bottom view of ANY ASR 9000 chassis anywhere in the 78-document intake: every figure caption in all 65 PDFs was searched for "Bottom View", "underside" and "bottom of the chassis", and the result is zero hits. That is a fact about how Cisco documents a rack chassis rather than about this model - a face that sits on rack rails and is never serviced gets no figure. The face is SIZED correctly from Table 13, so a rack elevation and the 3D box are the right shape; what it lacks is any statement of what is on it. Nothing is invented to fill it, and no region is added naming the absence, because a check passed by annotating that you have nothing is worse than a check failed honestly. THIS HOLDS THE CHASSIS AT CAPABILITY 2. Front, rear, top, left and right all now carry sourced content; the bottom alone does not, and level 3's implementation requires content on all six. The written design asks only that six faces be "present, sized, and mutually consistent", which this file satisfies - the content requirement comes from `_has_content`, which was written for level 1. devices.description: Cisco ASR 9922 Router - 44 RU and the largest of the family. TWENTY vertical line card slots in two cages, one above and one below a central cage of two route processors flanking seven fabric cards, with four fan trays between the cages and four power shelves across the top. The line cards in the LOWER cage, slots 10 to 19, are installed UPSIDE DOWN. Modelled as a bare cage.

gaps.note: Which line cards run with which fabric card generation, and whether the A99-SFC2 and A99-SFC3 may be fitted together, is NOT ENFORCED: no bay restricts what sits beside it. The Hardware Installation Guide has a 'Migrating from A99-SFC2 to A99-SFC3 Card' section (printed p270) that was not read for a rule. Table 23 gives 'FC2 Card (ASR 9922)' 165 W at 55 C, which is the figure the component carries.
gaps.wanted: a rule that pairs a fabric card generation with the line cards and with the other fabric cards.

gaps.note: Cisco publishes no chassis-level power draw for any ASR 9000. Table 14's "Power Dissipation" row says only "Use the Cisco Power Calculator ... to estimate the maximum power distribution", so the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Recorded in provenance as no-chassis-power-figure since the family was modelled; scoped here so a comparison can tell this apart from a figure nobody has looked for
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level maximum and typical draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the Power Calculator is the only answer the vendor will give

gaps.note: THESE BAY DIMENSIONS ARE A MODELLING STANDARD, NOT MEASUREMENTS OF THIS CHASSIS. All 29 card bays are 41.4 x 395.7 with a 355.6 opening (asr9000-card-standard in provenance). Before the standard they were 42.67 x 403.10 on the line card slots, grown to meet a component because a fit check reported the bay as too small, and the RP bays were 46.0 wide for the same reason. That history is why this entry exists: a fit check compares a bay to a component and NEITHER of them to the world, so it is satisfied by both being wrong together as easily as by both being right. What IS grounded: 395.7 is the Cisco "includes ejector bracket/lever" envelope, and a lab measurement of a real RSP-880 agrees; 355.6 is Table A-10, and the measured cages (358.17 and 355.75, kept in provenance) sit within 2.6 mm of it; the slot pitch and cage extents are measured off the stencil. What is NOT: 41.4 is the thickness Cisco states most often, chosen for every card, and the original-generation 1.72 in (43.7) and the RP 46.0 are overridden by it on purpose rather than disproved.
gaps.wanted: a caliper reading of an ASR 9000 card thickness (roc-ops/Portrayal#16), or a dimensioned figure giving the clear opening of any ASR 9000 card cage

gaps.note: The guide states that line cards are installed upside down in slots 10 through 19 of the bottom card cage but right side up in slots 0 through 9 of the top card cage. This is a real property of the chassis and the model cannot currently express it. The bays for 10 to 19 are geometrically identical to 0 to 9 and carry no rotation, because the card is inverted about its own long axis rather than rotated in the plane of the panel - a `rotate: 180` would spin the faceplate end for end, which is a different thing and would put the ejectors at the wrong ends. So a card rendered in slot 15 will show its ports and its part number the same way up as one in slot 5, and on real hardware it would not. Anyone reading port positions off the lower cage should know that.
gaps.wanted: a mirror or flip transform on a bay, distinct from rotation, or a photograph settling exactly which way an inverted card reads

gaps.note: The four fan trays are BAYS now, seating cisco/asr-9922-fan-v3, which is how the ASR 9910 and ASR 9010 already model theirs - a fan tray is a module you pull, not a hole in a plate. That moved the complaint from L39, which could only say the opening had nothing in it, to L33, which says the thing that goes in it is 36.95 mm too wide. Same disagreement, stated where the numbers are. cisco/asr-9922-fan-v3 declares 475.96 mm wide and this chassis's BODY is 447.0, so the component is 29 mm wider than the box it goes in. Compare cisco/asr-9910-fan at 445.2, which sits inside its own 447 mm body correctly. Both are class cooling and one of them is measured against the rack face rather than the body - the stencil records rack-face widths for trays and covers, and 475.96 is within a few millimetres of the 482.6 mm rack face. The openings here are the measured bands and the component is not placed.
gaps.wanted: asr-9922-fan-v3's width re-derived against the body, or confirmation that the fan tray really does span the rack face and needs a negative offset like a mounting ear

gaps.note: THE BOTTOM IS THE ONLY FACE OF THIS CHASSIS WITH NO SOURCE, and it is not a gap in this file's research. There is no bottom view of ANY ASR 9000 chassis anywhere in the 78-document intake: every figure caption in all 65 PDFs was searched for "Bottom View", "underside" and "bottom of the chassis", and the result is zero hits. That is a fact about how Cisco documents a rack chassis rather than about this model - a face that sits on rack rails and is never serviced gets no figure. The face is SIZED correctly from Table 13, so a rack elevation and the 3D box are the right shape; what it lacks is any statement of what is on it. Nothing is invented to fill it, and no region is added naming the absence, because a check passed by annotating that you have nothing is worse than a check failed honestly. THIS HOLDS THE CHASSIS AT CAPABILITY 2. Front, rear, top, left and right all now carry sourced content; the bottom alone does not, and level 3's implementation requires content on all six. The written design asks only that six faces be "present, sized, and mutually consistent", which this file satisfies - the content requirement comes from `_has_content`, which was written for level 1. See docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.
gaps.wanted: a bottom elevation, a photograph of the underside, or a way for a view to declare itself deliberately empty so that empty-by-verification counts where empty-by-omission does not

gaps.note: THE REAL MACHINE HAS THREE LEVELS AND THIS MODEL HAS TWO. Overview and Reference Guide, "Cisco ASR 9922 Router Power Modules": "ASR-9922 supports: Four AC PEMs (power shelves). Version 2 supports four power supplies and version 3 supports three power supplies", and for DC "Four DC PEMs. Each PEM supports up to four power supplies." So the chassis holds four shelves and each shelf holds the supplies; this face draws sixteen supply bays directly, which is 4 x 4 flattened. WHAT THAT COSTS IS FOUR SOURCED PARTS WITH NOWHERE TO GO. cisco/a9k-power-tray is the version 2 shelf, cisco/a9k-ac-pem-v3 and cisco/a9k-dc-pem-v3 are the version 3 shelves - all three drawn off stencil masters at 468.12 x 48.03 - and cisco/a9k-power-shelf-cover is the blank for one. They are unplaced because there is no shelf bay to seat them in, not because nobody knows where they belong: the guide names them by PID against this chassis. THE SIXTEEN BAYS ARE NOT WRONG, and this is why the flattening has stood: a version 2 shelf holds four supplies and 4 x 4 is sixteen, so the supply positions are right for the V2 build. They are wrong for V3, which puts three supplies in a shelf - twelve, not sixteen - and that difference is invisible while the shelves are not there. See roc-ops/Portrayal#262.

The other side carries the console, an RJ-45 and an SFP management port, the USB port, three fan modules and two power supplies. Ports number 1-54 and run DOWN each column, odd on the top row. Ships port-side intake (burgundy modules) or port-side exhaust (blue).

gaps.note: The front figure draws a column of seven rings at the right end beside the QSFP28 pair and a block of nine rings under the BCN, STS and ENV lamps. Callout 1 is "LEDs" and the text names no others, and appendix C lists the BCN, STS and ENV lamps and the port lamps only. They are drawn as marks without a state.
gaps.wanted: What the sixteen rings are, and whether they are lamps.

gaps.note: The guide states no default build among its six supply and airflow combinations. The configuration `ac-350w-port-side-intake` is the base, as for the 9348GC-FX3, so that a plain chassis lists with the family's first supply; it is a choice, not a statement of the guide.
gaps.wanted: Which combination Cisco ships by default.

gaps.note: The guide says the switch "supports a mix of AC and DC power supplies in the same chassis for up to 15 minutes" (PDF p8, printed 2) and its supply list allows "a mix of AC and DC power sources" but not a mix of airflow directions. A configuration seats one supply type in both bays, so a mixed build is not written as a configuration. The bays accept every listed supply, so a user can seat the mix by hand.
gaps.wanted: Whether the 15 minute limit applies to a permanent mixed build.

gaps.note: The installation options (PDF p25, printed 19) also name the N3K-C3064-ACC-KIT, with no contents and no procedure. NXK-ACC-KIT-1RU (appendix D, PDF p69, printed 63) and NXK-ACC-KIT2-2RU (install procedure, PDF p31, printed 25) have procedures and are on main as cisco/nxk-acc-kit-1ru@1 and cisco/nxk-acc-kit2-2ru@1; the third is not modelled.
gaps.wanted: The contents or procedure of the N3K-C3064-ACC-KIT.

A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The guide's overview shows the chassis only in the two flat views and calls out the grounding pad; no side wall is drawn and none can be measured.

A picture of the 350 W PHV and the 440 W DC supplies. The guide's figure shows AC supplies only ("AC power supplies shown"), and labels them with another product's part number. Their faces are the 350 W AC supply's with the inlet changed.
A stated size for the supplies and the fan module. The guide gives "Form factor RSP1" for the 350 W AC and PHV supplies and nothing for the fan.
A cage skin with a bail. The library's SFP cage has one skin and none shows a bail.

gaps.note: The Overview says the switch "will power down due to a fan-policy trigger if fewer than 2 fans are operational", and that with more than one rotor failed it "will issue a warning and power down in 2 minute".
gaps.wanted: Whether the first sentence counts fan modules or rotors. It is read as modules, two of three, so the group says 2+1.

devices.description: 48x 1/10/25G SFP28 and 6x 40/100G QSFP28 1RU data-centre leaf switch on Cisco's Cloud Scale LSE ASIC, running NX-OS or ACI. All fifty-four ports and the BCN, STS and ENV lamps are on the port side; two power supplies, four fan modules, the console, both management ports and the USB are on the other. Ports number 1-54 and run DOWN each column - odd on the top row, even beneath it. Ships port-side intake (burgundy modules) or port-side exhaust (blue). End-of-sale was announced in August 2021.

gaps.wanted: The data sheet (c78-742283, Table 2) gives the width as 17.3 in (43.9 cm); the installation guide's Switch Dimensions table gives 17.5 inches (44.5 cm). Same measure, same scope, different value. 439.4 is carried because a real-unit photograph, corrected for perspective on the SFP cage pitch, closes on it to 0.14%. A ruler across a chassis settles it.

A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The installation guide's two overview figures show a side wall in three-quarter view and call out six screw holes for the rack-mount brackets and two for the grounding lug on it, and the mounting chapter shows the lid the same way; none is flat and none can be measured. Each of the four carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked.

What the two round dark features at the upper left of the port side are. The stencil render and the port-side photograph both show two of them side by side at about 5.4 and 8.9 mm from the left edge, 11.8 mm down, above the BCN lamp, with no legend. The guide's callout for this corner names only BCN, STS and ENV. They are not drawn: a lamp, a button and a hole look the same at this resolution.

What the eight dashes in each QSFP28 band are. Between the up and down port lamps each band carries two rows of four short dark dashes, clear in the stencil and resolved in the photograph. They are in the right place and number to be per-lane breakout lamps for the two cages, and no staged document says so: the guide's LED appendix describes port lamps as triangles and nothing else. They are drawn as marks on the band and carry no state.

The meaning of the row printed under each QSFP28 pair: a square, an up and a down triangle, and a second square. Drawn as printed, from the stencil, and explained nowhere in the guide or the data sheet.

The colours and blink patterns of BCN, STS, ENV and the port lamps. The installation guide's LED appendix gives tables for the fan module and the power supply and one sentence for the chassis; the startup procedure adds only that STS "is green" after initialisation. Searched both staged documents for BCN, ENV and "port LED".

Faces for the other supplies this switch accepts. The guide lists N9K-PUV-1200W (HVAC/ HVDC, white), UCSC-PSU-930WDC (green), UCS-PSU-6332-DC (grey), NXA-PDC-930W-PI and NXA-PDC-930W-PE, and the data sheet adds NXA-PAC-500W-PI and NXA-PAC-500W-PE. The only supply any staged image shows is the 650 W AC one, so that is the only one the bays accept here.

A stated or measured size for the supply and the fan module. No staged document gives either in millimetres; both are read off the stencil render, which is 1.7% narrow on the port side where a photograph can check it.

The vertical step between the two SFP rows. 16.2 mm is the stencil's proportion; the registry's stacked-cage figure is 15.0. A square-on photograph with the full face height in frame would settle it and every other y on this face.

devices.description: 64x 400G QSFP-DD and 2x 10G SFP+ 2RU data-centre switch running NX-OS. The port side carries the QSFP-DD cages in sixteen columns of stacked pairs in an upper and a lower group, the stacked SFP+ pair, the console, an RJ-45 and an SFP management port, the USB port and the BCN, STS and ENV lamps. The other side carries four fan modules and two power supplies stacked at the right. Ports number 1-64 in pairs down each column, odd on the upper cage. Ships port-side intake only (burgundy modules).

devices.description: Cisco Nexus 9504 - the 7 RU, four-line-card modular chassis of the Nexus 9500 family, running NX-OS mode. The FRONT carries four line-card slots LC 1 to LC 4 from top to bottom, two supervisor slots SUP 1 and SUP 2 side by side below them, and below those four power-supply slots PS 1 to PS 4 lying flat in two rows of two either side of a centre panel with the chassis lamps. The REAR carries three fan trays FAN 1 to FAN 3, six fabric-module slots FM 1 to FM 6 behind the fan trays, and two system controllers SC 1 and SC 2 below them. Air enters at the front and leaves at the rear. Each line-card slot holds its blank and accepts the line-card blank and the nine line cards modelled so far (N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X97160YC-EX, N9K-X9732C-FX, N9K-X9716D-GX, N9K-X9736C-EX, N9K-X9732C-EX, N9K-X9736C-FX3, N9K-X9736Q-FX and N9K-X9408PC-CFP2); the other 9500 line cards follow.

gaps.note: The held copy of Cisco's support page "Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches" has no entry for the Nexus 9504, and no end-of-sale notice for the chassis is held, so its sale status is unknown. The 9508's entry on the same page says nothing about it.
gaps.wanted: the Nexus 9504's status on Cisco's support page, or an end-of-sale notice for N9K-C9504

gaps.note: The guide gives a typical and maximum draw per module and no figure for the chassis itself; the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Each line card carries its own typical and maximum draw, so a loaded chassis's total is the sum of its occupants; none is written here.
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the sum of the module table is the answer

gaps.note: Which fabric module each line card goes with, and how many are needed, is listed here and NOT ENFORCED: no bay or card restricts the fabric module it is seated with. The guide's Overview Table 1 (PDF pp8-9, printed 2-3) pairs the cards modelled here with the N9K-C9504-FM-E (this chassis has no FM-E2) and the N9K-C9504-FM-G; the count is the fabric modules required for maximum bandwidth. N9K-X9736C-FX: FM-E 5, FM-G 5. N9K-X97160YC-EX: FM-E 4, FM-G 4. N9K-X9732C-FX: FM-E 4, FM-G 4. N9K-X9716D-GX: FM-G 4 only. N9K-X9736C-EX: FM-E 4, FM-G1 4. N9K-X9732C-EX: FM-E 4, FM-G1 4. N9K-X9736C-FX3: FM-E 5, FM-G1 5. N9K-X9736Q-FX: FM-E 5 only. N9K-X9408PC-CFP2: the plain N9K-C9504-FM, 4, and neither the -E nor the -G1. The guide's notes: FM 5 (slot 25) works only with the N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X9736Q-FX and N9K-X9736C-FX3; the -G fabric modules need the N9K-C9504-FAN2 fan trays and take N9K-C9504-FAN-PWR in empty slots; all fabric modules in the switch must be of one type; and "Do not mix ACI-mode line cards with NX-OS mode line cards in the same switch" (PDF p7, printed 1). "Migrate the switch to 400-Gigabit -GX line cards" (PDF p118, printed 112) says to replace the older fabric modules with "N9K-C9508-FM-G" modules, a sentence copied from the 9508 guide.
gaps.wanted: a restriction in the format between a card and the fabric modules it is seated with

gaps.note: The clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19; callout 14 in the table on PDF p26, printed 20) gives the width of the chassis plus the vertical mounting brackets as 19.2 in (48.8 cm). The ear model has no field for an overall width, so the mounting-bracket region is not sized by it and the front face stays the 444.5 mm chassis width.
gaps.wanted: ear support for an overall width, or a dimensioned front view of the bracket

gaps.note: The guide's rack kit is N9K-C9504-RMK (two bottom-support rails and 20 each of M6, 10-32 and 12-24 screws; PDF p31, printed 25), with the accessory kit N9K-ACC-KIT (printed N9K-C9500-ACK in Appendix C, PDF p139, printed 133). The library has a kit contract for the N9K-C9500-RMK only, and listing it here would break lint while it says `unplaced:`. The 9504's own kit is not modelled and no kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: a follow-up that adds the N9K-C9504-RMK kit and lists the kits on the 9504, 9508 and 9516

gaps.note: The guide's DC supply procedures say "Verify that the Input 1 (IN1) and Input 2 (IN2) LEDs light up on the power supply" (PDF p43, printed 37, and p117, printed 111), but its Power Supply LEDs table lists only OK and FAIL (PDF pp137-138, printed 131-132), and the shared N9K-PDC-3000W-B draws OK and FAIL only. The IN1 and IN2 lamps are not drawn, and the supply is not edited here.
gaps.wanted: the position and colours of the DC supply's IN1 and IN2 lamps, drawn in a new version of the supply

gaps.note: The guide says an even slot (FM 2, FM 4, FM 6) must hold a fabric module to power the fan tray in front of it (PDF p118, printed 112; fan-tray lamps, PDF p135, printed 129, which lists only the FM, FM-E and FM-S), and names a blank only for the odd slots (N9K-C9504-FM-CV) and, for the FM-G, N9K-C9504-FAN-PWR for any empty slot. devices.description: Cisco Nexus 9516 - the 21 RU, sixteen-line-card modular chassis of the Nexus 9500 family, running NX-OS mode. The FRONT carries the chassis lamps across the top, sixteen line-card slots LC 1 to LC 16 from top to bottom, two supervisor slots SUP 1 and SUP 2 side by side below them, and ten power-supply slots PS 1 to PS 10 standing on end along the bottom. The REAR carries three fan trays FAN 1 to FAN 3, six fabric-module slots FM 1 to FM 6 behind the fan trays, and two system controllers SC 1 and SC 2 below them. Air enters at the front and leaves at the rear. Each line-card slot holds its blank and accepts the line-card blank and eight of the nine line cards modelled so far (N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X97160YC-EX, N9K-X9732C-FX, N9K-X9736C-EX, N9K-X9732C-EX, N9K-X9736C-FX3, N9K-X9736Q-FX and N9K-X9408PC-CFP2; the N9K-X9716D-GX is not compatible with this switch); the other 9500 line cards follow.

gaps.note: The guide gives a typical and maximum draw per module and no figure for the chassis itself; the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Each line card carries its own typical and maximum draw, so a loaded chassis's total is the sum of its occupants; none is written here.
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the sum of the module table is the answer

gaps.note: Which fabric module each line card goes with, and how many are needed, is listed here and NOT ENFORCED: no bay or card restricts the fabric module it is seated with. The guide's Overview Table 1 (PDF pp7-8, printed 1-2) pairs the cards modelled here with the N9K-C9516-FM-E and -FM-E2 (this chassis has no -G fabric module); the count is the fabric modules required for maximum bandwidth, read by line order. N9K-X9736C-FX: FM-E 5, FM-E2 5. N9K-X97160YC-EX: FM-E 4, FM-E2 4. N9K-X9732C-FX: FM-E 4, FM-E2 4 plus 1 redundant. N9K-X9736C-EX: FM-E 4, FM-E2 4. N9K-X9732C-EX: FM-E 4, FM-E2 4. N9K-X9736C-FX3: FM-E2 5, and not the FM-E. N9K-X9736Q-FX: FM-E 5, FM-E2 5. N9K-X9408PC-CFP2: the plain N9K-C9516-FM, 4, and neither the -E nor the -E2. The N9K-X9716D-GX appears in no row: it is not compatible with this switch. The guide's notes: FM 5 (slot 25) works only with the N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X9736Q-FX and N9K-X9736C-FX3 (PDF p9, printed 3); a N9516 "having 16 x N9K-X9788TC-FX line cards require a minimum of 3 FM-E2" (the note under the FM-E row, PDF p8, printed 2; that card is not modelled); and "Do not mix ACI-mode line cards with NX-OS mode line cards in the same switch" (PDF p7, printed 1). Its "Migrate the switch to 400-Gigabit -GX line cards" (PDF p113, printed 107) copies the 9508 guide's sentences about N9K-C9508-FM-G modules, for a card the same guide says this switch does not take.
gaps.wanted: a restriction in the format between a card and the fabric modules it is seated with

gaps.note: The 9516's own planning table (PDF p19, printed 13) gives the supervisors 80 W maximum for the N9K-SUP-A, N9K-SUP-A+ and N9K-SUP-B+ and 90 W for the N9K-SUP-B, and the worked example counts 2 x 80 W. The shared supervisor parts carry 90 W maximum (from the 9508 and 9504 tables) and are not edited here. The 9516's seated supervisors therefore read 10 W high each in a power total, except the N9K-SUP-B.
gaps.wanted: a corrected version of the shared supervisors, in its own pull request, or Cisco's single figure

gaps.note: The clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19, with its callout row on the same page) gives the width of the chassis plus the vertical mounting brackets as 19.2 in (48.8 cm). The ear model has no field for an overall width, so the mounting-bracket region is not sized by it and the front face stays the 444.5 mm chassis width.
gaps.wanted: ear support for an overall width, or a dimensioned front view of the bracket

gaps.note: The guide's rack kit is N9K-C9500-RMK (PDF p31, printed 25; contents in Table 5, PDF p135, printed 129), with the accessory kit N9K-ACC-KIT (printed N9K-C9500-ACK in Appendix C). The library has a kit contract for the N9K-C9500-RMK, but listing it here would break lint while it says `unplaced:`, and removing the sentence edits a shared part. No kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: a follow-up that drops the sentence from the shared kit and lists the kits on the 9508, 9504 and 9516

gaps.note: The guide's DC supply procedures say "Verify that the Input 1 (IN1) and Input 2 (IN2) LEDs light up on the power supply" (PDF p45, printed 39, and p112, printed 106), but its Power Supply LEDs table lists only OK and FAIL (PDF p133, printed 127), and the shared N9K-PDC-3000W-B draws OK and FAIL only. The IN1 and IN2 lamps are not drawn, and the supply is not edited here.
gaps.wanted: the position and colours of the DC supply's IN1 and IN2 lamps, drawn in a new version of the supply

gaps.note: The guide says a blank module sits in an empty supervisor or system-controller slot ("remove the blank module that is already in that slot. Unscrew its captive screw", PDF p79, printed 73, and p82, printed 76) and gives it no part number, drawing or dimension. The supervisor and system-controller bays therefore show nothing when empty.
gaps.wanted: the part number and a drawing of the supervisor and system-controller slot blanks

gaps.note: The guide has no flat front or rear elevation, and the NetBox elevations are not held. Every position on both faces is derived from the dimension table and the arrangement in the isometric figures; see the front-stack and rear-stack provenance. No position is measured.
gaps.wanted: a flat front and rear elevation of the chassis with dimensions, or the NetBox elevation images

gaps.note: The bay sizes are the module envelopes of the dimension table, and the positions are the stack derived from them; none is a measurement of the chassis. The fan-tray bays and the fabric-module bays occupy the same area of the rear face because the fabric modules are behind the fan trays.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear view with the fan trays removed

gaps.note: The side and top faces are named in the figures (handles on both sides, mounting bracket, rack rail positions) and no figure dimensions any feature on them, so those faces carry regions with no coordinates. The bottom face is empty: no view of it is published.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side and top view

devices.description: Cisco Network Convergence System 5001, a one-rack-unit router with forty 1/10G SFP+ ports and four 100G QSFP28 ports. The ports, the console and the management jack are on the port (front) side; two power supplies, two fan modules and a USB port are on the other. Ships port-side intake or port-side exhaust and with AC or DC supplies, four builds of one front panel. The guide says nothing about end-of-sale; the status is unknown.

The fan module's power draw, and the chassis' own draw. Appendix C gives supply ratings only.

The air filters, which the guide draws but does not size or number. Port-side intake takes a three-piece filter on the port-side faceplate (Figure 22); port-side exhaust takes clip-on filters on the supply and fan fronts (Figure 23). No part number, size or position is held for either.

devices.description: 24x 10/100/1000 PoE+ RJ-45 (370 W PoE budget) and 2x SFP+ uplink 1RU stackable access switch running LAN Base. The front carries the mode button and switch lamps at the left, two blocks of twelve jacks in two rows at the right of the face, then the USB Type A port, the USB mini-Type B and RJ-45 console ports, the Ethernet management port and the two SFP+ slots. The rear carries the FlexStack module slot with its blank cover, the fan exhaust, the RPS connector and the AC inlet of the built-in supply. Ports number 1-24 and run DOWN each column - odd on the top row, even beneath it. The SFP+ pair follows the copper ports.

gaps.wanted: A flat drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The guide's figures show the lid and one side isometrically (bracket screw holes and slots on the side); none can be measured. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked.

The RPS connector is the part cisco/rps2300-connector@2, drawn open where the photograph puts it. The part draws the plate, its two screw holes, the shroud with its dark top edge, the housing and the two rows of eleven cavities with a contact in each; it draws the cells with their chamfered lower corners and does not draw the slot in the screws, which the photograph shows at about one pixel. The rating strip stays chassis art. The guide says the cover (two Phillips pan-head screws, Figure 1-15) goes on when no RPS is connected.

This model's own rear in colour. The only held rear in colour with the FlexStack slot is the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L, whose plain plate reads #3f4447 and whose fitted module's plain frame reads #3f565d; the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-24TS-L rear (no FlexStack slot, read for colour only) reads #404145. The drawn #404040 is within 7 levels of 255 of each. The guide's own drawing of the rear (Figure 1-10, PDF p19, printed 1-17) is pale grey (#d4d6d8) and shades one finish by the light on each face, so it conflicts with the photographs; the guide gives no housing colour. The rear is drawn charcoal, a stand-in that the owner may accept or replace. The front is not in doubt: the teal edge, charcoal panel and white console surround are what the four 2960-S stencils agree on, and Figure 1-1 draws the same scheme.

Cisco's logo is never drawn (the region `logo-zone` stays). The corner marks 1X, 11X, 2X, 12X and so on at the corners of each block read clearly on the stencil but sit where the jack part's box begins: each mark's inner 0.6 to 1.0 mm lies under the part, so a mark would be half hidden and is not drawn.

The ETSI mounting bracket, printed "700-19781XX" (PDF p34, printed 1-10). Its revision digits are not read, and the guide gives no contents or install steps beyond Figure 1-10, so no kit contract is written.
The numbers of the two SFP+ slots on this 24-port model. The guide says "Module slot numbers are 49 and 50" under the 48-port figure only. They are numbered 25 and 26 here, after the copper ports.
A square-on photograph of this model's front. The only flat face is community art; every position is read from it at 11.3 px per mm.
The Mode button is drawn as plain panel art. No library part is a flush push button of this shape.

The rating label text beside the inlet. The photograph shows another model's label ("100-240V~ 8-4A") and the guide's drawing "12-6A", and this model's row of Table 1-2 reads 5 to 2 A, so none is carried.

A `common/led-arrow-sm` skin whose off fill is the stencil's solid light grey (#808080: 120 px, box (520,96,535,104) of a port arrow and 155 px, box (4660,118,4676,128) of the console arrow; each arrow 2.38 x 2.12 mm) without the dark fill and the #5b6167 edge. The part is on `main` and its skin is not edited, and a lamp's colour in the static drawing is the part's own (a lamp state paints only when a state is set), so each lamp keeps its dark triangle; a light grey triangle of the stencil's size is drawn under it, which leaves a light rim of about 0.25 mm, and the black disc the punched lamp opening drew is covered in the panel's colour. The three lamps by the console and management jacks are arrows too (Figure 1-9, PDF p18, printed 1-16, "Console LEDs": 1 USB console LED, 2 RJ-45 console LED; Table 1-10 gives their colours): they were round dots and are arrow lamps now, down for the USB console LED, right for the RJ-45 console LED (the up skin turned 90 degrees: a lamp, not a connector) and up under the management jack.

A white or silver body for the RJ-45 part. The console jack, the management jack and the 48 jack-block jacks are `std/rj45-ganged@2`, whose only skin paints a near-black body with light grey shoulders. The stencil draws the console and management jacks on a white plate (#efefef, 10086 px of each, boxes (4782,86,4959,226) and (4998,86,5175,226)) round a dark opening, so a plate of that colour and outline (15.6 x 12.34 mm) is drawn under each of the two jacks and the part keeps its own body. On the 48 block jacks the stencil draws charcoal bodies with white shoulders, where the render has near-black bodies with light grey shoulders; left: the part's skin. Request: an `std/rj45` skin with a white body or white shoulders. The latch stays up and the contacts down, as the stencil shows them.

A USB-A skin with a silver interior and the tongue at the left, as the stencil shows. `std/usb-a@1` is placed with `skin: usb2` and rotated 90 degrees, and draws a black opening (#17191c) with a pale tongue (#d5d9de) to the right of the middle of the vertical opening; the stencil draws a silver-grey shell with the tongue at the left. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small at this port to say more. The shell around the part is drawn silver (#7b7b7b).

A mini-B skin with the five contacts in the lower half of the opening. `std/mini-usb@1` draws the flat edge at the top, bevelled corners at the bottom and the five contacts (#7a8087) in the upper half; the stencil has the same flat edge and bevel and the contacts in the lower half. Request: `std/sfp` with the clips, squares, contacts and pull tab in its opening.

The "MGMT" and "BASET" legend right of the management jack. The stencil prints it vertically in yellow (#ffff99, 341 px, box (5190,95,5215,212)): the letters M, G, M, T, then a gap, then B, A, S, E, T, one above the other and upright, each 0.78 mm tall, 10.3 mm in all (it reads "BASET", with no hyphen, at 6x). devices.description: 48x 10/100/1000 RJ-45 and 2x SFP+ uplink 1RU stackable access switch running LAN Base, without PoE. The front carries the mode button and switch lamps at the left, four blocks of twelve jacks in two rows, then the USB Type A port, the USB mini-Type B and RJ-45 console ports, the Ethernet management port and the two SFP+ slots. The rear carries the FlexStack module slot with its blank cover, the fan exhaust, the RPS connector and the AC inlet of the built-in supply. Ports number 1-48 and run DOWN each column - odd on the top row, even beneath it. Slots 49 and 50 are the SFP+ pair.

gaps.wanted: A flat drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The guide's figures show the lid and one side isometrically (bracket screw holes and slots on the side); none can be measured. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked.

The RPS connector is the part cisco/rps2300-connector@2, drawn open where the photograph puts it. The part draws the plate, its two screw holes, the shroud with its dark top edge, the housing and the two rows of eleven cavities with a contact in each; it draws the cells with their chamfered lower corners and does not draw the slot in the screws, which the photograph shows at about one pixel. The rating strip stays chassis art. The guide says the cover (two Phillips pan-head screws, Figure 1-15) goes on when no RPS is connected.

This model's own rear in colour. The only held rear in colour with the FlexStack slot is the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L, whose plain plate reads #3f4447 and whose fitted module's plain frame reads #3f565d; the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-24TS-L rear (no FlexStack slot, read for colour only) reads #404145. The drawn #404040 is within 7 levels of 255 of each. The guide's own drawing of the rear (Figure 1-10, PDF p19, printed 1-17) is pale grey (#d4d6d8) and shades one finish by the light on each face, so it conflicts with the photographs; the guide gives no housing colour. The rear is drawn charcoal, a stand-in that the owner may accept or replace. The front is not in doubt: the teal edge, charcoal panel and white console surround are what the four 2960-S stencils agree on, and Figure 1-1 draws the same scheme.

Cisco's logo is never drawn (the region `logo-zone` stays). The corner marks 1X, 11X, 2X, 12X and so on at the corners of each block read clearly on the stencil but sit where the jack part's box begins: each mark's inner 0.6 to 1.0 mm lies under the part, so a mark would be half hidden and is not drawn.

The ETSI mounting bracket, printed "700-19781XX" (PDF p34, printed 1-10). Its revision digits are not read, and the guide gives no contents or install steps beyond Figure 1-10, so no kit contract is written.

A drawing of this model's own rear. Table 1-1 footnote 1 says it supports FlexStack and Figures 1-10 and 1-11 give the stacking rear a cover, but its serial-number figure (Figure 1-2 of the appendix, PDF p56, printed 1-6) draws no cover. That figure is captioned for models that do not stack too (the 2960S-48TS-S and -24TS-S), so it is not read as this model's own. The fan, RPS connector and inlet read within 3 percent of the PoE rear's positions along the long edge, which is inside the reading of an isometric figure, so they are placed as on the PoE rear, with the slot and its cover.
A square-on photograph of this model's front. The only flat face is community art; every position is read from it at 11.3 px per mm.
The Mode button is drawn as plain panel art. No library part is a flush push button of this shape.
The rating label text beside the inlet. The guide's drawings show "12-6A" and this model's row of Table 1-3 reads 1 to 0.5 A, so no text is carried.

A `common/led-arrow-sm` skin whose off fill is the stencil's solid light grey (#808080: 120 px, box (520,96,535,104) of a port arrow and 155 px, box (4660,118,4676,128) of the console arrow; each arrow 2.38 x 2.12 mm) without the dark fill and the #5b6167 edge. The part is on `main` and its skin is not edited, and a lamp's colour in the static drawing is the part's own (a lamp state paints only when a state is set), so each lamp keeps its dark triangle; a light grey triangle of the stencil's size is drawn under it, which leaves a light rim of about 0.25 mm, and the black disc the punched lamp opening drew is covered in the panel's colour. The three lamps by the console and management jacks are arrows too (Figure 1-9, PDF p18, printed 1-16, "Console LEDs": 1 USB console LED, 2 RJ-45 console LED; Table 1-10 gives their colours): they were round dots and are arrow lamps now, down for the USB console LED, right for the RJ-45 console LED (the up skin turned 90 degrees: a lamp, not a connector) and up under the management jack.

A white or silver body for the RJ-45 part. The console jack, the management jack and the 48 jack-block jacks are `std/rj45-ganged@2`, whose only skin paints a near-black body with light grey shoulders. The stencil draws the console and management jacks on a white plate (#efefef, 10086 px of each, boxes (4782,86,4959,226) and (4998,86,5175,226)) round a dark opening, so a plate of that colour and outline (15.6 x 12.34 mm) is drawn under each of the two jacks and the part keeps its own body. On the 48 block jacks the stencil draws charcoal bodies with white shoulders, where the render has near-black bodies with light grey shoulders; left: the part's skin. Request: an `std/rj45` skin with a white body or white shoulders. The latch stays up and the contacts down, as the stencil shows them.

A USB-A skin with a silver interior and the tongue at the left, as the stencil shows. `std/usb-a@1` is placed with `skin: usb2` and rotated 90 degrees, and draws a black opening (#17191c) with a pale tongue (#d5d9de) to the right of the middle of the vertical opening; the stencil draws a silver-grey shell with the tongue at the left. Neither skin of the part draws a silver interior (`default` draws a blue tongue, `usb2` a white one, in the same place), so the part stays as it is. The only way to bring the tongue to the left with this skin is a 270 degree turn of the placed part, which is a rotation and is the owner's to decide. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small at this port to say more. The shell around the part is drawn silver (#7b7b7b).

A mini-B skin with the five contacts in the lower half of the opening. `std/mini-usb@1` draws the flat edge at the top, bevelled corners at the bottom and the five contacts (#7a8087) in the upper half; the stencil has the same flat edge and bevel and the contacts in the lower half. The stencil is the only source of the contact side: Figure 1-5 (USB Mini-Type B Port, PDF p9, printed 1-7) draws a mini-B port with the bevelled corners at the top and contacts both on its tongue and in a row below it, which does not settle the side for this connector as it is mounted, and Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small. The part's skin is not edited and the connector is not turned: turning it would put the bevel on top, and a rotation after merge is a major version.

A version of the SFP+ cage part with the stencil's silver frame (#cfcfcf, 1423 px of each cage), its two clips on the right side (#bdbdbd with black edges), its two small squares near the top (#707070), its gold contacts at the lower left and its pull tab inside the opening. The part's own skin paints a grey collar (#9aa0a8) round a dark opening and its skin is not edited here. Drawn outside or under the part's box: the silver as the surround the part leaves visible (about 0.5 mm each side), the black projection at each cage's foot (#000000, 861 px, box (4570,427,4652,441)), the silver pull tab (#c1c5cb, 240 px, box (4588,416,4636,421); all but about 0.2 mm of it lies under the part's box and is hidden) and the white numeral tab under each cage (#f2f2f2, 2112 px, box (4570,450,4652,477)) with its numeral in #595959 (70 px, box (4600,456,4624,474)). Not drawn: the clips, the squares and the gold contacts, because they lie inside the cage's own opening and would paint over the part's skin. Request: `std/sfp` with the clips, squares, contacts and pull tab in its opening.

The "MGMT" and "BASET" legend right of the management jack. The stencil prints it vertically in yellow (#ffff99, 341 px, box (5190,95,5215,212)): the letters M, G, M, T, then a gap, then B, A, S, E, T, one above the other and upright, each 0.78 mm tall, 10.3 mm in all (it reads "BASET", with no hyphen, at 6x). A legend 0.78 mm tall is under the 1.5 mm font size the library's legend test asks for, so it is not drawn. Wanted: a photograph or a dimensioned front that gives the legend at a size that reads.

A dimensioned view of this model's rear. The NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L (3.41 px per mm) shows these things that the render does not, each looked at at 4x: the chassis' own diagonal edge at the far right, running from about (422.6, 18) up to (443.7, 1.5) mm with two small steps below it, which is the chassis outline and is not drawn over the face; two small oval tabs above and below the AC inlet, about 9 x 3 mm at (386 to 396, 3 to 6) and (386 to 396, 33 to 36) mm, whose interior (#323637, 110 px, box (1322,12,1344,17)) is 5 levels of 255 from the plate round it (#373b3e, 200 px, box (1360,12,1400,17)), too faint for an outline to be placed, so they are not drawn; faint rectangular outline marks stamped in the rear plate between the module and the fan and beside the RPS plate; a small round hole at the left of the fan, near (149.6, 28.7) mm; a small dark notch in the RPS plate's left edge, near (285 to 288, 25 to 33) mm; and the AC inlet's three pins, which are light grey blocks in the render and dark pockets with a small light mark in the photograph. All are drawn from one model's photograph and none from the guide, whose Figure 1-10 (PDF p19, printed 1-17) is too small to show them.

datasheet.title: CommScope CH3000 Chassis data sheet (2022, 87-10004 RevH)

devices.description: The CH3000 headend optics platform - a 3RU, 19-inch mid-plane chassis for cable headend and hub optics, designed by Aurora Networks (2004), sold under the ARRIS name and now by CommScope / Vistance. Sixteen identical full-depth slots take transmitters, receivers, amplifiers and a power supply from the front; the rear of each slot takes the module's dynamic back plate, which carries its optical and RF connections, or a half-depth passive. A mid-plane between the two carries the 12 VDC bus and the RS-485 management bus.

gaps.note: a front blank is named once: the FA3500 data sheet's ordering note ships "a BP3000 blank face plate" with the FA3524S, for the front of the slot its double-wide back plate leaves empty. No document draws or photographs a BP3000, and no rear blank is named in any of the 164 data sheets held; a rear plate legended BP3001 appears beside a BP-P2 in the CX3003C sheet's photograph and is probably the rear blank, but no document names or describes it.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing of the BP3000 front blank, and the part number of the rear blank

gaps.note: the PS3006D and PS3006N on the HT3580H chassis photograph carry an older face - a 3.5 mm jack legended Serial in place of the micro-USB, and vertical vent slots on the PS3006N - than the PS3006 data sheet's own photographs. The current face is modelled.
gaps.wanted: the revision history of the PS3006 faceplate

gaps.note: the HT3580H data sheet names three back plates for a CA3008 carrier and photographs one, the BD31A8-100-H10F modelled here. The BD31A8-100-H18F (eight BC inputs, no NC) and the BD35M8 mux plates (-ACx and -EEx with three SC/APC, -DCx with six LC/APC, each with nine F-type inputs) are described in text only, so their layouts are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a face-on photograph or drawing of a BD31A8-100-H18F and of a BD35M8

gaps.note: the FA3524S ships with a double-wide BP-F3 back plate (three SC/APC ports for its input and two outputs) that leaves the neighbouring slot empty for cooling, per the FA3500 data sheet's ordering note 2. The BP-F2, BP-F2-AL and BP-F4 are drawn in that sheet; the BP-F3 is not, so an FA3524S can be seated but its back plate is not modelled.
gaps.wanted: a drawing or photograph of the BP-F3

gaps.note: the chassis data sheets state the arrangement - "32 half-depth slots (16 front-loaded and 16 rear-loaded)" and "32 midplane electrical interconnects (16 front and 16 rear)", and the OR3144H sheet says a half-depth module can be plugged in from either side - so a half-depth module seats in a slot's front bay or in its rear bay, where a full-depth module's back plate would go, and that is how the half-depth modules modelled here seat. No photograph held shows one installed, front or rear, to confirm its face against the slot. Not modelled: the DT3550N transmitter, whose data sheet has no face image; the 8- and 10-channel CWDM demultiplexers (NP34D08, NP34D10, OP34D8C, OP34D10C), whose data-sheet photographs are the multiplexer's artwork relabelled - they print "CWDM MUX" where the photographed 5-channel demux prints "CWDM DEMUX", and the OP34D10C sheet's image is labelled OP34M10C; the OP3168P and OP3178P octal PON filters, whose faces are a dense grid of LC adapters with legends the data-sheet photographs do not resolve; the NP31F08S06 RFoG filter, which has no face image; and the 8x8 splitters (NP38S08, OP38S8S), which are two slots wide and only drawn.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a CH3000 with half-depth modules seated, front and rear

gaps.note: several half-depth families are modelled as the one variant their data sheet photographs, and the others would present a different port set: OP33F1x as the single OP33F1S (the dual OP33F1D has six ports); NP35C0x as the NP35C01D03 red/blue split (the family also takes CWDM/DWDM and DWDM-group splits, single or dual, with an optional test port, each legended differently); and OP35F4S as the variant with a -20 dB test port (the test port is optional). Each would need its own photograph.
gaps.wanted: face photographs of the OP33F1D, the other NP35C0x variants and an OP35F4S without a test port

devices.description: 1U one- or two-socket AMD EPYC rack server, 16th generation. Up to ten 2.5 inch front drive bays, or eight with a Smart Flow vent, four 3.5 inch, fourteen or sixteen EDSFF E3.S, or none. Two 60 mm power supplies stand at opposite ends of the rear. gaps.note: RISER 1A'S SLOT 1 SPANS SLOT 2 BY GEOMETRY ALONE. A figure 11-13 bracket fits across the two openings Dell punches, and slot 2 has no connector to lose, so dell/riser-1a-14g@2 lets a two-slot card seat there and the example configuration draws one. Which two-slot cards Dell qualifies in this chassis, in which riser, at what power and with what cooling, was not read: the technical guide this file cites lists slot widths and lengths, and was not searched for GPU support.
gaps.wanted: Dell's GPU support statement for the R740xd - the riser, the slots, and the cards and power it qualifies - which would say whether this span is offered, and whether riser 2 and 3 have one too

gaps.note: dell/riser-divider-plate-14g@1's OUTLINE AND DEPTH ARE MEASURED and its FACE IS NOT. Both bodies come off Dell's service model to the hundredth - face 267.32..278.64 and 297.10..308.42, y 1.81..42.42, 17.61 proud - but what is printed or punched on them has not been established from any figure. Riser 1's equivalent plate carries a five-slot column that appears in no cut of the model at any plane and had to be read off ISM figure 8; whether these two carry the same column, or anything else, was NOT SEARCHED FOR rather than looked for and found absent. The recess drawn for the card clip is drawn because a clip sits in a recess on riser 1, not because this plate was seen to have one.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or ISM figure at usable resolution across face 267..309, which would settle both plates at once - they are the same pressing

gaps.note: WHICH OF THE TWO IS IN FRONT IS ASSERTED, NOT MEASURED. dell/riser-1-top- shelf-14g@1 is 14.68 proud (measured, the chassis shell's front) and dell/riser-1-shroud-14g@1's plate is extruded at 17.76 (an approximation across a whole outline, as that file's depth key says), so the plate drew in front and the shelf read as tucked under the piece it closes the top of. The operator, looking at the render against the hardware, says the shelf is the outermost thing there. It is expressed as a 3.10 `lift` on the composition - the smallest value that clears 17.76 - so both measured depths survive untouched and only the ordering changes. If the plate's width and depth are ever settled properly (see riser-1-shroud-rib-width-unresolved, which is the same piece of missing evidence) this lift should be re-derived rather than kept.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing or a caliper on the hardware giving the riser-1 shroud plate's front and the chassis top shelf's front at the same face x, which is the one measurement that settles the ordering outright

gaps.note: THE MID BAYS ARE NOT NUMBERED HERE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. This device numbers its front drives 0 to 23 and its rear drives 12 to 15 or 24 to 27, in both cases because Dell's own label says so and the numbering was checked against it. NOTHING FOUND SO FAR SAYS WHAT DELL CALLS THE FOUR MID-BAY DRIVES. They are `mid-lff-0..3` and `mid-sff-0..3`, which are positions and not claims: they say "the four slots, left to right" and assert nothing about what the machine prints or what iDRAC reports. Inventing a range that looked like the others - 24 to 27 say - would have been the easy thing and would have been a fabrication of exactly the kind the front and rear numbering was careful to avoid.
gaps.wanted: the mid-drive-tray page of the R740xd installation and service manual, or a photograph of the tray with its silkscreen legible

gaps.note: THE PREVIOUS FORM OF THIS GAP SAID THE CAD POSE WAS EXPLODED. IT IS NOT, AND THE SENTENCE IS KEPT HERE BECAUSE IT IS THE INSTRUCTIVE PART. A reading of R740XD_GPU_Brackets_01-1 was rejected on the grounds that its y extent ran -40 to +24 against an 86.8 mm panel - "not a seated pose". That was a Y-CONVENTION ARTEFACT IN THE READER, not a fact about the model. Calibrated against the rear handle, whose device y is trusted, the convention is face_y = 86.8 - raw_y; it reproduces the handle's low edge at 42.35 to the hundredth and this assembly's own sibling R740XD_Expansioncard_Clip-1.001 at y 1.81..44.81, the figure riser-1-shroud-14g already carried from an independent read. The pose is seated and the 36.9 mm was real all along - a plausibility check that fires on the reader instead of the data rejects good evidence, and it cost a wrong fix at the other end of the part. WHAT THE MODEL ACTUALLY SHOWS, descended to mesh children, is two levels: Body_2_3.002 at 111.70..148.60, 11.06 proud - a wide lower shelf, now drawn - and Body_1_3.005 at 125.00..135.10, 17.71 proud - a narrow rib. WHAT IS STILL OPEN is the rib. riser-1-shroud-14g draws it 120.64..137.26, about 4 mm wider on each side than the body at that depth. The outline came from cad-outline.py cutting at the panel plane, which returns the SILHOUETTE of everything the plane crosses rather than one body, so it cannot settle a single body's width. Re-cutting it would move the slot column and the clip recess, both photo-measured off ISM figure 8 and both currently agreeing with the render, so it is recorded rather than guessed. RE-READ WHEN THE STRIP UNDER RISER 1 WAS RETIRED, and still open. The same model was cut across face y 66.24..68.05 under the riser, and nothing there stands in front of the rear sheet (Body_8_6, z 708.88 at most, behind fillers whose fronts reach 718.03). That settles the band below the plate and says nothing new about the rib above it.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the riser-1 shroud, or a clean section of R740XD_GPU_Brackets_01-1 above the shelf, to settle the raised rib's width independently of the panel-plane silhouette

gaps.note: THE NUMBER CAME FROM A DESCRIPTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. std/vga@1 stands 6.73 proud because that is what a D-sub does when its flange bolts through sheet metal, and on this machine's front the connector is on the control panel board, which sits back from the bezel - so only a little of it emerges. The operator, looking at the hardware, put that at "a millimetre and a half"; `inset: 5.23` is 6.73 less 1.50 and is therefore an estimate dressed as two decimal places. IT IS THE SETBACK THAT IS UNKNOWN, not the connector. The 6.73 is TE 114-40010's mating dimension and stays; what nobody here has measured is how far behind the faceplate the board sits. A caliper on the hardware, or any drawing that dimensions the control panel board against the front bezel, replaces one number and nothing else. THE REAR D-SUBS ARE NOT AFFECTED. They bolt through the rear panel in the ordinary way and carry no inset.
gaps.wanted: the control panel board's setback from the front bezel, measured

gaps.note: TWO NUMBERS, ONE APPEARANCE EACH, AND NEITHER CORROBORATED. This device seats both supplies at y 46.20, and the only other place that number appears is a comment on riser 2's plate saying the plate was cut back to "face 46.20 - the power supply's top edge", which cites this seating rather than a source. psu-1100w-ac-14g's provenance used to argue the module top was y 45.0, read off R740 ISM figure 9 - but it argued that in the same breath as a height of 41.8, and the height has since been measured off Dell's own service model at 39.1. A position argued from a reading whose companion number is disproven is not evidence for the position. THE CAD CANNOT ANSWER IT. glb-parts.py states the rule it enforces: sizes survive a pose and positions do not, and this scene draws the supply with its withdrawal handle swung open for a removal procedure. The body measures cleanly at 86.3 x 39.1 x 195.5 and its face y lands nowhere near either candidate. AN ATTEMPT TO RE-READ FIGURE 9 FAILED GATE 1 AT 13.18%, against a provenance that claims 0.26% for the same figure - so the failure is in the panel detection, not in the figure, and nothing may be taken off it until somebody finds the body's true top and bottom edges in that raster. The seating is left where it is rather than moved on a measurement that did not pass its own gate. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the body edges in ISM figure 9 identified by hand rather than by ink-density, which turns the 13.18% back into the 0.26% the figure is capable of and makes the fraction readable. 1.2 mm is worth one careful pass, because riser 2's plate is cut to this number.
gaps.wanted: the supply's top edge on the rear face, from a figure that has passed Gate 1

gaps.note: Dell's model carries riser 1 (three-slot, measured here to the tenth) and the low-profile riser 2C. It carries no full-height riser 2 and no riser 3. Their bodies - the PCB and the slot connectors in `body.boxes` on dell/riser-2a/2d/2e/2f-14g and dell/riser-3a/3b-14g - are riser 1's, stood at their own bays' outer edges, and riser 3's PCB is cut to end at the supply cage it stands on.
gaps.wanted: A model or a photograph of riser 2A and riser 3 seated, which would put both PCBs where they are.

gaps.note: ISM figures 17 and 18 number five fronts - 24, 16 and 8 x 2.5 inch at bays 0-23, 0-15 and 0-7, and 12 and 8 x 3.5 inch at 0-11 and 0-7. TWO OF THE FIVE ARE NOW DRAWN. `front` is the 24 x 2.5 inch; `front-lff-12` is the 12 x 3.5 inch, the one that mattered, because it is the front the rears numbered 12-15 and 12-13 belong to. It is a variant view with `face: front`, bound by the `lff12-` configurations, and its grid was measured off dellr740xd-12x35.webp at Gate 1 0.07% - the same backplane opening the 24 SFF bays divide, 428.832 / 4 = 107.208 against a measured period of 107.216. THE 16 AND 8 x 2.5 INCH AND THE 8 x 3.5 INCH ARE STILL NOT MODELLED, and no figure for them has been measured.
gaps.wanted: the remaining three fronts as further `face: front` variants, each with a configuration to bind it.

gaps.note: DELL ENUMERATES THEM. ISM table 28, "Supported backplane options for PowerEdge R740XD systems", lists front, mid and rear together - ten rows, and the coupling falls straight out: 2.5in x24 no rear 2.5in x24 + 2.5in x4 mid + 2.5in x4 rear 2.5in x24 (20 SAS/SATA + 4 NVMe) no rear 3.5in x12 no rear 3.5in x12 + 3.5in x4 mid + 3.5in x2 rear 3.5in x12 + 3.5in x4 mid + 2.5in x4 rear 3.5in x12 + 3.5in x2 rear 3.5in x12 + 2.5in x4 rear 2.5in x24 NVMe no rear 3.5in x12 Hybrid with NVMe U.2 no rear The 24-bay front takes ONE rear, the 4 x 2.5 inch, which figure 19 numbers 24-27. The 12-bay front takes either, and figure 19 numbers both from 12. This device carries the 24-bay front, which is why its rear reads 24-27. THE ARITHMETIC GOT THERE FIRST AND IS NOW REDUNDANT. Bays numbered 12-15 imply eleven bays this model does not have; that is how the error was found. Table 28 is how it is now SOURCED, and a guess agreeing with a document afterwards is worth more than either alone. THE RISER SIDE IS TABLE 25, and its discriminator is riser 2 rather than riser 3. Rear storage is offered in riser configurations 0, 1 and 2 and no others: 1 and 2 fit a one-slot low-profile riser 2 (2B or 2C, slot 4 only), while configuration 3 fits a three-slot 2A (slots 4, 5, 6) and has NO rear storage despite fitting no riser 3 at all. It is riser 2's full-height section that occupies the bay the rear cage needs. This device's configurations already encode exactly that - rear storage only with rc0, rc1 and rc2 - and row 3 is `rc3-1a2a`, added when the riser 3 opening and rear storage bay 3 turned out to be the SAME HOLE, closed by two different blanks depending on which configuration you picked. RE-READ AND STILL OPEN: that change touched which bay closes an opening, not the front-to-rear coupling this gap is about. Re-read again when riser 1's brackets moved 1 mm and slot 2 lost its numeral on 1A - both are ink and geometry inside one bay, and neither reaches across faces. Re-read a third time when riser 1's plate grew to meet the slot strip and the shroud: the bay's own box moved, and still nothing crossed a face. A fourth time when riser 2's three slots were aligned and its plate cut back to the full-height pair. That one surfaced a NEW question but not a new gap of this kind: a bay's occupant is drawn after the panel, so a card cannot be shown "only through its cutout" without a part drawn after the bays to mask it. Recorded where it belongs, on the riser 2 slot 6 cutout, rather than widened into this one. A fifth time when the screw tab was split out of the frame so it could draw in front of riser 2's bracket tails. That is a draw-order fact about one bay, not a coupling between faces. A sixth time when riser 3 became bay 1 reflected - mirrored brackets, a two-slot plate and its own slot strip. Handedness is a fact about one bay's own metal and reaches no further than that. A seventh time when riser 3 slid 9.525 right to sit over the power supply's edge. Moving one bay along its own face changes nothing about which front it can be sold with. An eighth time when two "rivet" pairs beside the divider turned out to be card retention clips. A misread of what is on the rear, corrected on the rear, and silent about any front. A ninth time when those rivets came back, scoped: they are what the riser cage mounts to and they show when drives are fitted instead. That one is a rear configuration telling two rear drawings apart, which is the mechanism this gap says is MISSING between faces - and still is. A tenth time when the C20 supply became its own part. A second occupant for an existing bay, on the same face, coupled to nothing at the front. TWO SOURCES DISAGREE AND ARE LEFT DISAGREEING. The system information label draws FIVE fronts - 24, 16 and 8 x 2.5 inch, 12 and 8 x 3.5 inch - where table 28 lists TWO front backplanes. Whether the 16- and 8-bay fronts are different chassis or one backplane drawn part-populated, nothing held here says. AND TABLE 28 HAS A MID DRIVE TRAY in three of its ten rows. This device models no mid bay at all, which is a whole third drive location missing rather than a detail. RE-READ WHEN `ru: 2` WAS STATED (#734), and all nine gaps still open. The chassis had no rack units at all, so its DCIM exports called a 2U server 1U; stating them moves nothing on any face and settles none of these.
gaps.wanted: NOW DEMONSTRABLE RATHER THAN HYPOTHETICAL. `rear-2-lff` draws a correct 2 x 3.5 inch rear on a 24 x 2.5 inch front, and ISM table 28 lists no such machine - every row carrying that rear has a 12-bay front. The mismatch even forced an id: the figure prints 12 and 13, which are already two of this chassis's front bays, so the rear ones had to be rear-drive-12 and rear-drive-13. An id clash is what this gap looks like from the inside. RE-READ AFTER THE REAR BAYS WERE SEPARATED, and still open. The rear half of this is now expressible: the chassis structure across bays 2 and 3 is its own always-present part, and what each bay holds - drives, PCIe, a blank - varies independently of the other. That was the piece `only-in` could not reach while one 287 mm component owned both bays. WHAT REMAINS IS THE FRONT. The 24 x 2.5 inch and 12 x 3.5 inch fronts are different panels, not different occupancy, and until the second is drawn nothing exercises the face-binding that would couple it to a rear. A way for a configuration to constrain more than one view at once. Today `only-in` scopes a bay to a configuration and every view chooses independently, so nothing stops a consumer selecting a 24-bay front and a rear numbered 12-15 - a machine that cannot be bought. The library needs either configurations that span views, or a declared incompatibility between them; and this device needs its 12 x 3.5 inch front modelled before either can be exercised, which is the same gap `rear-2-lff` already stands on.

datasheet.title: Dell PowerEdge R760 Spec Sheet

devices.description: 2U two-socket rack server, 16th generation - up to 24 x 2.5 inch front drive bays (or sixteen with the Smart Flow vent, eight, twelve 3.5 inch, or sixteen EDSFF E3.S), two 86 mm power supplies at opposite ends of the rear, up to eight PCIe slots on four risers, an OCP NIC 3.0 slot, a rear BOSS-N1 boot module and optional rear drives

gaps.note: the ISM refers to the 'Dell Enterprise Systems Rail Sizing and Rack Compatibility Matrix' for rail types and ranges and names none; the technical guide (chapter 10) names the families only - ReadyRails II sliding rails (the B21 4-post kit), Stab-in/Drop-in sliding rails, static rails, the cable management arm and the strain relief bar - with no part number or depth. Neither document is a kit's source, so no `kits` or `ears.positions` are written.
gaps.wanted: Dell's Enterprise Systems Rail Sizing and Rack Compatibility Matrix for the R760

gaps.note: riser configuration 11 (ISM table 153; technical guide table 14: R1 paddle + R2A + R3B + R4 paddle) carries paddle cards at risers 1 and 4 that 'do not have a physical PCIe slot'. No figure shows their rear, and what plates the empty positions is unknown, so the configuration is not built. The paddle risers are ISM figures 22 and 32 of the technical guide.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or ISM figure of the paddle-card build

gaps.note: THE DOCUMENTS' CONFIGURATION LISTS DIFFER. The technical guide's table 14 lists 0, 1, 2, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 5-1, 5-2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10-1, 10-2, 11 and 12; the ISM's table 153 lists 1 to 12 and adds 13 (R2A alone, one x16 low-profile slot) and omits 10-2, which its table 167 gives. The ISM governs: configurations 0 to 10 and 13 are built. Configuration 12 is R1Q + R2A + R4Q in both documents - exactly configuration 7's risers - and has no table of its own in the ISM, so it is not built apart from 7. The -2 builds (3-2, 5-2 and 10-2) differ from the -1 builds in the full-length risers 1P FL, 3A FL and 4P FL and double-width cards, not in anything the rear shows, so each shares its -1 build's rear.
gaps.wanted: Dell's statement of how configuration 12 differs from 7, if it does

gaps.note: ISM table 153 lists riser R4R with slot 7 only (Gen5 x16 on processors 1 and 2 in configuration 4-1; Gen5 x8 on processor 1 in 9 and 10-1), while table 18 gives it a slot 7 (x8+x8 SNAPI) and a slot 8 (x8, Gen5) and figure 222 labels two slots. dell/riser-4r-2u-16g@1 carries both slots, the configuration tables' x16 and processor 1 for slot 7; its own provenance has the detail.
gaps.wanted: Dell's per-slot statement for riser 4R

gaps.note: ISM tables 88 to 90 name the rear drive slots (0 and 1; 24 and 25; 0 to 3; 24 to 27) by front configuration but not which physical drive is which. The upper and left drives are taken as the lower numbers, an estimate, and the 24 to 27 numbering of the SAS/SATA builds is not modelled.
gaps.wanted: the rear drive module's service label (ISM 'rear drive module' figures) with the slot numbers

gaps.note: the Direct Liquid Cooling build (ISM figure 11) shows risers 3 and 4 with one slot each (slots 5 and 7), coolant tubes leaving beside PSU 2 through a rear I/O board with no VGA, and a processor cooling module in place of the heatsinks (figure 17). The rear I/O board for it is dell/rear-io-board-dlc-16g@1, which was drawn for the R660 and is a 1U face; the 2U build's tubes, grommets and slot cages are not drawn, and its top view is not.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on rear figure of the DLC build and a top view of its cold plates

gaps.note: the 1800 W (C15), 2800 W (C21), 3200 W 277 Vac / HVDC, 1400 W 277 Vac / HVDC and 1100 W -48 V DC supplies of ISM tables 15 and 16 are not modelled: no figure shows their faces, and the library holds no C22 inlet, 277 V inlet or DC terminal block that matches them (dell/dc-terminal-6ryj9 is a 14G part). The bays accept the 86 mm 2400 W supply and the 60 mm 700, 800, 1100 and 1400 W ones. The 2400 W face is itself READ from a figure that does not label it: see dell/psu-2400w-ac-86mm@1.
gaps.wanted: rear photographs of the other supplies

gaps.note: the E3.S service label (ISM figure 27) lists an 8-drive configuration (c: slot 1 only), and the ISM and technical guide draw only the two 16-drive fronts; no figure shows the 8-drive front's other four slots, so it is not built.
gaps.wanted: a front figure of the 8 x E3.S build

gaps.note: no photograph or ISM figure of the R760's front with its bezel on, straight on, is held; see dell/bezel-2u-16g@1, whose size, openings, button and lock are measured from Dell's R760 service model (r760.glb) and checked against the ISM's isometric figure 37. What the model cannot give is how the drawn face looks in light: the colour is this drawing's.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of an R760 front with the security bezel

gaps.note: Dell's R760 service model (r760.glb, `PEr760_ FrontBezel_-1.001` `Body_1_33.001`) has the bezel 19.7 deep, cad z 0.3..19.9 against the drive carriers' front face at z 19.5 (20.2 with the LED-number bodies); the ISM's table 10 gives 35.84 mm ear to front with the bezel and 22.0 without, which is 13.84 off the drives' face (the R660's table gives the same 13.84). Same measure, different value by 5.9 mm. The part's `depth` is the model's 19.7; its 3D plate is drawn to the ISM's 13.84, the figure Dell's own table allows to stand out of the chassis.
gaps.wanted: a side view or dimensioned drawing of the R760 with the bezel fitted

gaps.note: the risers' cage plates are drawn 1.0 proud of the rear wall (the ISM's table 10, PDF page 34, puts nothing but the supplies' handles past it), and a seated card's bracket flange stands past the wall with the part of the riser that covers it. The flange is the bracket's own 9.4 return flange (std/pcie-bracket-lp@1 and -fh@2, PCIe CEM 5.0 figures 11-9 and 11-5) and the cover is each cage's `flange-cover` node, a column the flange ends sit behind, as the R740xd draws its riser shroud. A rear bay cannot recess its occupant, so the flange stands 9.4 past the wall in a configuration with a card seated, and a filler's bracket gets the cover as a card's does. The ISM gives no depth for either. Dell's R760 service model poses its risers out of the chassis (its supply runs to 861.8 and its risers end at 754 to 770, short of the wall), so the cover's 19.3 is carried from the R660's model, where riser 2A's covers reach 19.3 and 19.8 past the wall: an estimate here, not a measurement.
gaps.wanted: a side view or dimensioned drawing of a seated bracket under its riser's cover, or the model with its risers seated

gaps.note: Dell's R760 service model (r760.glb, `PEr760_ Airshroud_ Assembly-1.001`) has the shroud 434.4 x 187.7 (plan y 241.1..428.8); the ISM's figure 15 (callout 4 on the embedded top view, 1.965 px/mm, about 2%) read 430.0 x 166.0 at y 250.0..416.0 - 21.7 shorter. The model is drawn; the figure's reading is kept in the part's provenance. The shroud's wings (ISM figure 15) are not in the model's bounding box and are kept from the figure.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned top view of the R760's air shroud

gaps.note: Dell's R760 service model (r760.glb, `PEr760_ SystemCover_-1.001` and the drive backplane cover) has the lids 444.0 wide, 5.0 over the body's 434.0 on each side; the ISM's table 10 gives 434.0 between the ears (Xb) and the R660's model has its lid at 433.4 against the same 434.0. The model's 444.0 is recorded in the parts' provenance and the lids are DRAWN AT THE BODY'S 434.0 (plan x 0.0): the lint (L150) does not let a part reach past the face without a stated `chassis.overhang`, and a lid's side flanges are not an overhang of the rack face. The depths, 571.6 and 54.0, are the model's.
gaps.wanted: the R760's cover as a dimensioned drawing, or its folded edges' width

gaps.note: Dell's R760 service model (r760.glb, `CoolingFan Prefab (n)`) has each fan module 64.0 x 58.2 on the plan and 68.0 tall; the ISM's figure 15 top view read 64.0 x 61.0 (about 2%), 2.8 longer. The width is the model's 63.8 pitch: each module's 64.0 box includes a handle that overlaps its neighbour's by 0.2, which the lint (an overlap of bays) does not allow.
gaps.wanted: Dell's fan module dimensions

gaps.note: The ISM's figure 15 shows one plate from the backplane to the chassis front (read 129.1 deep, plan y 593.6..722.7) and the part was first drawn as the 'drive backplane cover'. Dell's R760 service model (r760.glb) has the removable `PEr760_ DriveBackPlane_ Cover_ Assembly-1.001` only 54.0 deep (plan y 543.4..597.4) over the backplane, and the plate in front of it is the shell's own fixed cage top, `PEr760_ Shell_ Top_-1.001` (z 12.0..141.8, 129.8 deep, plan y 594.3..724.1 - the figure's reading to 1 mm). The cover part is the model's 54.0; the cage top is drawn as the top view's own panel decor, so the look is the figure's.
gaps.wanted: confirmation that the ISM's 'drive backplane cover' is the 54 mm piece

gaps.note: The model gives the rear row's x: r760.glb has the LOM card (`R760_ LOM`), OCP board and rear I/O board (`R760_ RearIO`) at cad x -128.0, -61.5 and 22.0 (the left edges), exactly 8.0 left of the R660's model (`PE_R660_LOM card_Assemby` -120.0, OCP -53.5, `PEr760_RearIOBoard_Assembly` 30.0) - and the R760's chassis centre line is 8.0 left of the R660's (-8.0 against 0.0, from the two models' system covers, and the R760's shell and supplies). The ISM's figure 10 reads the row 2 to 7 mm right of them (see the rear-row provenance); that is not supported by the model and is within the figure's 1.5 mm and perspective, so it is recorded here, not applied. The OCP board is 12.0 shallower in the R760's model (120.6 against 132.6); the R660's OCP parts are used.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear view of the R760's rear row

The device draws the model's, which is one build; the half-length support bar and bottom cover (ISM figures 39 and 40, 12) are not drawn.

devices.description: Eaton Rack PDU G4, managed, 0U: an 1829 mm black aluminium strip that hangs on two mounting buttons in a rack's vertical channel and hands a three-phase 208 V delta feed (a fixed 10 ft cord with a CS8365C plug, 40 A, 14.4 kW) on to 42 outlets - 24 IEC C13 and 18 Eaton C39 - in six colour-coded sections of seven, A to F.
