datasheet.title: Tripp Lite PDU12IEC spec sheet (1.9-3.8kW Single-Phase 120-240V Basic PDU, 14 Outlets, C20 16A Input, 1U Rack-Mount)

devices.description: Eaton Tripp Lite series basic PDU, 1U horizontal: a black metal box about 434 mm wide and 108 mm deep. It hands a single-phase 100 to 240 V feed, 16 A, on to 14 unswitched outlets in one load bank. On the front, four IEC C13 outlets. On the rear are an IEC C20 inlet for a cord the user supplies, a grounding stud and two 16 A push-to-reset breakers. Also on the rear, two IEC C19 outlets and eight IEC C13 outlets. No switch, no meter, no network interface. The housing is reversible and its two mounting ears are separate brackets, which also turn for 0U, wall and under-counter mounting.

gaps.note: three printed widths and none is the body. Spec sheet, Unit Dimensions: 19.000 in, and 44,5 cm in the row below (19 in is 482.6 mm). Owner manual, Specifications: 17 1/4 in beside 445 mm (17.25 in is 438.2 mm). The straight-on rear photograph, scaled on the stated outlet pitch, measures the body at 434.2, and the same photograph scaled on the stated C19 spacing at 436.0. 434.2 is drawn. 19 in is read as over the ears; 17 1/4 in may be the body with the ear brackets screwed to its sides, which no source says.
gaps.wanted: a dimensional drawing of the PDU12IEC, or a rule across the body of a unit.

gaps.note: spec sheet, Unit Dimensions: 4.250 in, and 10,8 cm. Owner manual, Specifications: 3 3/4 in beside 108 mm (3.75 in is 95 mm). 108 is used: it is printed in millimetres by both documents and in inches by one. No top or side view exists to measure.
gaps.wanted: a dimensional drawing, or a rule along the side of a unit.

gaps.note: the only photograph of the front is taken from above and to one side. A projective reading puts the four outlets in the middle of the face, where they are drawn, but gives their pitch as 29.2 against the stated 28.75 and the ear span as 471 against a rack face of 482.6, so it does not close and the block may be 3 mm either way. The mark at the left end is placed by the same reading.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front, or a dimensional drawing.

gaps.note: the owner manual lists two 16 A resettable breakers and the spec sheet one load bank of 14 outlets; neither says what each breaker protects. Searched: the spec sheet, the Eaton SKU export, the owner manual text and its three figures, and both 230 V brochures. No outlet states the breaker it runs through.
gaps.wanted: a wiring diagram of the PDU12IEC, or the word of the maker on what each breaker protects.

gaps.note: the owner manual (Connecting the PDU) fits a cable clamp bracket round the inlet with two chassis screws and a third that tightens on the cord. It is in no photograph, and the one figure of it is perspective line art with no dimension. It is not drawn, and neither are its screw holes.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear with the clamp fitted, with a scale.

gaps.note: a pale round mark 5.8 mm across sits below the grounding stud. The 3000 px photograph shows a faint figure on it and does not resolve it; the white lettering of the front mark, at the same scale in its own photograph, resolves cleanly, so the limit is the mark's contrast and not the camera. It is drawn as a plain disc.
gaps.wanted: a close photograph of the grounding stud and the mark below it.

gaps.note: the PDU also mounts vertically beside the rails, on a wall and under a counter with its ears turned a quarter, and takes the PDUSIDEBRKT toolless side bracket, sold separately. Only the 1U rack form is modelled. A 0U use needs the ear's own dimensions and where its screws sit on the body sides, which no source gives, and a part for the PDUSIDEBRKT, of which no source is held.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the mounting ear and of the PDUSIDEBRKT, and a straight-on photograph of a side.

gaps.note: the owner manual gives the nominal voltage as 100V to 240V; the spec sheet lists input voltages from 120 to 240 and titles the unit 120-240V. Both are carried in `input-ac`. THE CURRENT AT THE LOW END DIFFERS TOO: the owner manual gives the output as 15 amps for 100V to 120V and 16 amps for 208 to 240V; the spec sheet gives 16A total at every voltage, with 1.92kW at 120V, which is 16 A. `input-current-a` is 16, the figure both give at 240 V.
gaps.wanted: the rating label of a unit.

gaps.note: no source shows the top, the bottom or a side straight on. The front and three-quarter photographs see a plain lid at a steep angle and one ear side on; the owner manual figures are perspective line art. The four faces are sized from the chassis and drawn bare.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of the top, the bottom and one side, with a scale.

devices.description: Eaton Tripp Lite series switched PDU, 1U horizontal: a 444 mm black metal box that hands a single-phase 120 V feed (a fixed 12 ft cord ending in a NEMA L5-20P, 16 A continuous, 1.92 kW) on to 16 individually switched NEMA 5-15/20R outlets, eight on the front and eight on the rear, each with a lamp. On the front, a pre-installed WEBCARDLX network card (10/100 Ethernet, a micro-USB console, USB-A for sensors, a reset button and a status lamp) and a two-digit meter of the total load in amps; on the rear, the cord, a ground screw and a DE-9 port reserved for the factory. Bolt-on mounting brackets, reversible for front- or rear-facing installation.

gaps.note: THE SOURCE IS CLEAR AND THE LIBRARY IS SHORT: BK at 4x shows the rear's Config. Port as a female DE-9 (nine socket holes in a grey insert), and the vendor is not silent about it. What is missing is a part - the library has only the male half (std/db9@1, composed by common/db9-receptacle@1) - so it is drawn male. Its place, size and standoffs are right; its gender is not. The reason is the nearest the vocabulary has; none names a missing library part.
gaps.wanted: a female DE-9 receptacle part (sockets in a flush insert, as std/vga@1 draws its own), to replace the male one here.

gaps.note: the owner's manual says each outlet LED illuminates when its outlet is live and names no colour; the spec sheet says "power on-off status" and names none; every photograph shows the lamps unlit. The `on` state is declared with no colour, so the kit paints its default lit colour.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a powered PDUMH20NET, or Tripp Lite's word on the lamp colour.

gaps.note: the sides carry the tapped holes the mounting brackets screw to (three #6-32 screws a bracket, at more than one depth: owner's manual 1-1 and Features), and _C and DT02 show some of them, but only at a steep angle; no straight view or drawing of a side exists, so the sides are drawn bare.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of a side with a scale, or a dimensioned drawing.

gaps.note: no source shows the top or the bottom straight on: the spec sheet and the owner's manual have no such view, _C and DT02 see the lid only at a steep angle (a plain black lid with small screws near its edges), and nothing shows the underside. Both faces are drawn bare.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of the top and the bottom with a scale.

gaps.note: no photograph or drawing shows the PDU with the WEBCARDLX out, so the slot's hole is not measured. The bay states the plate's main body, 67.3 by 29.1, as its opening: the largest hole the plate covers, an upper bound.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the PDU with the card removed, or the slot's dimensions from Tripp Lite.

gaps.note: no held source dimensions the WEBCARDLX behind its faceplate or the slot it sits in (the WEBCARDLX manual gives none), so the card states no depth.
gaps.wanted: the WEBCARDLX's dimensions from Tripp Lite.

devices.description: 48x 10G SFP+ plus 6x 100G QSFP28 1RU aggregation router, sold as the AGR110, Broadcom BCM88370 Qumran-MX with a BCM15K TCAM, Intel Xeon D-1518, ONIE-preloaded. All ports on the front, numbered from 0 with even ports on the top row; two 650 W AC or -48 VDC PSUs and six 5+1 fan trays from the rear, front-to-back airflow in every ordering code published.

gaps.wanted: agr110-datasheet/doc.md:109 states 438.4 x 501.9 x 44 mm and agr110-qsg's hardware specification states 435 x 515 x 43.84 mm. All three axes differ and the depth differs by 13 mm, which is not rounding. The datasheet is modelled, for the reasons in provenance - the sibling's datasheet states the same triple independently, 438.4 is the body width this vendor's 1RU line uses, and the figure's own aspect prefers it - but the quick-start is not wrong for being outvoted, and the same conflict stands unresolved on agr130, which shares that quick-start. A tape measure on a real unit settles it in one minute.

The six QSFP28 ports are numbered 48 to 53 here on the strength of the vendor's zero-based scheme, not on a reading. No figure held resolves their numerals: the quick-start's section 6 zoom crops that end of the faceplate away and the datasheet render prints the band under its own callout highlighting. Which column is the lower number, and whether the separate bottom row continues the sequence or precedes it, need a straight-on photograph of the right-hand end of the front panel.

The bezel between the upper QSFP block's two rows carries FOUR marks per column where the SFP+ bezel carries two. That is either two lamps per port or a four-lane column serving one of them, and 9.1 px/mm cannot separate those. One lamp per port is drawn; the other two marks per column are not. A photograph of one QSFP shell at better than 9 px/mm settles it.

The quick-start's section 6 zoom draws PS0, PS1, Diag, Fan and Loc as text INSIDE a light rectangle, which reads as a legend printed on the lens rather than beside it - unlike Reset, two centimetres away on the same band, which is plain white text on the chassis. It is drawn here as a lamp with its legend over it. Whether the real part prints on the lens or beside it is a bench photograph.

The management jack's link and activity lamps are BELOW THE CONSOLE PORT, not in the jack - a reader with better photographs than this corpus holds sees them there, which is why the jack is modelled on the bare std/rj45-ganged@2 rather than the lamped Ethernet cell. They are now placed, straddling the `Mgmt` label at 409.30 and 420.20 mm, from a reader looking at the hardware. The datasheet render does not resolve them on its own - the band carries marks at 407.88, 409.63 and 410.73 mm and a brighter one at 30.1 to 31.0, and at 9.1 px/mm nothing separates a lamp from a legend among them - so the positions bracket the label rather than landing on a measured mark. What remains open is only the exact offset either side.

Twenty-six lamps on this face carry a legend printed on the lens: the twenty-four lane lamps their lane number 0 to 3, and the two management lamps `LNK` and `ACT` - legible in a close photograph of the hardware. It is not drawn, and the obstacle is the model rather than the evidence: the renderer paints a placement over its own silkscreen, so ink at a lamp's centre is invisible and L21 says so, and there is nowhere else for it to go - the port numerals sit 0.8 mm above the lamp row and the label bar directly below it. The same is true of the five system-LED legends at the other end of the face. What would fix both is a way for a lamp to carry a legend on its own lens, which is a component or renderer question and not this device's to answer.

The two grounding points do not look alike. Callout 7 points to a single round opening at the lower left, about 7.9 mm; the right-hand end carries a light plate with two holes one above the other, 424.7 to 436.7 mm, which matches the quick-start's "One grounding lug, 2 M5 screws" kit. devices.description: 12 x 400G QSFP-DD, 24 x 100G QSFP28 and 4 x 10G SFP+ 2RU aggregation router on a Broadcom Jericho2c+ with an Intel Xeon D Ice Lake and an OpenBMC service processor, sold as the AGR560 and stamped AS9947-36XKB. ALL PORTS ARE ON THE FRONT, NUMBERED FROM ZERO, in stacked pairs legended `N (up) (down) N+1`: the SFP+ quad at the left, three QSFP28 blocks of two columns by four rows, then three QSFP-DD blocks of two columns by two rows. THE SFP+ QUAD AND QSFP28 PORTS 0-3 ARE A COMBO PAIR and the panel says so with one continuous pink band across both. The out-of-band cluster carries MGMT, CONSOLE and ToD RJ-45s, 1PPS and 10 MHz coaxial timing jacks, a vertical USB 3.0 Type-A, a reset pinhole and FIVE system lamps - five, not the AIS800 family's six, because this machine has no ALRM. Two 2000 W Lite-On supplies and four fan trays are on the rear. It shares the AIS800-64D and AIS800-64O's 440 x 649.2 x 87 shell and their fan tray, and NOTHING ELSE: its supplies are half the power on different connectors and its port wall is a different machine entirely.

gaps.note: The grounding plate carries two screws for one lug, but no held document dimensions them: the rear photograph reads the two holes 16.0 to 16.3 apart, and the guide kit is one grounding lug and 2 screws, unsized. A two-hole lug lands on a pair host built at a lug pattern and a screw size, so both screws stay nominal and unsized, at the reading, until a source gives the size and the spacing.
gaps.wanted: the grounding screw size and hole spacing, or the part number of the kit lug

WHAT THE DC TERMINAL ACTUALLY IS. The datasheet names it and stops - "DC Inlet: Amphenol Terminal" - with no series, no part number and no drawing, and the guide adds only the wire gauge. So edgecore/agr560-psu-dc@1's block is drawn to the guide's rear elevation at 5.08 px/mm and nothing else: a 18.7 x 31.6 frame with two 10.7 wells on a 13.7 mm stud pitch. THE COUNT IS SAFE - the ordering table's cable is "6AWG PSU to 2 x Ring Terminal", so two studs is stated, not deduced - but the well diameter and the stud size are a round half of a measurement taken to about a quarter of a millimetre. An Amphenol catalogue drawing would replace them outright. The same gap is open on edgecore/ais800-64-psu-dc@1 for the same vendor's six-stud block.

A PHOTOGRAPH THAT SHOWS A SUPPLY LATCH ON THIS MACHINE AT ALL, in either build. Both supplies are drawn with a neutral #3d3d3f tab, and that is a measurement rather than a default: counted over the whole supply column of the datasheet's rear photograph at 9.56 px/mm, the AC build carries 133 red pixels - a 1.2 mm streak that is the red wire behind the fan guard - against the fan trays' 106,257 on the same face, and the module's right margin reads a flat dark grey. The guide's rear elevation, which is the only document that draws the DC build, cannot help: it renders both supplies with ZERO saturated pixels while colouring the trays' handles on the same drawing. SO THE HONEST READING IS THAT THE TAB IS NOT A COLOURED PART, and the AIS800 family's airflow-colour convention is not evidence here - that family ships in two airflows and photographs both, and this machine ships front-to-back only. Both components were first written with that family's red and green and both were corrected. What would close this is one clear photograph of either supply's right edge out of the chassis.

THE PERFORATION PATTERNS, PITCHES AND EXTENTS, which are the softest numbers on this face. The panel carries two styles - honeycomb along the top and bottom of the port wall and at the right-hand corners, and short slots above and below each QSFP-DD block - and both were found by clustering a local-variance map of a textured photograph rather than measured. gaps.wanted: Which end of the rear the fan trays number from. The chassis silkscreens a mark on the rail beside each bay, and at the source's real resolution it cannot be read: the rear elevation is embedded in the PDF at 1.83 px/mm, where a 2 mm numeral is 3.7 pixels. Upscaling the page render to 600 dpi makes the marks LOOK legible - a "7" appeared convincingly on the rail at the right-hand end - but the same detector run on the embedded image at native resolution shows there is nothing there to read, so it was discarded. A dimensioned drawing of the bracket on the chassis side, or a statement of the setback, settles it.

WHICH OF A QSFP28 PORT'S THREE LAMPS SHOWS WHICH BREAKOUT LANE. The quick start guide's Status LEDs panel states colours by SPEED and not by lamp - 'QSFP28 Port LEDs: Blue - 100G, Yellow - 40G, Cyan - 2 x 50G, Magenta - 4 x 25G, Green - 4 x 10G' - and never says how many lamps a port has, let alone what each one means. The face draws three, and a 4 x 25G or 4 x 10G breakout has four lanes, so the obvious one-lamp-per-lane reading cannot be right. The lamps carry the library's off/on default and no legend is invented. A LED table naming the lamps, or a bench photograph of one port under a known breakout, settles it.

WHICH FABRIC PORT EACH LAMP OF A BLOCK'S TWO-LAMP COLUMN BELONGS TO. Each fabric block carries a vertical pair of lamps at its inboard edge, one pair per row, serving that row's two ports. Nothing in either document says which lamp is which port, and at 2.27 px/mm the lamps are 2 px across with no legend beside them. Each pair is therefore drawn `for:` BOTH of its ports rather than one lamp being assigned to each, because assigning them would be a guess wearing a measurement's clothes. A photograph of the fabric block at 5+ px/mm settles it.

THE OUTLINE OF EACH AIR-FILTER COVER AND THE POSITIONS OF ITS CAPTIVE SCREWS. The filter is a real field-replaceable assembly - the guide gives it a three-step procedure: loosen the cover's captive screws, swap the old filter for a new one, then refit the cover and tighten the captive screws - and the Overview numbers it as item 3. What is NOT resolvable is where one cover ends and the next begins: the mesh WINDOWS measure cleanly but a cover's own edge is a shadow line a pixel wide, and the screw heads sit in the top strip where the filter media's texture defeats every threshold that finds a smooth disc elsewhere on the face. The filters are therefore drawn as the vent fields they present rather than as seated FRU components. A mechanical drawing, or a straight-on photograph of the front at 5+ px/mm, would settle it.

A MEASURED FACE OF THE 48 VDC SUPPLY. edgecore/cor550-psu-dc@1 is drawn from the quick start's angled illustration of the supply's terminal end (Connect Power, page 3), which has no scale: the envelope is borrowed from the AC supply, every position on the face is read from the illustration and estimated, the colours are sampled from a render, and which way the wires leave the two screws is not stated. THE TWO DOCUMENTS STATE DIFFERENT INPUT RANGES: the quick start prints '-48 - -60 VDC, 40 A max' and the data sheet '40 to 72 VDC', recorded on the part and not resolved. The AC supply's face is dark and the illustration's is light grey, also not resolved, and the diamond mark on the illustration is not drawn. No photograph or 3D model of this supply is held. A rear photograph or an elevation of the DC build, and the supply's ordering code, settle all of it.

THE VENDOR ORDERING CODES FOR THE AC SUPPLY AND THE FAN TRAY. The datasheet's ordering table lists chassis SKUs only (carried on the configurations), and the guide's replacement procedures name no part. Both FRUs are therefore named for the chassis, which library/components/README.md allows only because no model number exists to use instead. If a COR550 ordering table lands, both parts should be renamed to their FRUs and this device should take the major that costs - edgecore/fan-2u-1x1sn@1 is the precedent for both the rename and its price.

WHETHER EACH TRAY CARRIES ONE FAN OR TWO IN SERIES. The datasheet says '4+1 redundant, hot-swappable fan modules' and 'Fans: Hot-Swappable 4+1 redundant fans' and never gives a fan count. One rotor is visible through each tray's mesh. This vendor's other 2RU trays carry two in series and say so in words - edgecore/fan-2u-1x1sn@1's datasheets print '4 hot-swappable fan modules (2 fans per module), 8 fans total' - but nothing of the kind is printed for this machine, so the bay count is five and the fan count is not claimed.

The CSR200's shell with no fans in it: passively cooled behind a honeycombed faceplate, needing at least 1 m/s of external airflow, with no FAN lamp and no BITS port. Ports number from 1; all timing, management and power connections are on the front, and the two DC supplies are fixed.

gaps.wanted: A figure or drawing of this faceplate that can carry a dimension. THE ONE THAT EXISTS CANNOT, AND THE PROOF IS A STANDARD IT CONTRADICTS. Its SFP cage pitch reads 14.7-14.75 measured two ways - across the four cage bores and across the shell walls between them - against the SFF-8432 figure of 14.25 that the registry carries and that the CSR200's figure reproduces at 14.22. Its RJ-45 cell pitch reads 14.4 against a registry 13.97, the same three percent high. And its DC terminal blocks read about eleven percent SMALL against the sibling's. Nothing reconciles those with one scale. THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATION WAS TESTED AND FAILED. A perspective render would taper: panel height sampled along x is flat on both faces, 425-419 px across the CSR200 and 425-430 across this one, and the CSR180's absolute feature POSITIONS line up with the CSR200's to a millimetre or two over the whole 440. What is wrong is local scale, not geometry - the art is honeycomb dark-on-dark at low contrast and repeated careful reads of one feature wobble by 0.5 to 1 mm where the CSR200's repeat to 0.05. WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT: every standard part takes its size from the registry - SFP 14.25, RJ-45 13.97, USB-A, SMB - and the figure supplies POSITIONS and COUNTS only. That is the division docs/modelling-a-device.md already draws for ganged pitch, applied to the whole face. The two non-standard parts, common/dc-terminal-24@1 and edgecore/filter-slot-5915-16x@1, are sized from edge POSITIONS for the same reason, and each says so.

Which of the four stacked RJ-45 positions is which. The face carries two 1x2 stacks - four jacks - and the datasheet names only THREE non-traffic RJ-45s: the console (callout 4), the ToD/1PPS (callout 10) and the management port (callout 11). There is no BITS port on this model, which is the CSR200's callout 4 and the reason that device has twelve callouts and this one eleven. The silkscreen under the left stack is a single lamp and legend where the CSR200 has two, and it is not legible at 9.63 px/mm. So the fourth position is either blank or something unlisted, and the three that are named are placed here in the CSR200's order - console top right, management bottom right, ToD/1PPS bottom left - which is an INFERENCE FROM THE SIBLING, not a reading.

A figure of any face but the front. Neither document draws one. The side panels matter more here than on any other device in this family: this box is cooled by air someone else moves across it.

An LED table. Neither document has one, and unlike the CSR200's quick start this one does not even state that the PSU lamps come up green. Five system lamps are legible - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, ALARM - and every lamp here carries `off` and one green `on`, borrowed from edgecore/csr200 where a quick-start sentence supports it. Which of each optical port's two bezel lamps is link and which is activity - the same silence as on the CSR200, from the same vendor, about the same bezel.

Whether an air filter is sold for this model at all. gaps.wanted: A figure of any face but the front. Neither document draws one, and on THIS device that is a smaller hole than usual: the datasheet's own "All ports and PSUs are accessible at the front" means the rear carries no user-facing hardware but the grounding point. The quick start's step 3 pictures that point twice, once on the rear panel and once on the side, as a two-hole lug with the earth symbol beside it - enough to know it exists on both, not enough to place either, so neither is placed. The SIDE panels carry the intake and exhaust on a side-to-side box and are drawn nowhere.

What the component at 239.8-260.8 is. It is 21.0 x 3.8 in the silkscreen band between the SFP+ numerals and the AS7315-27X model text, and it reads as eight cells with the outer two red and the inner six pale. Neither document mentions it: the fourteen callouts do not point at it, the specification lists no display and no switches, and the quick start's step 5 figure - which is otherwise the most legible thing in the corpus - is cropped just short of it. A stack-identity display would fit the device, which stacks two units and has a STACK-SYNC and a STACK-CTRL port; so would a DIP bank. It is drawn as a plain bezel with no claim about which, and `common/seven-segment-dual@1` was NOT used, because reaching for a part whose name asserts what the thing is would be the guess this gap exists to avoid.

The module letters on the two-high QSFP28 block at 322.5-342.5. What the six lamps in the stacking block's bezel do. Their positions are measured - 325.1, 327.5, 330.4, 334.3, 337.5, 339.7 - and two of the six are visibly larger than the other four, which usually means a port lamp beside a set of lane lamps. Nothing in either document says. Four lane lamps and two port lamps is the shape the AGR110 uses, but that is a pattern, not a reading, so the six are placed and left unassigned.

How many fans are in the tray. The datasheet says "Hot swappable redundant fan modules" - plural, inside one tray - and the FRU table sells exactly one "Fan Tray Spare Part", FAN-1U-1x1J-S. The elevation shows a closed tray with no grille and no seams. So the tray is one module with no nested bays and the redundancy is stated in attrs without a count, rather than a number being invented to fill the field.

A wattage for either supply. The datasheet's "Power Capacity: 300 W (maximum)" and the quick start's "193 Watts maximum" are both the CHASSIS's - one a capacity, one a consumption - and neither is an output rating for a module. Input ranges are published for both variants and are carried on the parts; the output is not, so L27 stands on both and the hole stays visible.

An LED table. Neither document has one. Six system lamps are named on the faceplate - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, FAN, ALRM - and the quick start states one colour for four of them: "After power on, the PSU1/PSU2, DIAG, ALRM, and FAN LEDs should all be on green." Each fan module's left-hand strip carries its bay number and a small airflow arrow - the rear elevation shows 1 to 6 at 17.1, 67.5, 117.3, 167.7, 217.0 and 267.4 - and they are printed ON THE MODULE, not on the chassis behind it. edgecore/csr440-fan@1 is one contract used six times, so it cannot carry six digits; drawing them as chassis silkscreen puts them under the module that covers them, which L21 correctly reports as printing on nothing. A configuration's `skins:` maps one skin per COMPONENT rather than per bay, so the fix is either six near-identical contracts or a per-bay skin the format does not have. What is behind the perforated blank that fills the rear from 313.0 to the panel edge. devices.description: 48x 10G SFP+ and 6x 100G QSFP28 data-centre leaf switch, sold as the DCS201, Broadcom Trident 3 with an Intel Atom C3558. All fifty-four ports, both management jacks, the console and the USB are on the FRONT; two supplies and five fan trays are on the rear. Ports number 1-54 and run DOWN each column - odd on the top row, even beneath it. Ships front-to-back and back-to-front, and the two builds differ in the colour of every handle and latch.

gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Neither staged document draws any of them flat: the quick start's mounting figures show the lid and one side in three-quarter view while brackets are being screwed on, which is enough to see that nothing is printed or punched there and not enough to model. Each of the four therefore carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md - EMPTY BY VERIFICATION, not by omission. L45 STILL WARNS ABOUT THEM AND THIS GAP IS WHAT ANSWERS IT, because that rule exempts a view a gap names rather than one carrying an `empty:` sentence. Worth saying plainly: the CSR440 clears the same rule only because an unrelated chassis-weight gap happens to scope all six views, which the rule's own comment calls over-exemption; this one names the four faces because they are what it is about. IT DOES NOT COST THE DEVICE ITS CAPABILITY LEVEL. I asserted that it did and was wrong - the grader reads six views here and the 3D build is whole. A mechanical drawing would still improve these four faces from honest blanks to drawn ones.

What the last two white legend boxes say. The label strip carries six bracketed groups of four - the breakout lane legend, one bracket per QSFP28 port, and they read 49 to 54 in order - and then TWO MORE boxes of the same size and pitch at 362.98 and 369.01 mm, under the numerals for ports 47 and 48, belonging to no bracket. At 5 px/mm their contents are not legible and no table in either document accounts for a seventh pair. They are left undrawn rather than guessed, and this gap is the record that they exist and where.

An orthographic elevation, or a mechanical drawing. The only full-panel figures this corpus holds are perspective renders: the top cover is drawn above the face and the face tapers 0.9% from its top edge to its bottom. That costs the vertical axis entirely - every y on both faces is constructed from the registry's row pitch and the family's idiom rather than read - and it leaves the horizontal axis with a 0.84% residual against the stated width, which is why the panel is 442.5 because two documents say so rather than because the drawing shows it. A flat elevation would settle the row positions, the label-strip height and the width residual in one pass.

A way to print a numeral and its direction arrow together. Each of the 48 SFP+ numerals is drawn on the metal as a digit followed by a small up or down triangle - "1 up", "2 down" - naming which row of the column the port is in. Block expansion generates the digit and has no vocabulary for the glyph beside it, and hand-writing 48 marks to add it would take the whole block out of generation for one triangle each. The digits are generated and the arrows are not; the row is unambiguous from the numeral's own side of the column centre, which is measured and correct.

The positions of the four QSFP28 breakout windows. The guide's Port LEDs table says each QSFP28 port shows "1-4 LEDs Amber (25G breakout)" and "1-4 LEDs Purple (10G breakout)", so there are four windows per cage, and the art at 5 px/mm shows a row of dots inside each cage's bezel band without resolving where they sit. One lamp per port is drawn, carrying all four vocabularies as states - the same choice edgecore/as5912-54x made on the same cluster. Four windows at invented positions would be a claim about metal this figure cannot support.

An elevation of the DC supply. The rear elevation draws the AC pair; the DC variant appears only in the small three-quarter "DC Power" figure on page 2, which shows the green three-pole pluggable terminal and the bail handle clearly enough to know what is there and not clearly enough to measure it. edgecore/dcs201-psu-dc@1 therefore borrows its face size from the AC supply, which fills the same bay, and marks every element position estimated.

What each fan module prints beside its airflow diamond. Every one of the five carries a diamond mark in its upper right corner, and at 5 px/mm the characters next to it are not legible. The convention across this vendor is an F2B or B2F legend that follows the airflow variant, and that is what is drawn, from common/fan-module@1's field of the same name; the DCS201's own art neither confirms nor contradicts it.

A way to say that HALF THIS WALL FEEDS MORE POWER THAN THE OTHER HALF. The datasheet states the upper sixteen ports support up to 24 W per transceiver and the lower sixteen do not - a real, per-row electrical fact that decides which optics can go where. The model has no vocabulary for a per-row power budget on a port group: `attrs` on the group would claim it for all thirty-two, and splitting the block in two to carry two attrs would misdraw a wall whose sixteen columns are one continuous pitch. What the sixth system LED window is. The System LEDs enlargement shows six windows in a 3x2 grid and the guide's own list names five - Loc, Diag, PS1, PS2, Fan. The bottom-right window carries no legend in any figure or table in either document. It is drawn, given an id and named in a region as an unidentified indicator rather than omitted, because a mark on the metal that the model leaves out is worse than one it labels as unknown.

A reading of how far the two end vent fields actually reach. Their PATTERN was corrected here - they were drawn as honeycomb and the elevation plainly shows rectangular slots - but their extents, 1.20 to 4.80 and 433.00 to 437.20, are still the ones set by the pass that got the pattern wrong, and nothing in this change re-measures them. A darkness threshold on this elevation returns the seams between slots rather than the field, and scoring columns by vertical periodicity - which should find a slot field and ignore a seam - returns four columns at 5.31-6.10 mm on the left, which is not where the field visibly is. At 5.08 px/mm a 1.8 mm slot column is nine pixels and the anti-aliasing defeats both instruments. This device's photographs are 1.105 px/mm and are worse. THE ONE-BASED AS7816-64X-O SERIES IS NOT MODELLED, and the documents disagree about which numbering they draw. The ordering table sells two base models whose only stated difference is that the O prints ports, fans and supplies from one and the OZ from zero; it also offers the 48 V DC supply only in the O series. The datasheet's elevations are the O, the guide's front enlargement is the OZ, and the guide's rear prints fans 4..1 beside a front that says PSU 0. This device is the OZ and prints fans 3..0 on the datasheet's word. THE DC BUILDS EXIST ONLY IN THE O SERIES (dc-f2b and dc-b2f, 7816-64X-O-48V-F-R and -B-R), so the DC builds wear the OZ labels as a declared stand-in, not a second device. The O series prints ports 1 to 64, fans 4 to 1 and, read on the data sheet's rear photograph (page 2), PSU 2 at the left supply and PSU 1 at the right; this device prints PSU 1 at the left, PSU 0 at the right and fans 3 to 0. Views per configuration (front-o and rear-o, as arista/7010tx-48's rear-dc does) would draw the O labels, and the AC O-series SKUs would then want configurations too; that is the owner's decision. A photograph of a real OZ rear settles its fan legend.

WHERE THE LAMPS OF THE TWO INNER PORT ROWS ARE. The vendor states four lamps per port and the outer rows show them, four round lamps above the top row and below the bottom. The inner rows - the upper cages' bottom row and the lower cages' top row - show none in either document: the band between the cages carries only the numeral and arrow legend, and each cage's white belly strip carries six round features per column, which is neither four nor eight and matches the cage's own light-pipe and vent pattern. 32 ports' lamps are therefore not drawn. A close photograph of one column of a real unit would settle it.

WHETHER THE BACK-TO-FRONT BUILD'S FAN HANDLES ARE A DIFFERENT COLOUR. Both airflows are orderable (-F and -B) and every rear either document draws has red handles. devices.description: 64 x 400G QSFP56-DD 2RU spine switch on a Broadcom Tomahawk 4 with an Intel Xeon D-1548, sold as the DCS520 and stamped AS9736-64D. ALL PORTS ARE ON THE FRONT in TWO BANKS OF SIXTEEN STACKED COLUMNS, numbered from 1, with the legend `N (up)(down) N+1` printed BETWEEN the two cages of each column. Two 10G SFP+ management cages at the left are ports 65 and 66; five system lamps stand in a column above them; an RJ-45 console, an RJ-45 management jack and a USB Type-A stack at the right. SIXTEEN OF THE SIXTY-FOUR ARE 24 W PORTS and the datasheet names them one by one. It is the fourth device on the 440 x 649.2 x 87 shell and THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR WHOSE REAR PUTS A SUPPLY AT EACH END with the four fan trays between them - the AIS800-64D, the AIS800-64O and the AGR560 all stack two supplies at the left. One shell, two rear architectures.

gaps.wanted: A FAN FRU NUMBER FOR THIS MODEL. `edgecore/dcs520-fan@1` was written as its own part and it very probably is not one: the three other devices on this shell all seat a tray whose FRU number `FAN-2U-1x1SN-F` is printed in all three of their datasheets, and this machine's trays sit on a mean pitch of 85.58 against their uniform 85.71 - thirteen hundredths of a millimetre - with the same honeycomb, the same angled red bar with two pairs of slots and a central button, and the same corner lamp. THE MEASUREMENTS ARGUE FOR ONE PART MEASURED TWICE, NOT FOR TWO PARTS. The three gaps here run 85.54, 85.64 and 85.55, a spread of a tenth of a millimetre, where the other three chassis repeat 85.71 with no spread at all; and this face is 80.1 x 83.5 `measured` against the shared tray's 81.6 x 81.2 `photo-measured`, a disagreement of 1.5 x 2.3 mm. Irregular spacing and a face that misses by more than the pitch does are what pixel-measuring a drawing produces beside a dimensioned source. Two rulers, not two trays. NEITHER DCS520 DOCUMENT PRINTS A FAN PART NUMBER, so the argument that settled the other three is unavailable, and the drawings cannot settle it either: scaled to a common size and normalised, 46% of pixels differ by more than a standard deviation, but that is this guide drawing the tray bright with the rotor showing through the mesh against the AIS800 guides drawing it dark. A test that cannot tell a different part from different lighting decides nothing. One FRU list closes this. If it names `FAN-2U-1x1SN-F`, delete this component and seat the shared one.

WHERE THE RESET BUTTON IS. The datasheet's System and Port LEDs section ends with the bare line "Reset button", and neither document draws one that can be found: the guide's Overview callouts run 1-9 and none of them is a button, its System/Port LEDs enlargements cover the left end, the port field and the right cluster without showing one, and at 8.87 px/mm the datasheet photograph resolves the pinholes it does have - the grounding screws, the PSU status lamps - without any obvious candidate on the port side. So the device is modelled without it rather than with one guessed onto a plausible patch of metal. An enlargement of either end of the front panel closes this.

THE EXACT OFFSET OF THE LANE-LAMP STRIP FROM ITS CAGE. Four lamps per port is stated outright by the guide, the strip is visible on the posts in its enlargements, and its HEIGHT measures well - about 10.85 mm over four windows on a 3.5 mm pitch, which is why `common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1` fits it. Its x is the soft number: the enlargement puts the strip about 10.7 mm right of the column centre while the post it stands in spans 9.05 to 14.8, and the panel's two scales - 11.94 px/mm read across the columns against 10.53 read down the rows - do not agree well enough to choose inside that range. 11.0 is used and the render was checked against the reference at matched scale. A dimensioned faceplate drawing, or one enlargement with a known length in it, closes it.

devices.description: 24 x 1G RJ-45 PoE plus 6 x 1G/10G SFP+ 1RU access switch, sold as the EPS112 and stamped AS4625-30P. ALL TWENTY-FOUR COPPER PORTS ARE PoE and they are two classes, not one: ports 1-16 carry 802.3at/af up to 30 W and ports 17-24 carry 802.3bt Type 4 up to 90 W, with the 90 W eight marked out on the panel by an ORANGE BAND above and below them. The RJ-45s sit in twelve columns of two, ganged six and six; the SFP+ uplinks are three stacked pairs numbered 25-30 into the same sequence. A stacked management/console RJ-45 pair, a full-size Type A USB 3.0 storage port, a Reset button and six status lamps finish the face. TWO HOT-SWAPPABLE 600 W AC SUPPLIES AND THREE FIXED FANS on the rear - the fans are not FRUs. It is the third member of the 440 x 350.3 x 44 shell that edgecore/eps121 and edgecore/eps122 share, and the only one with its own quick start guide.

gaps.note: The grounding plate carries two screws for one lug, but no held document dimensions them: the rear photograph and the datasheet rear read the two screws 16.2 to 16.7 apart, and neither document names the screw or a lug. A two-hole lug lands on a pair host built at a lug pattern and a screw size, so both screws stay nominal and unsized, at the reading, until a source gives the size and the spacing.
gaps.wanted: the grounding screw size and hole spacing, or the part number of the kit lug

WHICH HEIGHT THE 440 x 350.3 x 44 SHELL IS ACTUALLY BUILT TO. Four instruments on this model's own documents - two of them exact to four decimal places - put its drawings at 440 x 44.00. Six instruments on the EPS121/EPS122's shared guide put THEIR drawings at 440 x 44.45 and fail at 44.0. Both families publish "44" in their specification tables and both are sold as the same 1RU chassis with the same rack kit. One of the two document sets is drawn a percent tall, and nothing in either settles which. A dimensioned mechanical drawing, or a ruler on one real machine, closes it for all three devices at once.

WHETHER THE THREE FIXED FANS ARE ROUND OR RECTANGULAR. This model's guide and its rear photograph both draw round openings 25.1 across; the EPS121/EPS122 guide draws 25.5 x 15.9 rectangles at the same pitch on the same shell - 47.87 here against 47.8 there, and 25.1 across against 25.5. The width and the pitch agree to within half a millimetre and the SHAPE does not, which is what a single fan drawn two ways looks like. Whichever is wrong, one of the two parts is drawing a guard nobody makes. A rear photograph of an AS4625-54T or a mechanical drawing of the fan wall closes it.

HOW FAR THE SUPPLY'S RELEASE TAB STANDS PROUD OF ITS OWN FACE. The two modules' silver faces are identical to a hundredth of a millimetre - 73.23 wide, 40.24 tall, both of them - but their red tabs run to 2.5 mm past module 1's right edge and 7.5 mm past module 2's. One part cannot do both, and at 2.80 px/mm the difference is seven pixels, which is more than the noise. The tab is drawn inside the face here. A square-on photograph of a supply out of the chassis closes it.

devices.description: 54-port Gigabit PoE access switch, 1RU, sold as the EPS202 and stamped AS4630-54PE. 48 x 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ-45 in twenty-four columns of two, ganged six and six and six and six, ALL of them delivering up to 90 W under IEEE 802.3at and 802.3bt - one rate and one PoE class, which is what separates it from both its shell-mates. Four 10G/25G SFP28 uplinks and two 100G QSFP28 stacking ports numbered 49-52 and 53-54 into the same sequence. TWO HOT-SWAPPABLE 1200 W AC SUPPLIES AND THREE HOT-SWAPPABLE FAN TRAYS on the rear, front-to-back only. IT IS 32 mm SHALLOWER THAN ITS TWO SIBLINGS - 438 x 442 x 43.7 against 438 x 474 x 44 - and its FACE is theirs.

gaps.wanted: A SQUARE-ON ELEVATION OF THIS MACHINE. All four of its datasheet figures read between -3.7% and -6.2% on aspect, and fitting its front elevation's twenty-four RJ-45 columns gives a straight-line rms of 0.695 mm with a quadratic implying the local pitch grows 3.8% across the row. Its guide has no square-on elevation at all. EVERY FRONT-FACE FIGURE IN THIS FILE IS CARRIED FROM `edgecore/eps203`, on the evidence that the two guides' port enlargements place the apertures at the same pixels. One orthographic drawing of this face would turn the whole file from borrowed to measured.

WHETHER THIS CHASSIS IS SHORTER AT THE TOP OR THE BOTTOM. It publishes 43.7 mm where its two shell-mates publish 44.0, and every face figure here is placed from the top edge because that is where the EPS203's measurements are anchored. Three tenths of a millimetre is two thirds of one pixel on the best EPS20x figure, so no staged drawing can say. A dimensioned mechanical drawing closes it, and closes the same question for the other two at the same time.

WHAT THE 32 mm COMES OFF. This chassis is 442 mm deep against its shell-mates' 474, and its front face and its rear face are both theirs - same port wall, same fan bays, same supply bays on the same pitch. So the difference is entirely in the sides, the lid and the floor, and not one staged figure draws any of them. Four undrawn faces is the normal state for this corpus; here it is the specific thing that would explain what makes this model different.

WHICH SPELLING THE METAL CARRIES. The datasheet's front elevation prints `AS4630-54NPE` and the quick start guide's port enlargement prints `AS4630-54NPEM`, both legible at 10x, and the two are renders of the same face by the same vendor. A REAR ELEVATION WITHOUT THE 2 PERCENT GRADIENT. devices.description: 32 x 100G QSFP28 programmable 1RU switch on Xsight Labs X2 with an Intel Xeon D-1713NTE, sold as the EXP100-32X. All ports are on the FRONT with the console, the 1PPS jack, the management jack and the USB; two AC supplies and six fan trays are on the rear. It shares its 442 x 509 x 44 shell and its whole rear with edgecore/exp800-16o and seats that device's fan and supply; its FRONT is its own, because thirty-two ports start the wall 53 mm further left and squeeze the console cluster that sits before it.

gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The single staged document draws two elevations and nothing else. Each face carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.

A view of the five system lamps that is not crossed by a callout arrow. This is the one part of the model whose confidence is `drawing` rather than `measured`, and the reason is a hard limit rather than a shortcut: THE ONLY ELEVATION IS ANNOTATED OVER THE CLUSTER. Two of the datasheet's nine leader arrows land on and beside the lamp grid, and at 10 px/mm a 2 mm window and a four-character legend are both about 3.4 mm wide, so which marks are lamps and which are words cannot be distinguished. AND THERE IS NO BETTER PHOTOGRAPH TO BE HAD. The vendor's product page serves four images; all four were fetched and their SHA-256 digests match the staged copies exactly, at 960 x 700, which is 2.1719 px/mm. That page also lists exactly ONE download for this model, the datasheet - no quick start guide exists, where the sibling EXP800-16O has one with a System LEDs enlargement that resolves the identical cluster at 600 dpi. The marks are taken as the lamps because the resulting 8.4 mm column spacing matches the EXP800's measured 8.2 mm. A quick start guide, or any photograph at 5 px/mm or better, settles it in one look.

The word the panel prints between each pair of port numbers. Every column carries a legend of the form `N (up) WORD (down) N+1` - the numerals are clear on both sources and the numbering runs 1 to 32 - but the word between them is about five characters and 1.2 mm tall, which is 12 px on the elevation and 2.6 px on the photograph. It reads plausibly as "Group", which would be consistent with a device whose every port breaks out four ways, but plausibly is not good enough to silkscreen onto a drawing. Only the numerals are drawn. The word is left off rather than guessed.

Whether the 1PPS jack is an SMA or an SMB. The datasheet names it "1PPS SMA connector"; the elevation draws it 6.49 x 5.25 mm and the photograph 5.98 x 5.07, where common/sma-jack@1 is 9.5 across flats. common/smb-jack@1 is seated because it fits what is drawn. The same conflict stands on edgecore/exp800-16o, whose datasheet uses the same words.

Whether a DC supply or a back-to-front build exists. The datasheet says only "Hot-swappable, load-sharing, redundant AC power" and "Supports front-to-back airflow direction", and no ordering table is staged. Its sibling edgecore/exp800-16o is offered in both airflows on the vendor's page; nothing says this one is. Only the AC F2B configuration is declared.

devices.description: 16 x 800G OSFP programmable 1RU switch on Xsight Labs X2 silicon with an Intel Xeon D-1713NTE, sold as the EXP800-16O. Every port, both the console and the management jack, the USB and a 1PPS timing input are on the FRONT; two AC supplies and SIX fan trays are on the rear. THE PORTS ARE NUMBERED FROM ZERO - the panel prints `0 (up) (down) 1`, `2 (up) (down) 3` and so on to 15, which is this line's only device that does not start at one.

gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Nothing in this corpus draws any of them flat - the mounting figures show brackets going on in three-quarter view, and the -FF photograph is a three-quarter of the front. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.

The second lamp on each OSFP port. The System LEDs enlargement resolves FOUR triangles under each column - two up for the upper port and two down for the lower - and the guide names both: a left lamp carrying seven rate and breakout modes, and a right lamp carrying link, activity and a blinking red for "no link on one or more ports". One per port is drawn and it carries the LEFT lamp's vocabulary, because that is the one that says what the port is doing. Drawing both would be 32 placements and 32 cutouts, and edgecore/dcs240, edgecore/dcs201 and edgecore/as5912-54x all make the same simplification on the same kind of cluster. The undrawn right windows are at 7.2 and 18.4 from each opening's left edge (provenance.port-strip).

One chassis size. The datasheet says 442 x 509 x 44 mm and the quick start's own hardware table says 438.4 x 589 x 43.1 - eighty millimetres of depth apart, with both self-consistent in inches, so neither is a typo. The datasheet's figures are used because the live vendor page agrees with them and because both of the guide's own elevations scale to a round 5 px/mm at 442 and to nothing in particular at 438.4. A DEPTH IS THE LEAST TESTABLE OF THE THREE and this model draws no side view, so nothing here would catch it if the guide is the right one. The weights disagree the same way, 10.005 kg against 13.48 kg with PSUs and fans installed.

Whether the 1PPS jack is an SMA or an SMB. The datasheet names it "1PPS SMA connector"; the elevation draws it 5.00 x 5.44 mm, where common/sma-jack@1 is 9.5 across flats and edgecore/dcs510 measures its own SMA nuts at 8.6. common/smb-jack@1 is seated because it is what fits the drawing, and seating the SMA envelope would overlap the LOC lamp 0.6 mm away. A caliper on the real jack settles it in one measurement.

Whether a DC supply exists. The datasheet says only "AC PSUs: 1+1 redundancy, load-sharing, hot-swappable" and the quick start "2 x AC PSUs"; no DC variant is named anywhere, and no ordering table is staged for this model. The other Edgecore data-centre switches in this library all offer both, so its absence here is recorded rather than assumed either way. Only AC configurations are declared.

devices.description: 1U 19in slide-out fiber enclosure. FS SKU #70361 - a sliding drawer with front access to patch cords and rear access to cable entry, holding up to four FHD fiber adapter panels or MTP/MPO cassettes for up to 144 fibers in 1U.

gaps.note: the extraction handles and FS logo visible in the page-1 product photograph are real but undimensioned anywhere in the corpus - no page gives their position, and a perspective product shot is not a source panel_measure can rectify the way the FHD cassettes' face-on renders were. The front view here draws the four bays and the rack ears only. RE-READ when fs/fhd-splice-12-lc@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: that addition names a cassette that seats inside a bay, not the enclosure's own front panel, so it neither closes this gap nor opens a new one. RE-READ AGAIN when fs/fhd-2mtp12-lc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: same reasoning - a two-MTP cassette still seats inside a bay the same 108.97 x 35.05 way its one-MTP sibling does, so it neither closes this gap nor opens a new one either. RE-READ A THIRD TIME when fs/fhd-1mtp12-sc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: an SC cassette seats in the same 108.97 x 35.05 bay opening its LC and splice siblings do - its front connector family is different, its body is 7.62 mm deeper, but neither changes what the enclosure's own front panel around the bay looks like - so the gap stands unchanged a third time. RE-READ A FOURTH TIME when fs/fhd-1mtp24-lc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: an MTP-24 cassette seats in the same 108.97 x 35.05 bay opening its MTP-12 sibling does - its front is the identical twelve LC-duplex layout fs/fhd-2mtp12-lc-os2-a@1 already uses, and its rear carries a wider MPO ferrule the front panel never sees - so the gap stands unchanged a fourth time. RE-READ when every FHD LC and SC cassette's adapter row moved 1.4-1.8 mm right (fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@4 and its siblings), once `panel_measure` framed FS's renders on the plate's real edge rather than its rounded corner: the rows sit inside each cassette's own plate, not on the enclosure's front panel, so the gap stands unchanged. RE-READ when the LC and SC duplex adapters on the cassettes renamed their bores from tx and rx to fibre positions 1 and 2 and the cassettes composing them took a major: an addressing change inside the bay occupants, not on the front panel around them, so the gap stands unchanged. RE-READ when the fifteen FHD adapter panels joined every bay's `accepts`: a panel is a plate of adapters seated in the same 108.97 x 35.05 bay, so it changes what fills a bay, not the enclosure's own front around it - the gap stands. RE-READ when fs/fhd-fapm6-rj45@1 and fs/fhd-fapm6-blank@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: two more panels in the same 108.97 x 35.05 bay, so the gap stands.
gaps.wanted: a square-on, face-on photograph of the closed FHD-1UFCE front, the same kind of image that let the cassettes' own faceplates be measured.

gaps.note: these five faces carry the bare envelope box from the dimensioned `chassis` figures and nothing else - no slide rail, no cable-management arm, no screws, no rear opening for the cassettes' MTP trunks to pass through. Page 7 dimensions only the front and top outlines, and even the top view resolves no surface detail beyond its own outline. RE-READ when fs/fhd-splice-12-lc@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: a splice cassette's trunk fibres still leave through the same undimensioned rear opening this gap already names, so the gap stands unchanged rather than needing a second one for the new cassette. RE-READ AGAIN when fs/fhd-2mtp12-lc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: its two MTP trunks leave through the same undimensioned rear opening too - twice the trunks, not a different opening - so the gap stands unchanged a second time. RE-READ A THIRD TIME when fs/fhd-1mtp12-sc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: its single MTP trunk leaves through the same undimensioned rear opening its LC and splice siblings use - a deeper cassette body (117.86 mm against 110.24, as was then believed; every FHD cassette here is 117.86, the 110.24 having been a misreading corrected in fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@2), not a different rear opening - so the gap stands unchanged a third time. RE-READ A FOURTH TIME when fs/fhd-1mtp24-lc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: its single MTP-24 trunk leaves through the same undimensioned rear opening its MTP-12 siblings use - a wider ferrule on one trunk instead of two narrower ones, not a different opening, and the same 117.86 mm body depth fs/fhd-2mtp12-lc-os2-a@1 already carries - so the gap stands unchanged a fourth time. NARROWED, NOT CLOSED, when the rear gained its opening: the owner of the model reports the back is open behind the slots, so the rear now draws one hole per bay and the cassettes' backs through it (see `provenance.rear-opening`). What the report cannot give is the opening's real outline - four holes or one, the bay's size or not - and nothing held shows the rear, so the photograph is still wanted. RE-READ when the Type AF and universal cassettes (57037, 68540, 68549, 182641, 182643) joined every bay's `accepts`: they are their Type A twins' bodies with different internal wiring and rear labels, so their trunks leave through the same undimensioned opening - the gap stands. RE-READ when the OM3, OM4, OM5 and OM4 universal cassettes (57017, 57342, 57024, 174246, 174248, 174250, 182642, 182644, 382889, 382897) joined every bay's `accepts`: they are their OS2 twins' bodies in another fibre with other-coloured adapters, and their rear renders - 57017.E, 57342.E, 57024.E and the g4 views of the other seven - print the same port-range legends and Type A labels on the same MTP bulkheads (the lid-edge seal sticker reads differently on the 2025-26 renders and is not drawn), so their trunks leave through the same undimensioned opening - the gap stands. RE-READ when the 36-fibre cassettes (105333, 105335) joined every bay's `accepts`: three MTP trunks instead of one or two, leaving through the same undimensioned rear opening from the same 99 x 31 body - the gap stands. RE-READ when every FHD LC and SC cassette's adapter row moved 1.4-1.8 mm right on its faceplate: a front-plate change, which none of these five faces shows - the gap stands. RE-READ when each rear MPO adapter gained its fibre elements, 1 to 12 or 1 to 24: they sit on the cassette rear, and the rear opening the trunks leave through is as undimensioned as it was - the gap stands. RE-READ when the bays stopped saying where a back lands (`rear.at`) and each back began landing where its own module's body stands, mirrored in the hole: the holes and the opening are unchanged, and nothing held shows them any better - the gap stands. RE-READ when the fifteen FHD adapter panels joined every bay's `accepts`: a panel's rear is its adapters' far ends, 16 to 32 deep instead of a 117.86 cassette body, and the cords reach them through the same undimensioned opening - the gap stands.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph (the cassettes seat from the front but the trunk cables leave from the back of the drawer) and a lid/side photograph, the same kind of source dcp-2's own equivalent gap asks for.

datasheet.title: QuickSpecs HPE ProLiant DL160 Gen10 Server

devices.description: HPE's 1U two-socket Intel Xeon Scalable rack server of the Gen10 generation, in its two front builds - four 3.5 inch LFF bays (878972-B21) or eight 2.5 inch SFF bays with a media bay (878973-B21) - over one rear: three PCIe 3.0 slots on two risers, two Flex Slot power supply bays, two embedded 1GbE ports, the iLO 5 port, VGA, two USB 3.0 ports, and blanks for the media module and the optional serial port. Retired by HPE; the QuickSpecs carries HPE's RETIRED notice.

gaps.note: no system power figure in the QuickSpecs (four editions), User Guide or Maintenance and Service Guide; each gives per-supply ratings and defers to HPE Power Advisor, a web tool, for configured draw. ENERGY STAR's certified server list has no DL160 Gen10 entry and the SPECpower result a search attributes to it is a DL360 Gen10. The server profile's power requirement is unmet for that reason.
gaps.wanted: a configured power figure from HPE (Power Advisor output or a DL160 Gen10 power specification)

gaps.note: the 8 SFF media bay accepts the optical drive cage (873961-B21 enablement kit, 9.5 mm drives 726536-B21 / 726537-B21) or the two-bay SFF drive cage (866458-B21), and the 4 LFF optical bay the 9.5 mm drive; only the blanks are drawn. The User Guide elevations GUID-696364B2 and GUID-7FDCEC9A show both options at 1.36 px/mm; the only photograph of either is a reseller's 10 SFF unit from above, and of the optical kit only its bare bracket and cables.
gaps.wanted: straight-on images of the optical drive bezel and the two-bay SFF cage in a DL160 Gen10

gaps.note: three Flex Slot supplies the QuickSpecs lists are not drawn: 865438-B21 (800 W Titanium), 865428-B21 (800 W Universal, HVAC/HVDC) and 865434-B21 (800 W -48 VDC). The Flex Slot QuickSpecs gives the DC supplies a different length (18.29 cm) and no image of any of the three faces is held.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of each supply's face

gaps.note: the server also exists with a non-hot-plug supply in place of the two Flex Slot bays: the User Guide's enablement procedure begins "Remove the non-hot-plug power supply" before fitting the redundant power supply cage, the system board has a non-hot-plug power supply connector, the Parts Support Guide heads a section with it, and HPE's own rear product image (straight on) shows one wide plate with a fan marked 92% and a single inlet where the bays are. No document held names its part number or rating or says which models shipped with it - every model in QuickSpecs versions 6 to 32 is listed with a hot-plug supply - so that rear is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: the non-hot-plug supply's part number and rating, and which models carried it

gaps.note: no image held shows a card in any of the three PCIe slots; which way up each bracket lies follows from where the riser connectors are, which HPE's PartSurfer photograph shows for the primary riser and only the User Guide's board figure for the secondary (see the riser parts). The FlexibleLOM riser (hpe/riser-flom- dl160@1) and the twelve FlexibleLOM adapters HPE lists for this server are drawn - six from the QuickSpecs and six more that only the Product Information Reference lists - each from a seller's photograph of its own faceplate (the 536FLR-T's photograph was read and its drawing is the 331FLR's, which it matches to a millimetre), and the cage's opening for them from two isometric User Guide figures: no image held shows that cage's rear straight on, with or without an adapter, so where an adapter sits on the rear is estimated. The primary riser BLANK (hpe/riser-blank- primary-dl160@1, 878532-001), which a server ordered with no riser carries, is drawn from PartSurfer's photograph and seated in the `lff4-no-riser` configuration; what stands in the SECONDARY riser's place on such a server no document held says; the one photograph held of a riser-less rear has it out of focus, dark with bright fastener heads and not a perforated cage face, which is too little to draw, so that configuration keeps the secondary cage and is probably wrong there.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on rear image of a server with the FlexibleLOM riser and an adapter fitted, and of a server with a card in each slot and a Media Module adapter fitted

gaps.note: the top view is drawn from the QuickSpecs Internal View, a photograph that fails the panel gate at 3.6%, so every interior position is a fraction and is estimated; and it is the only top-down image held. Not drawn because no image shows them from above: the redundant power supply cage and its power distribution board (the photograph has the non-hot-plug supply), the secondary riser cage for slot 3 (not fitted in the photograph), the drive cage and backplane under the lid, the energy pack, and the 4 LFF chassis' interior.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned plan of the DL160 Gen10 interior, or HPE's service model

gaps.note: the front bezel option is not drawn: the QuickSpecs lists the HPE 1U Gen10 Bezel Kit 867998-B21, which needs the quick-release ear kit, and the User Guide has 'Installing the front bezel option'. The only image held of it is a reseller's angled photograph.

devices.description: Juniper EX2300-C-12P is the compact, fanless member of the EX2300 line: a 1RU-high Gigabit Ethernet access switch 279 mm wide with 12 10/100/1000BASE-T ports, all with PoE+ and 124 W available, and two built-in 10-Gigabit SFP+/SFP uplink ports. The front carries the 12 jacks in two stacked rows numbered 0 to 11 (the upper jack of a column takes the even number), the two uplinks numbered 0 and 1, a USB port, the management Ethernet port with the RJ-45 console port under it, a mini-USB console port, three status lamps, four port-mode lamps, a Factory Reset/Mode button and an ESD point. The rear carries the earthing terminal, a heatsink and the AC power cord inlet; there are no fans. The power supply is built into the chassis, so there are no bays. It ships standing on its rubber feet; it can also be fixed under a desk, to a wall or a ferrous surface, or on two posts of a rack with the separately orderable brackets. datasheet.title: Juniper EX6200 Line of Ethernet Switches datasheet (1000390-002-EN, Aug 2011)

devices.description: Juniper EX6210, a 14 U modular campus and data center access switch that runs Junos OS. The front has ten horizontal slots: eight take line cards only, and slots 4 and 5 take a Switch Fabric and Routing Engine (SRE) module or a line card. Four power supply slots, PSU 0 to PSU 3, sit under them. A single fan tray at the rear cools the chassis from front to back. Every shipping order includes one SRE module, one power supply and the cover panels. The line cards are a family of their own and are not modelled: their slots show cover panels.

gaps.note: Height: 24.3 in in the guide's Table 7, which is 617.2 mm, and 61.1 cm in the same row; the datasheet gives 24.3 in and 61.6 cm. Width: 17.3 in (43.9 cm) and 19 in (48.3 cm) with the brackets in both. Depth: 15.5 in (39.3 cm) in both. The task gave 9 U; the guide and the datasheet give 14 U, and 24.3 in is 13.9 U. The inch figures are carried: 439.4 x 617.2 x 393.7 mm.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the chassis, or Juniper's confirmation of the height in centimetres

The EX6200-48T (48-port RJ-45), EX6200-48P (48-port PoE+) and EX6200-48F (48-port SFP) line cards (guide Tables 3 and 36 to 40, Figures 25 to 30). Each has 48 ports in a block, two lamps per port and the ON, ST and (for the PoE card) PoE lamps. A line card family is a separate piece of work. The two cards each shipping order includes are not shown; every line card slot shows its cover panel, and the guide says which slots the cards take nowhere.

The part numbers of the line card cover panel and the SRE module cover panel. Juniper's end-of-life table lists EX6200-BLNK-LC and EX6200-BLNK-SRE-LC without descriptions and the guide gives the panels no number, so none is written. EX6200-BLNK-PWR-1U is listed there too and the guide's Table 21 has no 1U cover.

gaps.note: Table 5 lists three 2500 W AC power supply cover panels for the DC order and Table 51 three 2100 W DC power supply cover panels; Table 21 names a cover for the two AC supplies only. The 2U cover (EX6200-BLNK-PWR-2U) is seated over the DC slots.
gaps.wanted: the cover panel part number for the 2100 W DC supply

A flat drawing or photograph of the 5000 W AC and the 2100 W DC supply faces. The guide draws both only in isometric (Figures 17, 23, 24, 66 and 68), so their lamps, switch, handle and terminals are fractions, and the 5000 W supply's 3U height is the guide's "approximately 3 U". The DC supply is drawn with two positive and two negative studs as Figure 23 shows; the text names one pair of input lugs.

Which power supply slot the single shipped supply takes. Every figure draws four supplies (Figure 5) and the guide says power supplies need not be installed in serial order, so PSU 0 is shown seated and PSU 1 to PSU 3 covered.

A straight-on drawing or photograph of the rear. Figure 2 is an isometric, so the fan tray, the rectangular opening in the plate, the exhaust band and the two earthing and ESD points are fractions of it; the opening's purpose is not stated.
The sides, top and bottom. Figures 1 and 2 show the sides in isometric with rows of screws, the bracket and a handle plate and no dimension; no flat figure of any of them exists.

The optional air filter (EX6210-FLTR, six captive screws over the intake strip at the front right; the datasheet lists it as a spare and the guide does not ship it). It bolts onto the front and is drawn in no flat figure, so it is not drawn.

The protective earthing terminal as a part that seats a ring lug. The guide gives a pair of threaded inserts for UNC 1/4-20 screws, 0.625 in (15.86 mm) apart, and a lug (Panduit LCD2-14A-L) with two screws, but draws them only in isometric (Figures 2 and 13). The pair is drawn as two plain insert heads, not as the library's stud-pair part: that part presents lug seats, which the library's pinned census of default lug turns (spec/tests/test_occupant_turn.py) counts, and an open pull request edits that test.
A straight-on photograph of the front and the rear. Every position comes from the guide's drawings and none from a photograph, so the colour and finish are not known.

devices.description: Juniper EX8208, the 14 U end-of-life modular Ethernet switch of the EX8200 family. Everything is on the front. devices.description: Juniper EX9251, a 1RU fixed-configuration core and aggregation switch that runs Junos OS, the smaller of the two EX9250 chassis. The front has 8 SFP+ ports (10 GbE) in two rows of four, 4 rate-selectable QSFP28 ports (100, 40 or 10 GbE), a GM/PTP SFP cage, a MGMT RJ-45, and the timing and service ports: BITS, CON (console), ToD, a USB port, and 1PPS and 10MHz SMB connectors in and out. The part numbers of the front-mounting brackets, rear-mounting brackets and ETSI brackets, which the guide lists by name only, and the bracket extents. They are in the accessory box.

A photograph of an EX9251 power supply. Where the ToD port's lamp is. The guide says "the LEDs for the ToD port" are lit steadily green but its Table 7 lists none and Figure 1 draws none; the BITS jack has two lamps in the top corners.
the GM/PTP port's behaviour; the guide says support for the port is not available in this release

The USB revision. The guide says Junos supports USB version 1.0 and later and that the flash drives must be USB 2.0 or later; the port is drawn with the neutral usb2 skin.
Table 25 lists a mini-USB Type-B console port among the management cables, which Figure 1 does not show; the front panel has the RJ-45 CON only, and no mini-USB console is drawn.

devices.description: Juniper QFX5130-48C, a 1RU data-centre leaf switch running Junos OS Evolved, with 48 SFP56-DD ports (100 GbE) for servers and 8 QSFP-DD uplink ports (400 GbE). The port side carries the 48 SFP56-DD cages in two rows of 24, in three groups of eight columns, and the eight uplinks in two rows of four, with a lamp for each. The fan and supply side carries the management panel at the left end: the RJ-45 management and console ports, a USB port, the reset button, the three chassis lamps, the 10 MHz and 1 PPS output connectors, two SFP+ ports and the ESD point. Six fan modules and two power supplies fill the rest of that side. The QFX5130-48CM has the same panel and is MACsec capable, so it is a set of configurations of this device. Both ship in four power and airflow variants, AC or DC supplies with front-to-back (AIR OUT) or back-to-front (AIR IN) airflow, and as a spare chassis with no supplies and no fan modules.

gaps.wanted: The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis.

What the windows at the corners of the lower (console) RJ-45 jack are. The guide describes lamps for the management port only (figure 32, Table 16) and none for the console. Not drawn on the console jack.

The part number of the fan modules. The datasheet's ordering table says QFX5130-48C-FANAO and -FANAI; guide Tables 4 and 17 say QFX5130-48C-FANAFO and -FANAFI. The datasheet's spelling is each component's model, since it is the one a buyer orders, and the guide's is in its description.

The airflow of JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO. Guide Table 24 prints "Airflow In (port-to-FRU)" in one row and "Airflow Out (port-to-FRU)" in the row for the 48C; Table 3 and the part number's AFO say port-to-FRU is Airflow Out (front-to-back). Airflow Out is used.
The lower AC input range. Guide Table 20 and the datasheet's Table 2 both say 100 to 127 VAC for the 48C and 48CM, while the datasheet's 32CD column says 115 to 127 VAC. The 48C figure is carried.

The DC input current. Guide Table 27 and the datasheet's Table 2 say 40 A maximum for the 48C and 48CM, while the 32CD says 35 A. The 40 A figure is carried. The guide's breaker advice reads "40 A (80 VDC) minimum", which is not repeated.
The size of the two SSDs. The datasheet's Table 2 says 2 x 100 GB for the 48C and 48CM; the guide's overview of the 32CD says 2 x 50 GB and its 48C text gives no size. The datasheet's 100 GB is used.

Which 32 of the SFP56-DD ports and which 4 of the QSFP-DD ports support MACsec on the 48CM. The guide says "32x 100G SFP56-DD and 4x 400G QSFP-DD ports support MACsec" and does not number them. Nothing is marked on the ports.

The connector type of the 10M Out and PPS Out jacks. The guide calls them "clock input and output connectors" and does not name a type; the photograph shows gold coaxial jacks 6.5 mm across, drawn as the library's SMA jack. Estimated. The USB revision. The guide names a "USB slot" and no revision, and says a drive up to 16.5 mm wide is needed to reach the reset pinhole. The port is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.

The lid, the underside and the side walls. The image library's side and top views are perspective photographs with no scale, the guide has no flat figure of them, and its mounting and grounding figures show the brackets and the two protective-earth screws on the top in perspective only.
The protective earthing terminal, two 10-32 screw holes on the top of the chassis near the management panel (guide figure 101). The figure is an isometric with no scale, so no position is given.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kit's contract. The guide names QFX5130-1RU-4PRMK and no kit contract exists in the library; none is written here.
The model name printed on the rear management panel. The 48C photograph prints QFX5130-48C and the 48CM photograph QFX5130-48CM; the two models share this device, so neither name is drawn.

devices.description: Juniper QFX5210-64C, a 2RU data-centre spine and leaf switch. It has 64 QSFP28 ports, numbered 0 to 63 in sixteen columns of four, and two SFP+ ports. The QSFP28 ports run at 100 GbE by default, at 40 GbE by transceiver, and at 50, 25 or 10 GbE by channelization. The port side also carries an RJ45 management port, an RJ45 console port, a USB port, a reset pinhole and four chassis lamps. The FRU side carries four fan modules, two power supplies and a two-hole protective earthing terminal. It ships as one front panel in several builds: AC or DC supplies, front-to-back (AIR OUT) or back-to-front (AIR IN).

gaps.wanted: The HPE datasheet a00150817enw, which the intake lists for a human to fetch. No datasheet figure is used.

Which lamps serve the inner ports of each column (1 to 31 odd, 32 to 62 even). The guide's Table 10 says four lamps for each QSFP28 port and its figures draw four lamps at the outer edges only, so the inner ports carry no lamp in the model.

The six round marks per column in the band between the two cages of a stack. The figures draw them as circles and the photograph shows ringed holes; the guide names them nowhere, so they are not drawn.
The two bi-colour lamps for each SFP+ port that Table 10 describes. No figure draws them and the photograph does not resolve any.
The bi-colour lamp the guide says is next to each fan module (Table 16). No figure or photograph shows where it is, so none is drawn.

The supply rating legend. Figure 8 prints 12-6A and 25A; the photograph of the real device prints 12-7A and 34A (Max); Tables 18 and 21 give 12 A at 100 VAC and 6 A at 240 VAC, and 25 A. The photograph's wording is drawn as printed; the tables' figures are in attrs.
Interface names are not printed on the metal and the guide's channelization text names none for this switch, so none are written.

The orderable part numbers of the DC and the AIR IN builds. The guide names the chassis spare QFX5210-64C-CHAS, the builds QFX5210-64C-AFI and QFX5210-64C-AFO (in its cautions), and the units but gives no SKU for the DC builds or any -S build, so the two DC builds are examples and not orderable.
An end-of-life announcement. None was searched for in this pass, and the guide states none, so the device states no lifecycle.

How many fan modules the switch can lose. The guide's Component Redundancy section says only that the switch has four fan modules and that a failed module that cannot keep the switch within its thresholds raises chassis alarms and can shut the switch down. Table 4 lists the fan modules as removable without action, and the cooling text says the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced. No N+1 form is claimed.
A power figure for a fan module. Table 3 and the cooling chapter give the airflow and the part numbers only; searched the cooling and power chapters and found whole-switch figures only.
The depth of the fan modules and of the supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only.
The position of the front mounting brackets of the rack kit QFX5210-4PST-RMK. Figure 22 shows them in perspective with no scale; no position is written.

devices.description: Juniper QFX5220-128C, a 4RU 100G data-centre spine switch that runs Junos OS Evolved. devices.description: Juniper QFX5240-64OD, a 2RU 800G data-centre spine switch running Junos OS Evolved. The rear carries two 3000 W AC power supplies stacked at the left and four front-to-back fan modules. The chassis width. devices.description: Juniper QFX5241-32OD, a 1RU 800G data-centre switch running Junos OS Evolved. It has 32 OSFP ports (800 GbE) in sixteen columns of two, in four groups of four columns, and two SFP28 ports side by side, with a pair of lamps above each column. The port side also carries the RJ-45 management and console ports, a USB Type-C port, the reset button and the three chassis lamps. The rear carries two 2400 W AC power supplies at its two ends and seven front-to-back fan modules between them. gaps.wanted: The QFX5240 line datasheet, which covers the QFX5241. Its address redirects to an HPE document server that refused every request made for this change. Nothing here is the datasheet's; the figures are the guide's.

The depth and the registry size of the OSFP cage. The library's std/osfp has no registry entry and carries an estimated depth; the 23.1 by 13.5 mm opening it uses was measured on another maker's 2RU box and the photograph here agrees with it to 0.3 mm in width.

The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures 20 to 23 carry no scale and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis; the fan module's "40 mm x 56 mm" does not say which side is the depth.
