The lamp of each SFP28 port. The guide's Table 14 gives each of the two ports one status lamp; neither the photograph nor the guide's flat figures show where it is.

The power of the AC switch. The guide's Power System text says 543 W typical and 1394 W maximum and its Table 15 says 537 W and 1381 W, which the text gives to the DC-with-ORv3 build. The text's figures are used.

The ORv3 switch-tray assembly QFX5241-32OD-DO-T1 and its spare QFX5241-32OD-TCHAS: 21.14 x 1.74 x 31.71 in (Table 10), drawn only in isometric (figures 13 and 14), a different envelope from this device. Its DC supply QFX5241-1U-PWR-DO is therefore not a component here. Not modelled.

The lamps of the management jack. Guide figure 19 and Table 13 describe two lamps on the management port; the photograph shows them at the corners of the jack. The jack is drawn with the library's lamped jack.
The rating label of each supply and the serial number labels (the Locate the Serial Number section). Not drawn.
The two-hole protective earthing terminal, "on the side of the chassis" (guide figure 9, isometric). No flat view of the side is held; the side views are empty.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kit's contract. The guide names QFX5241-1U-4PRMK and no kit contract exists in the library; none is written here.

devices.description: Juniper QFX5250-64OE-L, a 2OU liquid-cooled 1.6T data-centre leaf and spine switch for an Open Rack v3 (ORv3) rack, running Junos OS Evolved. The port side has 64 OSFP ports (1.6 TbE, for ORHS transceivers with a riding heat sink) in two banks of eight columns of four, with a lamp for every port. It also has two SFP28 ports (10 or 25 GbE), the RJ-45 management and console ports, a USB port, the 10 MHz and 1 PPS connectors, the ON/OFF and reset buttons and the LEAKAGE, ID, SYS and ALM lamps. A switch handle stands at each end of the port bank. The rear has no power supplies and no fan modules. It carries a coolant outlet (hot) and inlet (cold) UQDB06 plug at the ends and the IT gear input connector in the middle, which blind-mates with the rack's busbar. It is the only model the guide describes.

gaps.wanted: A QFX5250 datasheet and the maker's studio photographs of the model, front and rear. None was found, so the chassis colour, the finish of the levers and handles, the lamp colours and the legends' ink are not read off hardware. The front and rear are drawn from guide figures 10 and 11 alone.

An Open Rack mount value and an ORv3 rail kit contract (the library has neither; the guide names no rail kit). The body is a 2OU tray, 21 in wide: `ru: 2` is the guide's count of Open Rack units, and a viewer that treats it as two 44.45 mm EIA units draws a tray that is 21 in wide and 96 mm tall in a 19-in rack. The sibling celestica/ds6001 states no `ru` instead.
The maximum power output. Table 21 and the power text say 4300 W; Table 9 says 4800 W. 4300 W is used.
A leader or a photograph showing which cage each of the 64 lamps serves. The lamps are numbered 0 to 63 and the number is taken as the port number; the figure draws no leader.

What the small "U" and arch marks printed beside the two SFP28 cages mean; they are not drawn. The guide's callout 11 names only the cages. The SFP28 role is "in-band management ports" in the front-panel text and network ports in Table 19.
The console jack draws no lamps in figure 10; the management jack's two lamps are described in Table 14.
The depth of the UQDB06 plugs and the busbar connector; no figure gives one.
The lamp colours of the management jack beyond "green" for link activity and "solid green" for 1 Gbps (Table 14); the speed lamp's colours at 10 and 100 Mbps are not stated.
A rating label, if any; the rear figure draws none.

devices.description: Juniper QFX5700, a modular 5RU, 12.8 Tbps data-centre spine and leaf switch running Junos OS Evolved. The port side has two Routing and Control Board slots across the top (RCB 0 and RCB 1, one board fitted), and under them nine line-card slots, FPC 0 to FPC 7 and an eighth, numbered 8, that the guide calls unsupported and that holds a blank. The line cards (QFX5K-FPC-16C, QFX5K-FPC-20Y and QFX5K-FPC-4CD) are ordered separately and are not modelled here: every slot shows its blank. A model plate and the ESD point stand at the right of the port side. The rear has four 3000 W supplies in a row across the top, AC or DC, and two fan trays of four fans each below them. It ships as one front panel in AC and DC builds, as the QFX5700E build with its own forwarding engine board, and as a spare chassis.

gaps.wanted: what QFX5700-CHAS ships with. The datasheet calls it a spare chassis ("QFX5700/QFX5700E - Ersatzgehaeuse") and the guide's Table 27 lists only the base configuration. It is modelled with every bay open; whether it ships with the FPC blanks, the midplane only or the front brackets is not stated.

a redundant (four supply) build. Neither the guide nor the datasheet lists an orderable one: the base configuration has two supplies, and the guide says all four must be fitted for power redundancy. The four-supply population is a population of the PSU bays, not a SKU.
a photograph or figure of an empty RCB slot or of the JNP5K-RCB-BLNK blank, and of the power-slot blank (which the guide gives no code); both blanks are drawn plain from the openings they cover.
a flat figure or photograph of the QFX5700 DC supply face (the guide's figure 33 is an isometric); the reused part draws it from the AC supply's outline.

the guide's Table 21 (storage -40 to 85 C, humidity 55 to 70 percent) against the datasheet (storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 90 percent operating and 5 to 95 percent not operating). The guide's are carried.
the photograph prints nothing on the slot 8 blank and the drawing shows the same latches and screws as a card; the blank is drawn from the drawing.

devices.description: Lantronix SLC 8000 advanced modular console manager, a 1U chassis that connects up to 48 RJ45 serial or USB console ports to a network. The front has an LCD, a keypad, a memory card slot, two USB ports, an RJ45 console port and a modem jack. The rear has two network ports, three bays for I/O modules, and an AC power inlet. This model is the base chassis without I/O modules; the three bays are declared and no module is modelled.

gaps.note: The User Guide says the RJ11 modem port needs the optional internal modem card (56KINTMODEM-01). The jack is drawn on every build. No held document says whether the opening is present without the card.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the front with the modem card out, and its part number on the unit.

gaps.note: Figure 2-1 and the Quick Start Guide label an "Indicator LED" that no photograph held resolves. It is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front, and a table of what its LED means.

gaps.note: The rear has three I/O module bays; no document gives a module a size. The three bays are declared at the positions and size of the windows read off Figure 2-2, each stating the class of module it takes, and no module is modelled or seated. The I/O Module Install Guide and User Guide Table 3-8 give the module types: a 16-port RJ45 module, a 16-port USB module, a 16-port Ethernet switch module and an 8-port RJ45 module for bay 1. Their rules are words only and no tool checks them: the 8-port module goes in bay 1 only, the switch module in bay 2 or 3, never bay 1, and the bays fill in order from bay 1.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of an I/O module, and a straight-on photograph of the rear.

gaps.note: The chassis also ships with two SFP ports in place of the two RJ45 network ports, with a dual AC inlet, or with dual DC inputs. No photograph of the DC inlet is held and none of the SFP rear at a usable size, so only the copper network and single AC build is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear of an SFP model and of a DC model.

gaps.note: The four faces draw the envelope only. The User Guide places the battery and modem door on the top and the product label on the underside, and the Quick Start Guide says the sides carry air vents. The angled photographs show a vent field on each side and the door at the right-hand rear of the top, but not at a size that gives a position, so none is drawn.
gaps.wanted: photographs of the lid, the underside and both flanks, with the ear brackets off.

datasheet.title: MaiaEdge PBC/PCE datasheet v3

devices.description: MaiaEdge Path Border Controller - a 1RU appliance that merges L2 switching and L3 routing to provision deterministic private Ethernet paths over any underlying transport, with line-rate AES-256-GCM IPsec. Two 100GbE QSFP28 ports on the front beside a console and two management jacks, behind a built-in bezel, with a touch screen beside it; two hot-swap 550W supplies and a one-piece five-fan tray on the back, front-to-back.

gaps.note: The supplies are very probably Gospower G1251-0550WN-series 550 W CRPS modules taking AC or high-voltage DC through one inlet - a visual match on every feature against that module's photographs (see maiaedge/psu-550w@1's `identity`), and the Port Extender datasheet's "100-240VAC or 180-300VDC" is that module's range. But no document names the part, so its model is not recorded and no -48 V DC option is modelled or known.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of one supply's rating label - it is on the module's body, so pull one supply to take it.

gaps.note: WHAT THE LAMPS MEAN IS UNKNOWN. The slot left of port 0 is one light-pipe opening (photographed square-on), and the vendor's UI view draws four lamps in a column there; all four carry `for: chassis`. The maintainer counts one lamp per 100G port, and the photograph shows no lamp anywhere else near the ports, so two of the four are probably those - but nothing says which, and an invented mapping would be worse than none. The chassis status lamp on the bezel beside the right window is modelled. Red and green points seen through the louvres in the rack photograph are internal board LEDs and are deliberately not drawn. The touch screen is maiaedge/pbc-2000-lcd@2 and what it shows is software.
gaps.wanted: an LED table, or a photograph of the unit powered up with the transceivers out.

gaps.note: These four faces draw the chassis envelope and nothing else. The envelope itself is not a guess - 437.90 x 291.08 x 41.27 is dimensioned on page 3 of the datasheet - but no source held shows what is ON any of them: no vent field, no label, no screw pattern, no rail. The flat rect asserts the box and claims nothing about its surface, which is what lets the device carry a rack elevation and a 3D box without inventing detail.
gaps.wanted: photographs of the lid, the underside and either flank out of the rack. The unit was shot in service with a device directly above it.

gaps.note: The datasheet states the supply configuration and no chassis draw figure, so none is recorded. L27 stands, and the chassis total is a floor rather than a total.

devices.description: MikroTik CRS309-1G-8S+IN is a compact Cloud Router Switch, 272 mm wide. It has eight SFP+ cages, one 10/100/1000 Ethernet port that takes PoE in, and a DE-9 serial console. It runs SwOS or RouterOS (dual boot). The front carries the eight cages with an ACT and a 10G lamp above each. Beside them are the POE/BOOT jack, the CONSOLE connector, the RESET button and the USER and PWR lamps. The rear carries the DC jack (DC 12-57 V as printed), a cable-restraint slot, an earthing stud and a finned heatsink that cools the unit. There is no fan and no built-in mains supply: a 24 V 1.2 A adapter ships in the box. It mounts in a rack on the ears supplied.

devices.description: MikroTik CRS312-4C+8XG-RM is a fixed 1U Cloud Router Switch. It has eight 1G/2.5G/5G/10G RJ45 ports and four combo ports. Each combo port is a 10G RJ45 jack (1T to 4T) and an SFP+ cage (1F to 4F), one in use at a time. It also has a 10/100 management jack (MGMT/BOOT), an RJ45 serial console and a USB type A port. It runs SwOS or RouterOS. The front carries the eight 10G jacks in two blocks of four. Beside them are the combo jacks under a blue bracket and the two by two SFP+ block. Then come the CONSOLE and MGMT/BOOT jacks, the RESET button and the USB port. The USER, FAULT, POWER 2 and POWER 1 lamps follow. The two AC supplies and the four fans are built into the chassis, so there are no bays. The air passes through a vent field in the right wall. The rear carries the two IEC C14 inlets, POWER 1 and POWER 2. A spring wire clip stands over each. It also carries four fan grilles and twelve crosshead screws.

devices.description: MikroTik CRS320-8P-8B-4S+RM is a fixed 1U Cloud Router Switch with high-power PoE out. It also has four SFP+ cages and an RJ45 serial console, and runs SwOS or RouterOS (dual boot). The front carries the 24 jacks in three blocks of four columns by two rows under an orange PoE-out band. A pair of lamps sits above each column and another pair below it, each lamp numbered. The four SFP+ cages are a block of two by two with a numbered lamp under each. The front also has the CONSOLE jack, the RESET and MODE buttons and the PWR, USR, FAN and PoE lamps. The 500 W AC supply and the two fans are built into the chassis, so there are no bays. The fans draw through grilles in the right wall. No document held shows the rear, so the rear is not drawn and the AC inlet is not placed.

devices.description: MikroTik CSS326-24G-2S+RM is a fixed 1U Cloud Smart Switch. It has 24 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports and two SFP+ cages, and runs SwOS only. The front carries the 24 jacks in three blocks of four columns by two rows. They are numbered 1 to 24 as printed, with the odd number on the lower jack of a column. Port 1 is marked POE IN for passive PoE power. A lamp with the port number printed on it sits under each jack. The front also has the two SFP+ cages with their ACT/LINK and 10G lamps. It has the PWR and USR lamps and the RES reset button, and no console jack. The rear carries the DC jack (DC 8 - 30V as printed), a cable-restraint slot, the earthing stud and the vents. There is no built-in mains supply: a 24 V 1.2 A adapter ships in the box, so there are no power bays. The round opening on the rear is a stamped fan-guard grille with four fan-mount holes and no fan fitted. The product page lists passive cooling, so no fan is drawn. The CRS326-24G-2S+RM is the sibling with RouterOS and a console jack and is its own device.

gaps.note: The earthing stud has a wing nut (photograph 1268; the drawing's 11 mm). The stud is placed as mikrotik/earth-stud-disc, a plain disc that stands in for the wing nut. The reason is the nearest the schema has: the part itself is what is missing, and the library has no `needs-part` reason.

datasheet.title: Nokia NFXS-D (7360 ISAM FX-16 Shelf - version D) ISAM Unit Data Sheet R5.6, 3FE-65209-BAAA-TQZZA Issue 04

devices.description: The 14RU ANSI shelf of the Nokia 7360 ISAM FX (Lightspan Access Node FX) GPON/NGPON access node, part 3FE65209BA. Its line-termination (LT), network-termination (NT) and NT I/O cards stand VERTICALLY in one cage, left to right LT1 to LT8, NT A, NTIO, NT B, LT9 to LT16. Below the cage are three bands: the fixed PDBP-C power distribution front (two 70 A dual-pole breakers, the Energy Hazard label, the shelf name, the critical/major/minor and BAT A/BAT B/ACO lamps and the ACO push button, beside an ESD earth bonding point); the BFAN-H fan tray; and the connector band (remote craft port at the bottom left, the four -48 V dual-post terminals TB1-1 to TB1-4 on their angled shrouds, the BITS wire-wrap pins, the ToD/1 Hz RJ-45 and the 50-pin CO alarms connector). The PDBP-C is built into the ANSI shelf and has no part number of its own, so it is drawn as the shelf's own panel, not as a bay. The LT slots take only the LT blank until the line cards are modelled (roc-ops/Portrayal#538).

gaps.note: Every ANSI-valid LT card the coverage grid lists is modelled and accepted in these slots, except FELT-B AC (3FE69486AC), for which no data sheet exists in any staged document. FELT-C is an ETSI/MII card and is not accepted by this ANSI shelf. The copper DSL/POTS cards (NDLS, NPOT, NIAT, NDPS, NVPS) are out of scope by decision (roc-ops/Portrayal#538).
gaps.wanted: a FELT-B AC unit data sheet

gaps.note: The front of the fan area is drawn three ways. The BFAN-H data sheet 3FE66546AAAATQZZA03 Figure 2 puts ALM at mid-width with three label windows. nokia/bfan-h@1 draws the last, and it is seated unchanged. gaps.note: The safety cover over TB1-1 to TB1-4 (UDS Figure 20, HIM Figures 45 and 47) is not modelled; no staged document gives it a part number or a dimension.

gaps.note: No staged document draws the rear, top or bottom of the FX-16 as an elevation; Figure 13's second view, captioned "top", is the left side.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph

gaps.note: The left side in Figure 13 also draws two rows of eight fasteners at mid-height, a row of eight under the top edge, four near the bottom and a rectangular opening beside the ground studs (the cable opening HIM s6.3.2 mentions). devices.description: Compact 1RU PTP grandmaster, boundary clock, NTP server and GNSS receiver with a high-quality OCXO (Stratum 3 / G.812 Type III). Fanless. Everything is on the front: two hot-swappable AC or DC supplies, two expansion slots for timing fan-out cards, four 1G Ethernet ports (two of them combo RJ-45/SFP), BITS, ToD, clock and PPS I/O, and the GNSS antenna input.

gaps.note: The data sheet gives 443 wide and the manual 436 "without mounting brackets". Both of the face's own images measure 443 x 44 to about 1% and 436 x 44 to 2-3%, so the faces are drawn 443. The reconciliation - a front plate a little wider than the body - is read from one three-quarter render, not measured.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the chassis, or a ruler across a real unit's front and across its sides.

gaps.note: The product-page three-quarter render shows each flank with two fields of round vent holes and three pairs of screws, two of them the bracket positions the manual describes; it is at an angle that measures none of it. The top and bottom are shown by nothing. These four views carry the envelope only.
gaps.wanted: a square-on photograph of one flank and of the lid.

gaps.note: Manual p46 - blank plates "must be installed in unused PSU or expansion slots", each with a captive thumbscrew on the right. No image of either blank is held. The expansion-slot blank is modelled from that text alone (oscilloquartz/osa542x-lc-blank@1, art estimated); the PSU blank is not modelled, so a pulled supply draws as its opening.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing of the expansion-slot and PSU blank plates.

gaps.note: The IRIG-B card's optical output is a round barrel 7.4 across in a 375 px render; no document names the connector type.
gaps.wanted: the IRIG-B card's own data sheet or a newer install manual.

gaps.note: The manual gives part numbers for the BTOH-16, CPOH-16 and PTOH-16 and defers the PSUs, the GE-4S and everything else to the OSA 5420/5421 System Description, which is not held. The IRIG-B card postdates the manual.
gaps.wanted: the OSA 5420/5421 System Description.

devices.description: 1RU 19-inch chassis for the DCP transponder and muxponder family. Two half-width traffic slots at the front; two hot-pluggable PSUs, a four-fan tray and the management board at the rear.

gaps.note: UM s3.1.5 says "The air inlets and outlets are positioned in the front and back", but fig 2-4 is an empty chassis shot into a dark cavity and resolves no vent pattern on the chassis front itself. The populated render (fig 1-1) does show honeycomb mesh, but that mesh is on the TRAFFIC UNITS' faceplates, not the chassis. So the front view draws no vent of its own and whether the chassis carries any is unresolved. RE-READ when the duplex adapters renamed their bores from tx and rx to fibre positions 1 and 2 (the adapter at v5, and the A22 that composes it, in the traffic slots at v2): the rename lives inside the slot occupants, not on the chassis front between them, so it neither closes this gap nor opens one - the gap stands.
gaps.wanted: a face-on photograph of a populated DCP-2, which would show the chassis front beside a unit faceplate and separate the two. Every front image in the corpus is either an empty chassis or a three-quarter render.

gaps.note: These four views carry the ENVELOPE ONLY - the 440 x 45 x 500 box from the manual's spec table, with the front faceplate shown edge-on as a dark band - and no observed surface detail: no lid screws, no side rails, no ventilation. That is the same treatment dcp-r-9d-cs gives its four, and it is honest rather than complete. The populated three-quarter render (fig 1-1) does show the lid and the left flank, but it is a lit marketing render on a black ground at an angle that measures nothing.
gaps.wanted: a square-on photograph of the lid and of one flank. Failing that, the 3/4 render would support screw positions on the lid if it were rectified, which is what was done for smartoptics/dcp-404@1's top face.

gaps.note: The management board is called "mgmt-board" in the DCP-2-FB/HW ordering description and "part of the DCP-2 chassis" in UM s2.6, and it has no orderable part number of its own. Its ports are placed directly on the rear view with the plate drawn as decor, rather than modelled as a bay.
gaps.wanted: a statement either way on whether the board is field-replaceable. If it is, this becomes a bay accepting a management-board component, and the seven ports move onto that part.

gaps.note: UM s3.2.8 puts the protective ground on the FRONT RACK BRACKET - "It is located on the right-side front rack mount(s)" - with an M5 nut and an unpainted pad around it. The stud is now modelled: the kit's front brackets and its mid-mount bracket each compose one (smartoptics/dcp-rack-kit@1), so it is where the bracket is and not on the chassis. What remains is that the generic ear a viewer draws for this chassis has no stud, so no face of the DCP-2 shows the terminal, and that the stud the brackets compose is the library's nominal one, which draws an M4 nut where the manual's is M5.
gaps.wanted: a generic ear that can show the stud a kit part carries, and an M5 nut-on-stud part in the library. Until then the terminal is in the kit's data and not in the drawing.

HOW FAR BEHIND THE FACEPLATE THE BRACKET'S FLANGE SITS in each of the three four-post positions. UM s3.2 names the positions (chassis flush, transponder flush, recessed) and prints no dimension for any of them, so no `at` is stated and the generic ear is drawn flush. A dimensioned drawing of the bracket on the chassis side, or a statement of the setbacks, settles it.

gaps.note: Both jacks of the ETH0/CONSOLE pair show small light features at their corners in fig 2-5. On ETH0 those read as link lamps; on an RS-232 console jack they are more likely shield retention tabs. CONSOLE is drawn as a bare std/rj45-ganged rather than the lamped common/rj45-ganged-eth used for the Ethernet ports.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph above about 5 px/mm, which would separate a lamp window from a retention tab. The best in the corpus is 2.7.

Every port lamp therefore keeps the component's off/on default rather than an invented vocabulary.

The library holds only the two-column ufispace/qsfpdd-led-strip-2x4@1 and this device may not add components, so both ends seat the wide part and its bezel overhangs the real metal by 2.8 mm outboard. datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9311-64D 400GE Data Center Switch Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9311-64D 400G data center spine switch - 2RU white box, 64x QSFP-DD 400G in four rows of sixteen (two 2-high stacked cage banks) plus 2x SFP+ 1/10G, an RJ45 out-of-band port, RJ45 and micro-USB consoles, USB 3.0 and a 1PPS/10MHz SMB timing pair, on Broadcom Tomahawk 4 at 25.6 Tbps; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 2400W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable in AC or DC and in front-to-back or back-to-front airflow

gaps.note: The HIG's section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the RJ45 management jack, and says nothing about the port lamps. Each QSFP-DD column carries a four-part cluster - a two-window light pipe at each end of the cage width with a round lamp inboard of each - and nothing states which half serves the upper port and which the lower, nor what the pipe's two windows mean against the round lamp. Every lamp keeps the component's off/on default; each cluster's `for` lists the two ports of the column it stands over, which is adjacency and not an asserted mapping. The SFP+ pair has no lamps drawn beside it at all.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The HIG Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 176.53 x 81.5 mm (W x D x H). HIG Figure 9's rear elevation, which passes the aspect gate at 0.45%, draws four identical faces abutting from x 17 to x 837 px with no chassis web between them, and four independent repeated features on that face - the airflow tag, the status lamp, the handle and the release tab - all sit on a 205.33 px pitch, which is 83.84 mm. The face is 83.7 x 80.0 and the table's number is 81 x 81.5. The likely resolution is the S9300-32D's: 81 measures the fan BODY behind the flange and the face is wider. That is an inference and not something either document says, so the manifest carries the measured face and this entry carries the disagreement.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-805616, or a caliper on the FRU

gaps.note: The ports ARE numbered 0-63 and 64-65 - HIG Figure 10 prints every numeral - but it prints them on the schematic module faces, where a seated module would cover them, so the figure does not say where the metal carries them. Nothing was found on the metal: the dark chassis web between the two cage bands profiles flat with no bright marks, and the 520 px front photograph is 1.19 px/mm, far too coarse for a 2 mm digit. No numerals are therefore drawn, rather than 66 of them being placed by guesswork.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on front photograph at 4 px/mm or better, or a vendor faceplate artwork sheet

gaps.note: Every small legend on the left-hand block is 4-6 px tall in the only orthographic front figure held, and does not resolve at 20x with autocontrast. Their positions and extents are measured; their WORDING is the HIG Figure 4 callout list and the Front Panel LED table's row names, which is a strong inference and still an inference. Four glyphs ARE legible and are drawn as seen: an up and a down triangle above the SFP+ block and another pair beside the RJ45 stack, plus the three-box network symbol to the right of the second pair. Three legends that certainly exist are NOT drawn, because nothing identifies them: a roughly 6 mm word between the USB symbol and the lower up-triangle at x 18.7-24.7 y 77-80, and two small marks flanking the SFP+ triangles at x 20.3-22.7 and x 32.9-35.4, y 12.7-15.3.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on front photograph at 4 px/mm or better

gaps.note: The HIG states the 110 V AC per-supply output twice and differently. Section 7 says that on a 110 V input each AC supply gives only 1000 W, too little for a supply to be swapped while the switch runs. Section 9's AC note says that on a 110 V source the S9311-64D still runs on both PSUs at 1200 W each, 2400 W in total. Same measure, same scope, two values. Neither is the number this manifest carries - power-output-w on the PSU contracts is the 2400 W nameplate from the datasheet's ordering lines, at the 200-240 V input the datasheet specifies - but a reader budgeting a 110 V feed needs to know the guide contradicts itself.
gaps.wanted: the PSU-242 supply datasheet, or a UfiSpace erratum for HIG R1.2

gaps.note: No held figure shows a DC build seated in the chassis. HIG Figure 9 and the datasheet rear render both show the AC unit with its C20 inlet, so the DC contract's fan frame, pull bar, latch and lamp positions are carried over from the AC unit rather than measured on a DC face. What is specific to the DC unit - a two-row input block, V+ over V-, with two lug/screw holes above it - comes from HIG Figure 6's CAD front view, whose own scale is only good to a couple of percent, so the block is drawn on the AC inlet's measured footprint instead of on that sheet's scale. The datasheet also names the connector for the INTAKE variant only ('CRPS TE 2204535-3 ELON Mini') and names none for the exhaust variant modelled here.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or elevation of a DC-configured S9311-64D, or the Delta drawing for PSU-242-DEERN at a stated scale

gaps.note: The HIG says 'The 400G QSFP-DD ports highlighted support both ZR+ transceivers up to 32 units' above Figure 12, and Figure 12 renders the lower band of 32 ports (32-63) pale against the upper band's normal dark. 32 is exactly one band, so the count and the shading agree - but the guide never says whether the pale band is the highlighted set or the excluded one, and the sentence's 'highlighted' is not defined anywhere in the document. No port is therefore given a per-port ZR attribute; the capability is recorded on the device as 'up to 32' without naming which 32.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace optics compatibility matrix, or a Figure 12 revision with a legend

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says 'there are two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed' and then shows one, on the rear panel's right-hand strip under the yellow label (Figures 22 and 23). The prose calls that location 'the side of the switch', which the strip arguably is, so it is not even certain the two sentences describe two different places. Only the located one is drawn; nothing is placed on a side face by inference.
gaps.wanted: a figure or photograph showing the second grounding location

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9311-64D, and the Available to Order block names only the four PSUs and two fans. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's -BN0B/-BR1B SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so orderable SKUs for the AC/DC and airflow builds almost certainly exist. The configurations therefore carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

gaps.note: The back-to-front supplies are not the exhaust units in blue. The datasheet gives the intake AC unit a different inlet ('PSU-242-AICB-NN ... CRPS-D-SUB/AC-inlet, blue latch') and the intake DC unit a different connector ('PSU-242-DIEB-NN ... CRPS TE 2204535-3 ELON Mini, blue latch'), and the HIG says only that their outlook differs. No held image shows either face, so ac-b2f and dc-b2f seat the exhaust contracts with a blue latch: right in colour, bay and airflow, wrong in inlet.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of a back-to-front S9311-64D, or face drawings of PSU-242-AICB-NN and PSU-242-DIEB-NN

gaps.note: spec/schemas/standards.yaml carries no `osfp` key, so std/osfp@1 - built for this device - declares `interface: osfp` instead of `conforms:`, and L9 therefore never checks its 23.10 x 13.50 mm aperture against anything. The number is measured off HIG Figure 8 and corroborated by the OSFP MSA module envelope (22.58 x 13.0 mm), which is not the same thing as the MSA's own faceplate-opening figure. The cage DEPTH, 47 mm, is a straight estimate: no held document dimensions an OSFP receptacle. The same absence shows up a second time in the tooling: lint's own PLUGGABLE_CAGES set lists eleven cage media and not osfp, so L40 skips the osfp-800g group and then reports `attrs.optics-osfp` as naming no group's media. THAT WARNING IS LEFT STANDING because it is true and it is this gap's own record - the optics list is correct and nothing in the toolchain can currently reach it through the media name.

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9500-22XST Disaggregated Cell Site Gateway Router Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9500-22XST disaggregated cell site gateway router - 1RU temperature-hardened white box, 4x 100M/1G RJ45 plus 8x SFP+ 10G, 8x SFP28 25G and 2x QSFP28 100G, a full timing block (GNSS, 1PPS and 10MHz on SMA, BITS on RJ48, ToD on RJ45) with a Stratum 3E OCXO and an internal GNSS receiver, Broadcom Qumran-AX at 300 Gbps; two front-service 1+1 PSUs and three rear 2+1 fans

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says 'there are two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed', and Figure 22 draws both on one unlabelled flank: Location-1 just behind the front face, drawn here as one M4 pair, and Location-2 about 194 and 209 mm behind it, which is not drawn yet. Which flank the figure shows is not stated; the right is taken from the Figure 5 inset.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the real unit flanks, or a figure captioned with the side

gaps.note: No held document dimensions the two grounding holes. The hardware installation guide names the screws (two M4) and the accessory lug (50 x 11.1 x 7.5 mm, #6 AWG) and draws the holes; the flank figure reads 15.6 to 15.9 apart, and the pair is drawn at the 5/8 in. (15.875) that reading and the two-hole lug both point at.
gaps.wanted: a drawing that dimensions the grounding holes, or the accessory lug's own datasheet

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the five system lamps (GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN, PWR), the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the management jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Figure 9 draws an up/down green pair in the web of every SFP+ and SFP28 column and two lamps in the QSFP28 web, so which port each lamp belongs to is clear from the arrows; what its colours and behaviours MEAN is not stated. Every port lamp therefore keeps common/led-dot's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. The same guide annotates nine rows of the system-lamp tables 'need NOS to activate this feature', so these may be NOS-defined rather than merely undocumented - which is a different fix, and the reason this is vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: HIG Figure 9 draws the ganged shells 25.5 mm tall, which cannot hold two 10.4 mm SFP openings on any manufacturable belly-to-belly pitch; the front photograph and std/sfp-ganged's own TE-measured 15.00 mm row pitch require 27.6 mm. The manifest carries 27.6 and the 15.0 mm pitch, and the whole port band therefore sits 1.05 mm higher at the top and 1.05 mm lower at the bottom than the guide figure draws it. The figure had already failed the aspect gate by 2.1 percent in the same direction, which is why the photograph was preferred rather than split the difference.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of the faceplate, or a caliper on the shell

gaps.note: Each fan carries a two-line legend on the chassis web beside it - the word FAN over an arrow and one digit - in the same position and the same form as the S9301-32D's rear. At the rear render's 1.168 px/mm the digit is not legible at any zoom, so the numbering is carried 0-based to match this device's own port table (0~3, 4~11, 12~19, 20~21) and the S9301-32D's rear rail, and NOT the sibling S9510-28DC, which prints FAN-1 to FAN-5 and is 1-based. Two house precedents disagree and no held image of this device settles it. The legend is also not DRAWN on the faceplate: it sits inside the module's own flange area and the chassis web between bays is 0.9 mm, so a chassis mark there would be painted over by the seated fan. The group numbering carries the fact; the drawing does not.
gaps.wanted: a legible photograph of the rear fan bays, or a rear elevation figure

gaps.note: Searched and absent, and this is the SAME silence the sibling S9510-28DC already records for the same fan rather than a second independent reading: the HIG dimensions and weighs the fan FRU (51.5 x 57.8 x 42.2 mm, 90 g) and tables its LED without ever stating a wattage, and this device's own datasheet names FAN-402825-HD only as an ordering line. The PSUs are sourced from their model numbers (PSU-201, 200 W); the fan has no equivalent, so L29 stands and the chassis module total is a floor.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name only S9500-22XST, and the Available to Order section names only PSU-201-DISB, PSU-201-AISB and FAN-402825-HD. Per the S9510-28DC precedent in this library, whose -BN0B and -BR1B SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no PDF, orderable SKUs for the AC and DC builds exist somewhere; the configurations therefore carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

gaps.note: The five system lamps measure 3.3 x 3.0 mm in Figure 9 and the library's nearest part, common/led-rect@1, is 4.6 x 2.6 - wider and shorter than the drawn lamp. It is used here because it is what the sibling S9510-28DC carries for the identical five-lamp row and because this device may not add components, but on the measured 6.85 mm pitch it closes the printed gap between neighbours from 3.5 mm to 2.25 mm.
gaps.wanted: a square ~3.2 mm indicator component, or a caliper on the lamp window

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9500-30XS 100G Disaggregated Cell Site Gateway Router Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9500-30XS disaggregated cell site gateway router - 1RU temperature-hardened white box for outside-plant cell-site backhaul, with 20x SFP+ 100M/1/10G, 8x SFP28 1/10/25G and 2x QSFP28 40/100G on a Broadcom Qumran-AX at 300 Gbps, a full timing block (GNSS, 1PPS and 10MHz on SMA, ToD on RJ45, BITS on RJ48, Stratum 3E OCXO, SyncE and 1588v2), front-serviced 1+1 400W supplies at the left of the faceplate and five 4+1 hot-swap fans at the rear

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the out-of-band jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The twenty-eight SFP arrows and the two QSFP28 lane strips therefore keep their components' off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Note that several rows elsewhere in those same tables are annotated as needing NOS integration to activate, so these may be NOS-defined rather than simply undocumented - which would be a different fix, and is why this is vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: THIS IS A DEFECT IN A SHARED COMPONENT, NOT IN THIS DEVICE, and it is recorded here because this device is where the evidence turned up - specifically in the matched- scale comparison of the rendered rear against the rear photograph, which is the only check that could have found it. ufispace/fan-402825@1 places its status lamp at [2.0, 1.6] - top left of the face - and its own provenance cites 'HIG Fig 8 drawing' for the geometry. This device's HIG Figure 8 (fig-0014) and this device's rear photograph both put the lamp at the BOTTOM of the fan's right-hand flange, below a knurled thumbscrew and a red 'E' airflow tag that the component does not draw at all; the component also draws a plain round rotor where both images show a hex grille, and a straight handle bar where both show a curved tube. The two guides' Figure 8 is byte-for-byte the same image, so the component contradicts the figure it names. It was reused unchanged rather than forked or edited, because it is shared with the S9510-28DC and a correction would change that device's rendering on this device's reading.
gaps.wanted: a decision on ufispace/fan-402825's element positions and face art, or a photograph of the FRU out of the chassis

gaps.note: The S9510-28DC - the same 440 x 302 x 43.5 chassis, the same five FAN-402825, the same rear artwork - places its first fan bay at x 8.0 with a 53.2 mm pitch. Measured here from that artwork and from this device's rear photograph independently, fan 0's face starts at 18.0 and 18.2 respectively, on a 52.6 mm pitch, and both images draw a plain chassis border across 2.2-17.6 where the sibling puts fan metal. The bank's total span agrees (265.5 against 266.0); only its origin does not. This manifest carries the measured 18.1, and the sibling's 8.0 is either a different anchor or an error that should be checked before either is trusted.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear drawing, or a tape on a real unit

gaps.note: The faceplate paints its first four SFP columns - ports 0 through 7 - in a blue band and the remaining six SFP+ columns in a plain dark one, while the datasheet lists all twenty as one thing, '20 x 100M/1/10G SFP+ ports'. Nothing in either document says what the blue marks. It could be a MACsec-capable subset, a 1G-capable subset, or housekeeping. The band is drawn because it is on the metal; no port carries an attribute derived from it.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace port-capability matrix, or a NOS port map for this platform

gaps.note: Neither held document states a maximum system power for this platform. The datasheet gives 'Typical power: 153.8 Watts (no transceiver)' and the input ratings, and the HIG's Connecting Power section gives provisioning instructions without a figure - unlike the same vendor's S9311-64D guide, which prints a maximum twice. power-max-w is therefore absent rather than estimated, and a reader budgeting a circuit has only the 400 W per-supply rating and the typical figure to work from.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace power calculator or a maximum-consumption line in a later guide revision

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9500-30XS, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and one fan. The datasheet does say the platform has 'a standard SKU and a premium SKU', differing in memory and storage, without naming either. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's -BN0B/-BR1B SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so orderable SKUs almost certainly exist. The configurations carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide, or the standard/premium SKU strings

gaps.note: The datasheet's port list says '8 x 100M/1G SFP ports' and the HIG's own Port Overview table says ports 4-11 are SFP at 100M/1G. The HIG's Figure 5 overview callout, pointing at the same eight cages, instead reads '8 x 2.5G SFP'. Same ports, same measure, different value. The manifest carries 1G because two independent statements - one in each document, one of them a table rather than a drawing callout - agree on it against a single callout label.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or NOS port-capability note for ports 4-11

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says the designated grounding location 'is located on the side of the router' and shows both locations in Figure 22, but never says which side, and the figure is an unlabelled flank elevation. They are drawn on the RIGHT flank because the front faceplate prints its earth symbol at the right-hand end, which is a reason and not a source. Their positions along the depth ARE measured (Figure 22, anchored on the 302 mm chassis bar).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the real unit's flanks, or a figure captioned with the side

gaps.note: No held document dimensions the grounding holes. The hardware installation guide names the screws (two M4 each) and the accessory lug (50 x 11.1 x 7.5 mm, #6 AWG) and draws the holes; Figure 22 reads them 15.8 and 15.7 apart, and each landing is drawn at the 5/8 in. (15.875) that reading and the two-hole lug both point at.
gaps.wanted: a drawing that dimensions the grounding holes, or the accessory lug's own datasheet

gaps.note: The rear face carries two plain plates either side of the fan modules, measured at x 18.1-69.6 and 229.3-280.0 and drawn at 18.6 and 229.3 after the matched-scale comparison. Each is 51.5 mm wide - one fan module - and each lands on the 52.3 mm fan pitch continued outwards, so the rear reads as five fan positions of which three are populated. The vendor says 3 fans and 2+1 redundancy and names no blanking part, so these are drawn as decor rather than as bays with fillers: a bay with no orderable occupant would be a promise the parts list does not make. If they are in fact fan-bay blanks this should become two more bays and a filler component.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear with a plate removed, or a UfiSpace accessory list naming a fan blank

gaps.note: 'FAN <0' / 'FAN <1' / 'FAN <2' appear at the top of each fan module's right-hand strip in the HIG rear elevation. If they are chassis printing they are hidden behind the modules; if module printing, the shared ufispace/fan-402825 component cannot carry a per-position digit. Neither is drawn. Recorded here for the same reason, and in the same words, as ufispace/s6301-56stp - a photograph of an empty fan bay would settle which metal carries the ink.
gaps.wanted: photograph of an empty S9501-18SMT fan bay

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the five system lamps (GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN, PWR), the PSU FRU lamp, the Fan FRU lamp and the management jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The eight corner dots on the RJ45 block and the fourteen up/down arrows in the SFP and SFP+ lands therefore keep their component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nine rows elsewhere in those same tables read 'need NOS to activate this feature', so these may be NOS-defined rather than simply undocumented; that is a different fix, and the reason this is filed as vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: A two-high ganged SFP block normally mirrors, so that both rows' bail latches stay reachable, and std/sfp-ganged draws an asymmetric aperture (module slot above, cage lip below) that shows the difference. The only elevation that resolves these cages is HIG Figure 9, and Figure 9 prints its large annotation numerals ON the cages, covering exactly the detail that would settle it. The rows are drawn belly-to-belly, the lower row rotate: 180, because that is the library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S3: upper rotate 0 over lower 180, both bails outward) and the port lamps between the rows point up over down - the rule and the lamps, not an observation of the metal.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on high-resolution front photograph, or a vendor 3D model

gaps.note: ufispace/fan-402825 states no draw and its own contract records the search across all 573 converted documents: eight UfiSpace datasheets name the part only as an ordering line, with no wattage anywhere near it. This HIG is the same - it weighs the fan FRU at 90 g and tables its lamp, and its only wattage figures are the system's 85 W maximum and the 200 W per-circuit reserve, neither of which is a fan's draw. L29's standing warning is the live count of how much of the chassis total is a floor.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet

gaps.note: only the DC build is drawn. The first pass modelled the two supplies as BAYS so a configuration could swap a DC connector for an AC one, and the matched-scale comparison against HIG Figure 5's AC elevation showed why that is wrong: the AC build does not just change the connector, it MOVES THE PRINTING. Its 'PSU n' legend sits at y 11.0 and its C14 window opens at y 11.9, against 17.1 and 18.1 on the DC build measured here - so the two are different front panels, not one panel with two occupants, and a bay would have made a false claim in both directions (that the supply pulls out, and that the panel is otherwise the same). ufispace/psu-120-ac is built and sourced and sits in the library ready for whoever draws that panel; this device places ufispace/psu-120-dc directly, as the fixed connector it is.

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives NO table for the port lamps. The sixty-four lane lamps drawn here therefore keep ufispace/lane-led-quad@1's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nothing states whether the four lamps above a cage are four lanes, or a link/activity pair per breakout, or something else; the component's own provenance reaches the same conclusion from a different platform's guide.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The four SFP28 ports have no lamp of their own. Eight lamp groups are drawn in each band and there are eight QSFP columns, so none is spare, and the guide never mentions an SFP28 indicator. What the faceplate does say is that the first QSFP column's two lamp rows are painted yellow and orange, continuous with the SFP28 legend band, where every other column's are green - and the guide says those four ports are the breakout of port 0. The natural reading is that port 0's four lane lamps are the four SFP28 ports' lamps in breakout mode. It is a reading and not a statement, so the lamps here are attached to port-0 and port-1 and the SFP28 group carries no indicator.
gaps.wanted: a NOS LED table naming the breakout lamps, or a photograph of a unit with the breakout enabled and one SFP28 port linked

Every internal consistency check that can be run does pass - sixteen badges per band, two bulges each, one column each, and a numbering that closes at 63 - which is why they are drawn rather than left off. gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU FRU lamp and the fan FRU lamp in full, and says nothing at all about the port lamps. The binding written here (upper row to the upper port) is the natural reading and is an inference. Every lamp keeps the component's off/on default rather than a vocabulary borrowed from a sibling guide.

gaps.note: THE 64 SFP28 LAMPS ARE THE TRIANGLES IN THE YELLOW BAND, and this gap used to say they did not exist. It said the hardware almost certainly had them, that HIG Figure 8's pale strip UNDER each module resolved to about two pixels at 9.585 px/mm, and that rather than invent 128 positions no reading supported, none were drawn. The search was in the wrong place: the lamps are above the modules, not below them, and the drawing already carried them - as 32 silkscreen marks reading `▲▼`, one per port pair, printed on the band. An up triangle for the top-row port and a down triangle for the bottom, which is the idiom the sibling S8901-54XC models correctly with common/led-arrow. Measured off the same figure, from the dark ink inside the yellow band rather than from a green cast beside it: each triangle is 2.35 x 1.47 mm, the two of a pair sit 2.79 mm apart, and the pairs repeat on a 14.37 mm pitch which is the port pitch. What remains unknown is only what they MEAN. HIG section 10 tables SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0 and PS1 in full and says nothing about any port lamp, so all 64 keep common/led-arrow-sm's own off/on default rather than a link/activity or speed vocabulary borrowed from a sibling guide.

The rotation used here - upper port unrotated, lower rotate 180, both cage lips into the strip and both bails outward - is the library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4), which the measured S9600-56DX and S9311-64D now both follow. It is the rule, not a reading of this device, and a photograph that shows otherwise overturns it.

The IDs 48-51 are certain, from the HIG's Port Overview table and Figure 8's callout, and are used for every id and rel-pos; what the metal prints beside these four cages is not established, so the arrows and lamps are drawn and the numerals are not. datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9611-36D 400G Open Core and Aggregation Router Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9611-36D 400G open core and aggregation router - 2RU white box, 36x QSFP-DD 40/100/200/400G in two rows of eighteen with OpenZR+/ZR on the top row, plus 2x SFP+ 1/10G, an RJ45 out-of-band port, RJ45 and micro-USB serial consoles, USB 3.0 and a 1PPS/10MHz SMB timing pair, on Broadcom Jericho2c+ BCM88850 with an OP2 BCM16K knowledge base at 14.4 Tbps and 16 GB of deep buffering; Stratum 3E OCXO, SyncE and 1588v2 Class C timing; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 3000 W supplies (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, exhaust airflow only

gaps.note: No figure of the seven UfiSpace guides that show the DC supply's terminal block names a conductor at either pole: the guides' connecting-power figure marks the two lugs' cables by colour only (red on the left pole, blue on the right) and the supply's own face prints no legend that a held figure shows. The two poles are stated `unstated`, and a feed is not called crossed on them.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph or drawing of the PSU-302-DESR's terminal block with the legend printed at its poles

gaps.note: Every held image of this faceplate letters it S9610-36D: the S9611-36D HIG's own port-overview figures 8 to 11, the S9611-36D datasheet's front and rear views, and all three vendor renders. The S9611-36D and S9610-36D are a near-twin pair and UfiSpace has illustrated the S9611-36D's documents with the sibling's artwork. The silkscreen here prints S9611-36D on the reasoning that a router does not letter itself as a different product, which is a judgement and not a reading. Nothing else on the face is affected - the dimensions, port table, LED table and callouts in the guide are all written for the S9611-36D.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a real S9611-36D front panel, or vendor faceplate artwork

gaps.note: The HIG's section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps, and stops. Nothing states what a port lamp means - link, activity, fault, or a lane aggregate - and no colour but the artwork's unlit green is shown. WHICH port each lamp belongs to is not in doubt (the printed triangle beside it points at its column), so every lamp carries a single `for:`; only the vocabulary is missing, and each lamp therefore keeps the component's plain off/on default. The two lamps above the SFP+ stack are the weaker case: they sit side by side above the upper cage rather than one per cage, and are assigned left-to-port-0 / right-to-port-1 from the '0 up-triangle / down-triangle 1' legend directly above them, which is a positional reading and not a stated mapping.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: Four features on the left-hand column are on the metal in every image and are named in no document. Two shallow round blind bosses, a small textured square window that reads like a mesh or a sensor, and a pair of short rounded slots under the beacon display. HIG Figure 4's callout list runs Reset, Beacon LED, 1PPS, 10MHz, USB, Micro USB, RJ45, System LED and 2 x SFP, and covers none of them. They are drawn as panel decor at their measured positions and given no part identity, because guessing one would put a name in the tree that no source supports.
gaps.wanted: a labelled front-panel figure, or a photograph of a real unit at close range

gaps.note: The HIG's Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 151.3 x 81.5 mm (W x D x H). The module seams in HIG Figure 4's rear elevation, which passes the aspect gate at 0.37%, sit on a 121.4 px pitch, i.e. 83.5 mm, and the vendor rear render puts the same seams on 291.3 px, i.e. 83.95 mm - so the drawn faces are about 2.7 mm further apart than the table's module is wide. The likely resolution is the S9321-64E's, where the same 808012 fan measures 81 in the table and 83.2 across the drawn flange: 81 is the body behind the flange and the face is wider. That is an inference and not something either document says, so the manifest seats the table's 81 mm module on the measured 83.7 mm pitch and draws the difference as chassis web, and this entry carries the disagreement.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-808012, or a caliper on the FRU

gaps.note: This HIG dimensions the fan 81 x 151.3 x 81.5; the S9321-64E HIG, from which ufispace/fan-808012@1 was built, dimensions the same 808012 series 81 x 154.8 x 81.5 and weighs it 741 g against this guide's 737 g. Face size and height agree exactly and only the depth and weight differ, which is what a suffix change (-HC here, -HCE there) usually is. The component is reused unchanged because nothing on the modelled face depends on the 3.5 mm, and the configuration overrides the model string to FAN-808012-HC, which is the part this datasheet actually orders.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace fan ordering guide covering both suffixes

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says the router 'can be grounded from the router's case and/or the power supply units (PSUs)', and both rear images show what that means: an earth symbol and a round stud on the lower left of each supply's own face, below its two status lamps. Neither ufispace/psu-302-dc@1 nor ufispace/psu-302-ac@1 contracts that stud - they were built from the S9321-64E, whose figures do not show it - and those components are shared with another platform, so it is recorded here rather than added to them from this device's evidence alone.

gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or elevation of an AC-configured S9611-36D

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9611-36D, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and the one fan. datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9620-32E 800G Open Aggregation Router Datasheet (2025-06-30)

devices.description: UfiSpace S9620-32E - 2RU 32-port 100/200/400/800G QSFP-DD open aggregation router with 4x 1/10/25G SFP28 ports and 2x 10G SFP+ management uplinks; Broadcom Qumran3D BCM88870 at 25.6 Tbps with a 32 GB deep buffer, Intel Ice Lake-D 8-core with an AST2620 BMC, 1+1 hot-swap 3200W AC or DC PSUs, 3+1 hot-swap fans, front-to-back airflow

gaps.note: UfiSpace has published a hardware installation guide for every other UfiSpace platform modelled in this library and none for the S9620 family. That single absence is behind most of the other entries here: no Component Physical Information table to check the FRU faces against, no front-panel or FRU LED tables, no Port Overview table stating the ID ranges, no space-clearance or grounding section, no rail or pin counts, and no orthographic top, side or bottom elevations. The whole model rests on one datasheet and its two embedded renders.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-32E hardware installation guide, or any UfiSpace mechanical drawing of this chassis.

gaps.note: the six system lamps sit beside a printed white legend box whose six words are unreadable at every resolution held - 11-px-tall smears at 9.17 px/mm on the only image of them. The names carried on the placements (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID) are the S9321-64E HIG's names for the same six-lamp column on the same vendor's 2RU faceplate, in the order that lamp column runs, and the glyph outlines here are consistent with them. THEY ARE A DIFFERENT PRODUCT'S DOCUMENT, and the reason is filed as sources-disagree rather than needs-photo because the disagreement is between what this device's artwork says (nothing legible) and what a sibling's table says, which is not the same thing as nobody having looked.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the left end of the front panel, or the S9620-32E hardware installation guide's front-panel LED table.

gaps.note: not one lamp on this device has a documented meaning. The datasheet tables no LED behaviour at all, and the HIG that would carry the front-panel, PSU FRU and fan FRU LED tables does not exist for this family. So the six system lamps, the 32 per-port lamps, the six SFP-cage lamps and the supply's own lamp all carry positions and no states. Every other UfiSpace device in this library transcribes those tables in full; copying one across from a different SKU would assert this platform's behaviour from another platform's document, and the lamp names above are already one borrowing more than is comfortable.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-32E hardware installation guide, or a NOS LED table.

gaps.note: three unlabelled round openings about 6 mm across - one at (6.89, 48.80) on the front left, two at (430.66, 21.89) and (430.65, 71.54) on the front right - and a 2.0 x 30.9 dark slot at x 431.98-433.94. No legend, no callout, and nothing in the datasheet names them. The S9321-64E carries the identical arrangement and its provenance leaves them unidentified too, so two models have now failed to name the same UfiSpace family feature. They are drawn as dark decor and named here so the marks are recorded unknowns rather than unexplained ink.
gaps.wanted: a hardware installation guide front-panel figure with callouts, or a photograph of the bezel from an angle.

gaps.note: the datasheet orders PSU-322-DEJR-NN (3200W DC, exhaust) beside the AC unit, and both embedded renders show the AC build with C20 inlets. Nothing held shows the DC face. ufispace/psu-322-ac is measured; no psu-322-dc component is built, because every number on it would have been guessed from the AC sibling's outline. The bays accept and default to the AC unit only, so the dc configuration seats it under the DC model name - wrong at the inlet, which this gap and lint L120 keep in view. The build is declared anyway because its feed is a field tools filter on.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing of the PSU-322-DEJR-NN face.

gaps.note: the datasheet's FAN Types line orders FAN-805616-HCD; ufispace/fan-805616, built for the S9311-64D from that device's HIG, is drawn as FAN-805616-HCE. gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FRU datasheet or ordering guide covering the 805616 fan family.

gaps.note: ufispace/fan-805616 states no draw; its own contract records the search that established the vendor does not publish one for the 805616 family. This datasheet adds nothing - its only watt figures are the 696 W system typical and the two 3200 W supply nameplates. L29's standing warning is the live record that the chassis module total is a floor rather than a total.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's rating label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet.

gaps.note: the datasheet gives 'Typical power: 696 Watts (no transceiver)' and no maximum. On every other UfiSpace platform here the maximum comes from the HIG's Connecting Power section with its test conditions printed beside it (40 C ambient, optics populated, 100% load); with no HIG there is no such figure and none is derived. Two 3200 W supplies bound what the chassis can draw and say nothing about what it does draw.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-32E hardware installation guide's Connecting Power section.

gaps.note: six stiffening grooves are countable on the isometric render of the cover and their direction is legible; their pitch, length and the cover screw positions are laid out evenly over the stated 580 mm depth and are estimated. The count is the vendor's, the spacing is mine.

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9620-54DC 400G Open Aggregation Router Datasheet (rev 20260811V01)

devices.description: UfiSpace S9620-54DC 400G open aggregation router - a 1RU 440 x 480 mm white box on Broadcom Qumran3u BCM88400 at 1.2 Tbps with 4 GB of deep buffer, carrying 54 ports on one face: forty 1/10/25G SFP28 and eight 1/10/25/50G SFP56 in twenty-four belly-to-belly ganged columns, then four 100G and two 400G QSFP-DD in three more. A timing block down the left edge takes a GNSS SMA, 1PPS and 10MHz SMB and a ToD RJ45 against a Stratum 3E OCXO with SyncE, 1588v2 and an internal GNSS receiver; the management RJ45, serial console and USB 3.0 the datasheet lists appear nowhere on this face. Five hot-swap fans (4+1) and dual 750 W supplies (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, front-to-back

gaps.note: UfiSpace has published no hardware installation guide for the S9620 family - the intake's own coverage sheet records the miss for all three S9620 models - so this device is modelled from a datasheet and two product renders and nothing else. Everything a guide normally supplies is therefore absent here: no faceplate figure with numbered callouts, so no callout audit was possible and any feature the render does not show is not merely unmodelled but unknown; no front-panel or FRU LED table, so no lamp on this device carries a state vocabulary; no component dimension table, so the fan and PSU faces are the library's from a sibling platform; no rear elevation; no rail or grounding section. This is the single largest limitation on the model and every other gap here descends from it.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC Hardware Installation Guide, when UfiSpace publishes it

gaps.note: The largest front image UfiSpace serves is 520 x 150 px, which is 1.125 px/mm and 0.89 mm per pixel. Every size token on the product page was probed (/image/5e/, /image/5g/ and eighteen others) and nothing larger exists; the datasheet's own copy of the same picture is 158 px native. The render passes Gate 1 on aspect (9.900 against 10.000) so its PROPORTIONS are trustworthy and the standard pitches confirm them across 24 columns to 0.3 mm - but no printed legend on this faceplate is legible, no connector keyway is readable, and every coordinate quoted here to a tenth is really good to about half a millimetre.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of a real S9620-54DC faceplate at 2000 px or better

gaps.note: The datasheet lists a 100/1000M RJ-45 management port, an RJ45 serial console port and a USB 3.0 Type-A port. NONE OF THE THREE IS ON THE FRONT FACE - the front render shows exactly one RJ45, inside the timing block, and no USB opening anywhere, and the whole left block is only 24 mm wide. They are therefore on the rear, which UfiSpace publishes no image of. So three documented ports exist on this device and are modelled nowhere, and the mgmt group is not declared at all rather than being declared empty.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or the hardware installation guide

gaps.note: No rear image of this model exists - the vendor publishes a front and a 45-degree front angle and nothing else, and there is no installation guide. The inventory is sourced (five hot-swap fans in a 4+1 set, two hot-swap 750 W supplies in a 1+1 set, all exhaust, front-to-back) but EVERY REAR COORDINATE IN THIS FILE IS INVENTED: the 52.0 mm fan pitch, the x 12.0 start, the supplies at the right, the vertical centring. They are laid out the way the library's other UfiSpace 1RU boxes are laid out, which is a plausible arrangement and not this chassis's. Nothing else is drawn on that face for the same reason.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of an S9620-54DC, or the hardware installation guide

gaps.note: The tile at x 78.2-105.5 carries six lamps - four green across the top, one green and one blue below - and a printed legend beside each. At 1.125 px/mm those legends are two pixels tall and cannot be read, so NO legend is printed in this drawing and the lamps carry positional ids. The arrangement is the S7801-54XS's exactly (four lamps with a blue ID lamp beneath the fourth), whose HIG names them SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and ID, and the extra green lamp under the first is where a timing platform's SYNC lamp sits on the S9610-36D. That reading is recorded here so the next reader has it; it is not written into the artwork, and no lamp carries a state vocabulary because no LED table exists for this platform.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC HIG's front-panel LED table, or a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: The faceplate prints port numerals on the yellow, teal and blue bands - two glyph clusters per column are visible - and this render cannot resolve a single digit. The numerals drawn are reconstructed as 0-53 left to right, even on the top row and odd on the bottom, which is what every UfiSpace box in this library does and what the per-column up/down lamp pair implies. Two things are genuinely open: whether UfiSpace numbers the 400G pair first on this SKU rather than last, and whether the run starts at 0 or 1. The olive band under the four 100G ports carries no printing at all, so those four are drawn unlabelled.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph, or the HIG's port map

gaps.note: PORTS 48-51 ARE DRAWN WITHOUT NUMERALS ON PURPOSE, AND THEY ARE THE ONLY FOUR OF FIFTY-FOUR THAT ARE. The olive band under the two 100G QSFP-DD columns carries no printing: crop the three bands side by side at 26x and the teal band to its left is packed with dark glyph clusters, two per column, while the olive band holds a white up-triangle at each end, a white down-triangle at each end, eight round lamps along its lower edge and nothing else, and the steel-blue band to its right carries light glyphs at both ends. The blue band is the control that makes this a reading rather than a resolution artefact: it is the same darkness as the olive one and its printing survives, so a legend on the olive band would have survived too. Numerically the olive band's upper half (rows y 91-93 px) is uniform where the teal and blue bands vary. The vent strip above the shell was checked as well and carries only the lamp row and its two triangles. So this faceplate appears to identify its 100G pair by band colour and row triangle rather than by number. Printing 48-51 would put ink on the drawing that is not on the metal, which is the one thing silkscreen must never do - so they are left off, and this entry exists so that a reader comparing the render against the photograph can tell a deliberate absence from an unfinished model. If a legible photograph ever shows numerals there, they belong on the band in the light fill the blue band uses, which is what is legible on an olive ground.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph, or the HIG's port map

gaps.note: The silver strip between the upper and lower cage rows on all three QSFP-DD shells is FINELY MARKED, not blank, and this render cannot separate the marks. Rows y 73-78 px read 190 / 84 / 152 / 130 / 96 / 186, so there are two darker rows at 21.1 and 23.8 mm inside a lighter band - that much is solid, and it is what the drawing reproduces, as decor. What it will not do is name a count. A local-minimum scan finds a 4.44 mm rhythm, but the two 100G columns - which are identical hardware - put that rhythm at offsets 1.7/6.2/10.6/15.1 mm in one column and 4.1/8.5/13.0/17.4 in the next, asymmetric in opposite directions and disagreeing by 2.4 mm. Two identical columns cannot really differ; that is the signature of sampling a pattern finer than the pixel grid, and the residual darkness between the minima says the true pitch is about half, near 2.2 mm, which 0.89 mm per pixel cannot resolve. So it is not decided whether these are indicators or the ganged cage's gasket comb. Against them being lamps: each 100G port already carries four round lamps that DO resolve, four above the shell and four on the olive band below it, so strip lamps would give one port twelve indicators; and the pattern continues across the 400G column, which has no lamp row above it at all. Nothing is drawn as an LED here on that reasoning, and no lane count is asserted in either direction.
gaps.wanted: a faceplate photograph at 2000 px or better, or the HIG's port-LED figure

gaps.note: Two identical 8.0 mm SMB jacks sit at (29.3, 5.3) and (44.4, 5.3) with a printed legend beside each that this render cannot read. They are assigned 10MHz and 1PPS in the order the datasheet's Timing Interfaces row lists them, which is a convention, not a reading - and the S9610-36D prints its pair the other way up in a vertical stack, so there is no house order to fall back on either. The GNSS SMA is identified independently, by being the larger connector and the only SMA the datasheet lists.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: The ToD RJ45's latch direction cannot be determined: the opening is eleven pixels across and the notch that would settle it is one. The jack is drawn in std/rj45-ganged's own orientation. On a single jack this is cosmetic; it is recorded because the library has been caught by mirrored stacked pairs before and the check was genuinely run here rather than skipped.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: Each of the twenty-four SFP columns carries two small dark 1.8 mm squares on the silver inter-row strip, at 2.7 and 12.0 mm from the column edge, flanking the up/down lamp pair - 48 of them, counted. They are drawn as decor because nothing identifies them: they could be a second lamp per port drawn unlit, a shell fastener or a gasket feature, and with no LED table and no faceplate figure there is no way to choose. Drawing them as lamps would assert a per-port indicator this device may not have.
gaps.wanted: the HIG's front-panel figure, or a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: No document held states what any port lamp means. The geometry is read: one up-triangle and one down-triangle per SFP column, four round lamps above and four below each 100G QSFP-DD column, and two lamps below the 400G column with none above it. The last of those is measured rather than assumed - the vent perforation runs unbroken above the 400G shell where it is visibly interrupted above the 100G shell - but whether the 400G pair really has one lamp each, or a lane row this render cannot separate, is open. Every lamp keeps its component's plain off/on default. The strip between the two QSFP-DD rows is finely marked rather than blank and is drawn as a banded decor field of the measured tone; its marks could not be separated and are deliberately not modelled as lamps. See the qsfp-inter-row-marks gap, which carries the measurement that decides it.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC HIG's LED tables, or a NOS LED reference

gaps.note: This datasheet's Fan Types line reads 'FAN-405636-HD, exhaust air flow'. The library has ufispace/fan-405637, built from the S9110-32X's guide, at 50.7 x 40.0 mm. One digit apart in a number that encodes the rotor, so the two are probably one family and possibly not one face. There is no S9620-54DC guide to measure the real module against and no image of it, so the component is reused with its model attribute overridden to FAN-405636-HD and the substitution recorded here rather than hidden. If the faces differ, five bays on the rear are the wrong width.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace fan ordering guide, or the S9620-54DC HIG's component table

gaps.note: No wattage for the fan module appears anywhere. The datasheet's Fan Types line reads 'FAN-405636-HD, exhaust air flow' with no figure beside it, and there is no installation guide to carry a component table. Both datasheet pages were searched at 200 dpi for every occurrence of 'W', 'Watt' and 'power': the only hits are the two PSU ordering lines (750W), the AC/DC input ratings and the single system figure (125 W typical, no transceiver). The L29 warning this device carries is therefore left standing, and the modelled module total is a floor rather than a total.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FAN-405636 specification, or a measured figure from a live unit

gaps.note: This datasheet orders PSU-751-AESR-1C and PSU-751-DESR-1C; the library's psu-751 components were drawn for the S9110-32X, which orders PSU-751-AESR and -DESR at the same 750 W and the same input ranges. The '-1C' suffix is undocumented in any held file. The faces are assumed identical and the model attribute is overridden per configuration.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace power-supply ordering guide

gaps.note: Both supplies are orderable and no held image shows either one seated, because there is no rear image. The base configuration seats the DC unit, which is an arbitrary choice recorded as arbitrary - on the S9610-36D the same choice was settled by reading a terminal block out of the rear elevation, and here there is nothing to read.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of a shipped unit

gaps.note: The angle render shows the left side face carrying a column of countersunk ear-mount holes near the front and a run of rail features along its length, and the lid carrying three long transverse stiffening ribs and a scatter of fastener dimples. The counts are read off that render at 45 degrees; NOT ONE POSITION IS DIMENSIONED ANYWHERE, so every coordinate on the four non-port faces is estimated and evenly spread. The bottom face is not shown in any image at all and carries only a compliance sticker at an estimated position.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing, or straight-on side and underside photographs

gaps.note: Three features on the left block are drawn because two independent images put them there and are not named, because with no guide there is no callout list to name them with: a 4.4 mm round icon at (72.4, 5.7) carrying a diamond-shaped glyph, between the model legend and the lamp tile, and two 2.7 mm dark circles at (6.2, 37.4) and (16.9, 37.4) under the ToD jack. A third, the 2.7 mm circle at (6.2, 14.5), is placed as common/reset-button on the reading that a recessed pinhole above a management jack is a reset - which every other UfiSpace box in this library has - and that reading is a guess too.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC HIG's front-panel callout list

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number; the datasheet's Available to Order block covers only the two supplies and the one fan. The configurations therefore carry no part numbers rather than invented ones, as on the S9610-36D.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs
